stories.title: BSP’s lone UP MLA Umashankar Singh dies at 55:Mayawati's rakhi brother and three-time Rasra legislator passes away after battling stage-four brain cancer
stories.summary: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) MLA Umashankar Singh, the party’s only legislator in Uttar Pradesh, died at a hospital in Delhi on Wednesday evening. He was 55. Singh had been battling cancer for a long time and had also undergone treatment in the US. His condition had deteriorated after the disease reached stage four. Singh represented the Rasra Assembly constituency in Ballia district for three consecutive terms. BSP chief Mayawati considered him her brother and had tied a rakhi on him during a visit to his Lucknow residence last Raksha Bandhan when he was unwell. He is survived by his wife, Pushpa Singh, daughter Yamini Singh and son Prince Yukesh Singh. Yamini married in 2019, while Yukesh married in 2024. Yukesh is also the CEO of his father's company, C.S. Infraconstruction Ltd. Joined BSP in 2011, won Rasra seat three times Singh began his political career in student politics. In 1990, he was elected general secretary of the students' union at AAC College in Ballia. He later became Ballia district panchayat chairman in 2000, establishing a strong presence in local politics. Singh joined the BSP in 2011 and was elected MLA from Rasra for the first time in 2012. Despite the BSP's tally falling from 206 to 80 seats in the state, he secured more than 84,000 votes and defeated his Samajwadi Party rival Sanatan Pandey by around 52,000 votes. He retained the seat in 2017 and won it for a third consecutive time in 2022. His victory in 2022 gave the BSP its only seat in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly. Known as ‘Robin Hood of Rasra’ Singh was popularly known as the ‘Robin Hood of Rasra’ because of his reputation for helping people in his constituency. A contractor by profession, he was credited by supporters with getting development work done in the area even when the BSP was not in power in the state. In 2012, Singh organised the mass marriage of 251 girls. Four years later, he organised another mass wedding involving 351 Hindu and Muslim couples. In November 2025, Mayawati appointed him leader of the BSP legislature party in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly. Faced disqualification over government contracts Singh had also faced controversy during his political career. He was accused of taking a road construction contract in his own name while serving as an MLA. Then Uttar Pradesh Governor Ram Naik found him guilty in the case. Singh challenged the decision in the Supreme Court, which later ruled in his favour. On January 14, 2017, Naik had disqualified Singh over an alleged violation of the Representation of the People Act related to government contracts. A Lokayukta investigation had found the allegations to be valid. His Assembly membership was subsequently cancelled following the Election Commission's recommendation and directions from the High Court. It was reportedly the first case in Uttar Pradesh in which an MLA's membership was retrospectively terminated.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi's student event faces venue setback:Trust cancels booking, cites academic disruption and damage from ongoing rains
stories.summary: The booking of KP Ground in Prayagraj, where Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition (LoP) and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi is scheduled to hold a student interaction programme on August 8, has been cancelled by the Kayastha Pathshala (KP) Trust. The trust's acting president, Chaudhary Jitendra Nath Singh, informed the city Congress committee about the decision in a letter issued on Wednesday. He cited possible disruption to students' studies and the risk of damage to the ground because of continued rain. Preparations for the event were already in the final stages, with work on the pandal under way. The sudden cancellation has triggered uncertainty among Congress leaders. Trust suggests postponing event until after rains The trust said the proposed programme could affect students from two schools operating near the ground. It also said the ground is meant for outdoor sports and could be damaged because of the ongoing rain. According to Singh, the college principal had informed him that a High Court order requires students' studies and academic activities to remain unaffected. The trust has suggested holding the event during the holidays after the monsoon. It has cancelled the earlier permission and asked Congress to collect the money deposited for the booking. Copies of the letter have been sent to the district magistrate, officials of Kayastha Pathshala, Chaudhary Naunihal Singh Academy and the trust's accountant. The accountant has been asked to return the deposited amount by cheque after completing the necessary formalities. Congress legal team seeks solution Congress leaders said their legal team is in Prayagraj and is holding discussions with trust officials and the administration. City Congress president Fuzail Hashmi said the party had received the trust's letter and that the legal team would try to find a solution. He said 1.74 lakh students had registered for the programme so far and indicated that the matter could reach the High Court. Congress spokesperson Haseeb Ahmed said the student interaction would be held in Prayagraj on August 8 as scheduled, starting at 5pm. Rahul Gandhi expected to interact with students Rahul Gandhi is expected to interact directly with around 300,000 students during the programme. The Leader of the Opposition has already held two such student interaction programmes. The first took place in Kota, Rajasthan, on June 17, followed by an event in Dehradun, Uttarakhand, on July 17. The nationwide campaign focuses on issues including paper leaks, expensive education, irregularities in recruitment and unemployment. ₹2 crore Pandal being prepared Preparations for the Prayagraj event had been progressing at KP Ground, with a pandal reportedly being built at a cost of around ₹2 crore. Organisers had also planned fireworks worth around ₹10 lakh for Rahul Gandhi's arrival. A Delhi-based company has reportedly been given responsibility for catering, while a corridor is being constructed inside the pandal for the interaction between Rahul Gandhi and students.

stories.title: UP man marries wife to younger lover:Blesses newlywed couple after 21 years of love marriage
stories.summary: In a bizarre yet extraordinary case of understanding, a husband in Uttar Pradesh’s Sant Kabir Nagar arranged his wife’s marriage to her lover 21 years after their own wedding. The couple has five children. The husband, Buddhiram Nishad, reportedly arranged the marriage of his 37-year-old wife, Phoolmati, to her lover, who is 13 years younger than her, Awadhesh, at a temple on Tuesday. He stood by as Awadhesh applied Sindoor and exchanged garlands with Phoolmati, before blessing the newly married couple. The incident took place in the Dhanghata police station area, with videos of the wedding emerging on Wednesday. Couple has five children Buddhiram, a daily-wage worker from Devri village, had married Phoolmati from neighbouring Hakimpur village 21 years ago. The couple has four sons and a daughter. Their eldest son is 17, while their youngest is two-and-a-half years old. According to the family, Phoolmati had allegedly been in a relationship with Awadhesh for around five years. First, see 2 pictures of the wedding Wife had left home with lover Phoolmati had allegedly left her husband and five children around two months ago and gone to Punjab with Awadhesh. She later returned after repeated efforts by her family and villagers. However, her return led to frequent arguments between her and Buddhram over the relationship. Buddhiram said he had caught his wife speaking to Awadhesh on the phone several times and objected to their relationship. Husband says he did not want to risk his life Buddhiram said he was away for work when Phoolmati left home. When he returned, he found that she and the children were not at home. Villagers later told him that they had seen Phoolmati leaving with Awadhesh. He then informed the police. According to Buddhram, Phoolmati was unwilling to end the relationship and both she and Awadhesh wanted to live together. He said he did not want to risk his life over their relationship and decided to let them stay together with mutual consent. Husband performs wedding at temple At around 6 pm on Tuesday, Buddhram arranged the couple's wedding at a Shiva temple in Ashrafpur in the presence of relatives and villagers. He reportedly stood by as Awadhesh applied sindoor to Phoolmati's forehead and exchanged garlands with her. He then blessed the couple. The children were also present during the ceremony. Phoolmati took her two-and-a-half-year-old son with her after the wedding. Phoolmati and Awadhesh subsequently left for Lucknow.

stories.title: Merchant navy officer’s brother drapes tricolour over body:Says ‘government denied honour’; mother and wife cry holding coffin
stories.summary: The mortal remains of merchant navy officer Sagar Gupta, who lost his life in a Ukrainian drone attack, were brought to Kanpur on Wednesday evening at around 4 pm, 18 days after his death. As soon as the family saw the body, his wife Shalu and mother Ramadevi broke down and became inconsolable while hugging the coffin. The house was filled with cries of grief. His niece Lakshmi, sister-in-law Jyoti and elder sister Pooja also broke down in tears. Sagar’s elder brother called him a martyr. With tears in his eyes, he said, “We had asked the government for a tricolour for our brother. We did not get it. So I bought one from the market.” He then draped the national flag over Sagar’s body. A crowd of relatives and neighbours gathered outside the house for Sagar’s last glimpse. Officials from the district administration also reached the spot after receiving information. In front of them, the family demanded martyr status for Sagar, a government job for his wife Shalu and a compensation of ₹2 crore. The officials have not given any concrete assurance yet. The family said the last rites will not be performed until their demands are fulfilled. The body has been kept in a deep freezer. See 4 pictures Family said - saved 8 in one attack, martyred in another attack Sagar Gupta was a resident of Shastri Nagar in Kanpur. In 2018, he joined Avon Navigators Marines Private Limited, a company based in Thane, Navi Mumbai, through the Directorate General of Shipping. He was currently working as a chief officer in the merchant navy. According to his family, Sagar left home on June 13 and travelled to Russia via Turkey. On July 18, the ship on which Sagar was deployed was attacked twice by Ukrainian drones in the Black Sea. After the first attack, Sagar moved eight crew members on the ship to a safe location. He was trying to take the ship to a safer area when the second attack took place, in which he lost his life. The family was informed about the incident on July 21 through a phone call from one of Sagar’s friends. Since then, they had been waiting for his mortal remains to return to India. On Wednesday morning, Sagar’s body reached New Delhi from Moscow, Russia, in an air ambulance. Later, his elder brother Manish Gupta and brother-in-law Shobhit brought the body home in an ambulance on Wednesday evening.

stories.title: BCA student found with throat slit in Lucknow:Classmate found critically injured beside body; she was alone at home
stories.summary: A murder incident of a BCA student has come to light in Lucknow. Her body was found on the first floor of her own house on Wednesday evening. There were deep cut marks on her throat. Her classmate was also found injured in serious condition near the student's body. Police investigation has revealed that the classmate himself murdered the student by slitting her throat with a sharp weapon. The incident took place in Narpatkheda, Para area. The body of the deceased Smriti Pandey (17) has been sent for post-mortem. Devansh Pathak (18), a resident of Alamnagar, has been admitted to the hospital for treatment. See 2 pictures- Student was alone at home Smriti Pandey (17) was a first-year BCA student at TS Mishra College. According to the family, Smriti's younger sister Jagriti had gone to college at the time of the incident. Father Shailendra Pandey is retired from the Indian Army as a Naib Subedar. He is currently working as an NCC instructor in Kanpur. Mother Kiran Pandey is a homemaker, while brother Sachindra Pandey is preparing for the SSC exam in Prayagraj. On Monday, family members had gone to their native district Amethi. Smriti and her younger sister were at home. When the younger sister returned home on Wednesday evening, she saw Smriti's blood-soaked body lying near the bed. Devansh Pathak, also covered in blood, was lying nearby. After which she raised an alarm and the police were informed. DCP Kamlesh Dixit said that today, information was received about the murder of a girl in Narpatkheda, under the Para police station area. Upon receiving the information, the police reached the spot. A 17-year-old girl was found dead. There were injury marks on her neck. A student from her class was found lying nearby in an injured state.

stories.summary: Police in Gorakhpur's Gulriha arrested a 22-year-old man on Wednesday for allegedly raping a 17-year-old girl after luring her with a false promise of marriage. The accused, identified as Vinay Nishad, a resident of Jungle Ekla No. 2, Tola Hatwa, was produced before a court and sent to jail at around 5 pm. The victim had lodged an FIR at Gulriha police station on August 1. Now read the complete case Victim says accused disappeared after pregnancy According to police, the 17-year-old girl alleged that Vinay trapped her in a relationship by assuring her that he would marry her. She claimed he repeatedly had sexual relations with her on the false promise of marriage, following which she became pregnant. The victim alleged that after learning about the pregnancy, the accused switched off his mobile phone and cut all contact with her. She later informed her mother about the incident. On Saturday, the two approached Gulriha police station and filed a named complaint against the accused. They first connected on Instagram Police said the girl had been in contact with the accused for nearly two years and they regularly spoke over the phone. Family members had reportedly warned her several times, but she continued meeting him after believing his assurances. The two had first come into contact through Instagram. Gorakhnath Circle Officer Ravi Singh said an FIR was registered against the accused under the relevant sections of the law and the POCSO Act based on the complaint. He was arrested and sent to jail after questioning.

stories.title: Varanasi civic body steps up cleanliness drive:4 lakh dustbins to be distributed to 2 lakh households, campaign begins on PM Modi’s birthday
stories.summary: The Varanasi Municipal Corporation has intensified efforts to improve its ranking in Swachh Survekshan 2025 after finishing 17th. Having lost crucial marks last time due to poor waste segregation, the civic body will distribute 4 lakh dustbins to residents to encourage source-level segregation of waste. The mega cleanliness drive will begin in Varanasi on September 17, Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday. Around 2 lakh households across the municipal area will receive 4 lakh dustbins free of cost. Under the initiative, every household will be given two dustbins—one green and one blue—so that wet and dry waste can be collected separately from every home. The initiative is expected to make waste segregation and disposal more efficient. The green dustbin will be used for wet waste such as fruits, vegetables, leaves, peels and leftover food. The blue dustbin will be meant for dry waste, including plastic bottles, chips packets, slippers, paper and glass. Prime Minister Modi inspired the entire country towards cleanliness from Kashi. On his birthday, we are promoting cleanliness by distributing four lakh dustbins across the city. — Ashok Tiwari, Mayor The event will begin on the Prime Minister's birthday Mayor Ashok Tiwari said the Municipal Corporation is working towards securing a top position in the Swachh Survekshan rankings, with efforts underway in every sector. As part of the initiative, around 4 lakh dustbins will be distributed free of cost to households so that waste can be collected separately from every home. Residents will segregate their waste before handing it over to municipal sanitation workers during door-to-door collection. The campaign will begin on September 17 and cover 2 lakh households across all 100 municipal wards. The Mayor said that while Kashi inspired the country’s cleanliness movement under the Prime Minister’s leadership, the city is now not only distributing 4 lakh dustbins but is also expanding its quick-response grievance redressal system to 50 wards. The goal is to ensure that civic complaints are resolved within four hours. Prime Minister Modi inspired the entire country towards cleanliness from Kashi. On his birthday, we are not only distributing four lakh dustbins across the city to promote cleanliness, but also expanding the quick-response system to 50 wards. Our goal is to ensure that citizens’ grievances are resolved within four hours. — Ashok Tiwari, Mayor 25 new wards to be connected with Quick Solution Project Mayor Ashok Tiwari said that along with the cleanliness campaign, the Municipal Corporation is also accelerating work on faster resolution of civic issues. The ‘Quick Response Smart Pilot Project’, launched on July 21 in 25 wards along the Ganga riverfront, will now enter its second phase. From September 17, another 25 wards will be added, taking the total coverage to 50 wards. Under the expanded system, 14 major civic issues related to six departments will be resolved within a maximum of four hours. To make the process transparent and technology-driven, the Municipal Corporation has introduced a WhatsApp chatbot system. Lodge complaints directly on WhatsApp number Residents can lodge complaints directly through WhatsApp on 8601872601. Once a complaint is submitted, the system automatically matches it with the master database and forwards it to the concerned official through a mobile application, along with a live photograph and GPS location. After the complaint is registered, the citizen receives a ticket ID. The assigned official then visits the site, resolves the issue and uploads a photograph of the completed work through the departmental app. The application automatically locks the photograph with the current GPS coordinates and timestamp. Once the backend system verifies the work, the complaint status changes from 'Pending' to 'Closed', and the citizen is immediately notified.

stories.title: Lucknow Primary Teachers' Association state executive meet:Action sought on teachers' issues, from old pension to TET
stories.summary: The state-level joint executive committee meeting of the Uttar Pradesh Primary Teachers’ Association was held on Wednesday at the Diploma Engineers’ Building in Raj Bhavan, Lucknow. District presidents, secretaries, state office-bearers and representatives from around 72 districts participated in the meeting. The meeting focused on pending demands of teachers, new education policies, service-related issues and the organisation’s future strategy. Focus on strengthening organisation at block level The meeting was chaired by state president Sushil Kumar Pandey. He said the organisation will be strengthened by restructuring committees at the block level and including active and dedicated teachers. He appealed to teachers to remain united at the district level and raise their voices for their rights. ‘Teachers’ unity helped achieve Fifth Pay Commission benefits’ Former state president and chief guest Abhimanyu Prasad Tiwari said teachers received the benefits of the Fifth Pay Commission due to their unity and struggle. He urged teachers to continue their collective efforts for the welfare of education, teachers and future generations. Old pension scheme and TET issue raised State president Sushil Kumar Pandey said the TET issue has affected the jobs of lakhs of teachers. He said despite several representations, no decision has been taken by the government, causing resentment among teachers. He also reiterated the demand for implementation of the old pension scheme to ensure social security for teachers. Anger over delay in pending payments Concerns were raised over the attitude of departmental officials. Pandey said pending payments of teachers are not being cleared on time and accountability should be fixed against officials responsible for such delays. He said the fight for teachers’ interests will continue from the streets to the assembly. Demand to stop frequent non-academic orders The state executive committee demanded a halt to the continuous issuance of non-academic orders in schools. Objections were also raised against withholding teachers’ salaries without explanation. Other demands included appointment of a computer operator in every school, restoring school timings changed during the Covid period and promoting teachers to the post of Block Education Officer. Confidence expressed in state leadership District presidents and secretaries from all districts expressed unanimous faith in the executive committee led by Sushil Kumar Pandey. Office-bearers raised the slogan “Hum chale mool sangathan ke saath” and pledged to remain united and continue working for teachers’ welfare. Attendees Former state president Abhimanyu Prasad Tiwari attended the meeting as chief guest. Former state senior vice-president Ram Teerth Mishra and former national president of the All India Primary Teachers Federation (AIPTF) Geeta Pandey were present as special guests. Members of the state executive committee along with district presidents and secretaries from around 72 districts also attended the meeting.

stories.title: Kairana Hindu exodus accused killed in encounter:Daylight gunfight in Shamli leaves constable shot in abdomen
stories.summary: A ₹1 lakh reward criminal, Mohammad Furkan, was killed in a daylight police encounter in Uttar Pradesh's Shamli on Wednesday. According to police, Furkan opened indiscriminate fire with a carbine and pistol as soon as he spotted the police team. A constable was shot in the abdomen during the exchange. Police retaliated in self-defence, during which Furkan was shot and collapsed. Both Furkan and the injured constable were rushed to hospital, where doctors declared Furkan dead. The constable was referred to Meerut for advanced treatment. Furkan had been absconding for the past four years. Twelve years ago, he allegedly shot dead trader leader Vinod Singhal in broad daylight at Kairana's main market. More than 20 cases, including murder, robbery and extortion, were registered against him. Police said Furkan was an active member of the Mukim Kala gang. In 2016, three traders were murdered in Kairana, after which several Hindu families reportedly migrated from the town. Furkan and Mukim Kala were among those accused in connection with the exodus. The encounter took place around 3 pm in the forests near Rangana village in the Jhinjhana area, about 16 km from the district headquarters. See two pictures Trader leader shot dead in broad daylight In August 2014, Furkan, a member of the notorious Mukim Kala gang in western Uttar Pradesh, allegedly gunned down trader leader Vinod Singhal at his grocery shop in Kairana's main market after he refused to pay extortion money. He was arrested and sent to jail. After spending nearly six months in jail, Furkan secured bail. Soon after his release, he allegedly reached the shop of cold drink agency owner Ishwarchand alias Billu and demanded extortion money. When Billu refused, Furkan allegedly threatened to kill him like Vinod Singhal. Fearing for their lives, Billu's family left Kairana and settled in Panipat. Around the same period, gang leader Mukim Kala allegedly shot dead traders Rajendra and Shiv Kumar for refusing to pay extortion money. The killings triggered protests by traders in Shamli, who shut markets and demanded the arrest of the accused. Police said the atmosphere in Kairana deteriorated thereafter, with traders continuing to migrate. BJP MP released list of migrated families in 2016 On May 30, 2016, then BJP MP from Kairana Hukum Singh raised the issue of the alleged migration of traders and Hindu families from the town. He released a list of 346 families who had reportedly migrated. Following the controversy, the then Director General of Police announced a ₹50,000 reward on Furkan. On April 8, 2017, police arrested him after an encounter in the forests near Aldi village in Kandhla police station area. He was later released on bail. In 2019, Furkan allegedly became involved in drug trafficking. After being arrested again, he was sent to jail. On November 8, 2021, following Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's visit to Kairana, Furkan surrendered before a court after cancelling his bail in a Gangster Act case. He remained in jail for some time, secured bail again, and absconded. Police had been searching for him for nearly four years before Wednesday's encounter.

stories.title: SP MP Barq accused of inciting mob in Sambhal violence:Judicial Commission says 4 deaths not due to police firing
stories.summary: The violence that took place in Sambhal on November 24, 2024, was the result of a pre-planned conspiracy, according to a judicial commission report. The report said the roles of Sambhal MP Zia-ur-Rehman Barq, Sambhal MLA Iqbal Mahmood’s son Sohail Iqbal, Jama Masjid Intazamia Committee president Zafar Ali, secretary Mashhood Ali Farooqui, vice-president Laddan Khan, advocate Qasim Jamal and other committee members came to light during the investigation. The commission said the crowd was provoked with the aim of stopping the court-ordered survey and establishing political dominance at the local level. The report was prepared after examining statements of 199 witnesses, forensic reports, videos, documents and police records. The Uttar Pradesh government had constituted a judicial commission to investigate the Sambhal violence. The three-member commission submitted an 857-page report in Hindi and English to the state government on Wednesday, which was tabled in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly the same day. Know what was said in the report Propaganda spread that Jama Masjid is in danger According to the report, MP Zia-ur-Rehman Barq made speeches on November 19 and 22 regarding the survey and the mosque, which created an impression among people that the Jama Masjid was under threat and could be taken over. The commission said videos of these speeches were circulated on social media, increasing tension in the area. It added that people were not informed that the court had only ordered a survey. Instead, a message was allegedly spread that the mosque could be demolished or taken away, which created a more sensitive atmosphere. The report said a large number of people gathered after being influenced by this narrative and were prepared for violence. People arrived with stones and weapons as part of a conspiracy The commission said that on the morning of November 24, a large number of people gathered around the Jama Masjid carrying stones, weapons and other items. The report said the objective was to stop the survey and attack the police-administration team. It stated that preparations for the attack appeared to have been made in advance. According to the report, Sohail Iqbal reached the mosque in the morning and, after leaving the spot, allegedly moved among the crowd and provoked people. Witness statements mentioned his presence and alleged role in instigating the crowd. Following this, a large number of people came out from lanes around the mosque and joined the gathering, after which incidents of stone-pelting, arson and firing began. Four deaths not caused by police firing, says report During the violence, incidents of stone-pelting, firing at police, damage to government property and snatching of weapons were reported. A total of 28 police personnel were injured, including seven who suffered bullet injuries. The commission said the four people who died were killed by bullets fired from .315 bore weapons. It stated that police did not possess .315 bore weapons and available ballistic evidence did not confirm that the deaths occurred due to police firing. The report said police first used tear gas, chilli grenades, stun grenades and rubber bullets to control the situation and did not use lethal weapons. Police and administration prevented major communal violence The commission praised the police and district administration for handling the situation with restraint and strategy. It said authorities prevented the crowd from reaching Hindu-majority areas, which helped avoid a larger communal clash. The report added that the situation could have become far more serious if the crowd had entered those areas. Violence aimed at stopping survey and establishing political dominance The report said the main objective behind the violence was to stop the court-ordered survey and establish political dominance at the local level. The commission recommended action against the accused under strict provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). It also suggested effective legal and administrative measures to prevent similar incidents in the future. Three-member judicial commission was formed On November 28, 2024, the Uttar Pradesh government formed a judicial inquiry commission headed by former Allahabad High Court judge Justice Devendra Kumar Arora. Retired IAS officer Amit Mohan Prasad and retired IPS officer Arvind Kumar Jain were appointed as members of the commission. Now know the complete matter On November 19, 2024, the Hindu side claimed that Sambhal’s Shahi Jama Masjid was the Shri Harihar Temple and approached the Civil Senior Division Court in Chandausi seeking a survey. Following the court order, the first phase of the survey was conducted on the same day. The second phase took place on November 24, when thousands of people gathered at the site. Violence broke out while attempts were allegedly made to disrupt the survey. Police faced stone-pelting and firing, resulting in four deaths. SP Krishna Kumar Bishnoi, ASP Anuj Chaudhary, deputy collector and 28 police personnel were injured. FIR against more than 2750 people including SP MP A total of 12 FIRs were registered at Sambhal Kotwali and Nakhasa police stations. More than 2,750 people were booked, including SP MP Zia-ur-Rehman Barq and Sohail Iqbal, son of SP MLA Iqbal Mahmood. A total of 158 accused, including Jama Masjid president Zafar Ali, were sent to jail. Those arrested included three women and three associates of absconding gangster Sharik Satha, who was described as the main conspirator behind the Sambhal violence. The three associates were identified as Mulla Afroz, Waris and Ghulam. Mulla Afroz was booked under the National Security Act (NSA) in October 2025, followed by similar action against Waris and Ghulam. After receiving bail from the Allahabad High Court, Zafar Ali was released from Moradabad jail on August 1, 2025. He had been sent to jail on March 24 and spent 131 days in custody. On June 18, the SIT filed a 1,128-page chargesheet against 23 people, including MP Zia-ur-Rehman Barq. However, the name of SP MLA Iqbal Mahmood’s son Sohail Iqbal was not included in the chargesheet.

Besides this, 30 new air conditioners will be installed in wards, while a seminar hall and library will be developed for DNB students. The hospital administration is also working to improve cleanliness and lighting arrangements on the premises. The update came a day after District Magistrate (DM) Deepak Meena inspected the hospital on Tuesday and reviewed the existing shortcomings. SIC took stock after DM's inspection During his surprise inspection on Tuesday, DM Deepak Meena directed the hospital administration to address the facility gaps at the earliest. Following this, SIC Dr OP Singh inspected the entire hospital on Wednesday and reviewed the issues. He said the district administration is committed to providing a better environment and treatment facilities to patients and their families. The new action plan has been prepared following the DM’s instructions. SIC said 10 new dialysis beds will be added following the instructions of the Deputy Chief Minister. This will help kidney patients avoid long waiting periods and ensure timely treatment. Emergency services planned at trauma centre The hospital is preparing to start emergency services at the long-pending trauma centre with available resources so that accident victims can receive immediate treatment. The hospital will also receive 30 new air conditioners with the support of MP Ravi Kishan. These will be installed in different wards to provide relief to patients from heat and humidity. Library to be built behind ICU Dr OP Singh said a proposal has been sent to build a seminar hall and library on one to two decimals of vacant land behind the ICU. This will provide better study and research facilities for DNB medical students. He added that cleanliness across the hospital campus is being improved as per the DM’s directions. Lighting and CCTV arrangements are also being upgraded at various locations. One patient will get 2 passes Security arrangements have also been revised. Now, patients admitted to the emergency department will receive only two visitor passes. Only two attendants with valid passes will be allowed inside at a time to prevent overcrowding in wards. SIC assured that the new facilities and development works will provide significant relief to the public and improve healthcare services at the district hospital.

stories.title: No toll on Lucknow–Kanpur Expressway:NHAI waives fee until ₹4,700-crore road is repaired after repeated cave-ins
stories.summary: Amid repeated problems on the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway, the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has taken several key decisions. NHAI has issued a notice proposing to declare the expressway construction company PNC Infratech as a non-performing contractor. The company will not be awarded any future projects by NHAI. The company will also have to bear the cost of repairing defects on the expressway, which is estimated to be around ₹3 crore. No toll collection will be allowed until the expressway is fully repaired. NHAI held a press conference in Lucknow on August 5 regarding the matter. During the press conference, NHAI Regional Manager Gautam Vishal shared details of the action taken so far. He said that a slip was noticed near kilometre 64 of the expressway on July 26, after which immediate repairs were carried out. He added that wherever similar complaints were reported, repair work was carried out continuously.

stories.title: 50-year-old man misbehaves with woman:Lucknow resident hits him with slippers over 35 times in 1.5 minutes, chases him for 500 metres
stories.summary: A woman thrashed a 50-year-old man with slippers on a road in Lalbagh area of Lucknow’s Kaiserbagh police station limits on Wednesday afternoon after he allegedly made an inappropriate comment at her. According to people present at the spot, the woman hit the accused more than 35 times with her slipper within around one-and-a-half minutes. The accused tried to escape to protect himself, but the woman chased him for around 500 metres and continued hitting him. A crowd gathered at the spot during the incident, and a video of the incident has also surfaced. Woman says man passed inappropriate remark According to the woman, she was going to deliver a lunchbox to her brother around 12:30 pm on Wednesday. During this time, a 50-year-old man allegedly passed an inappropriate remark at her. She said she got angry after the sudden incident and confronted the accused on the spot. She then removed her slipper and started hitting him. See 2 pictures... People intervene and calm the situation A crowd gathered during the incident. Eyewitnesses said the accused admitted his mistake and apologised to the woman. People present at the spot also requested her to let him go. The woman later released him after warning him not to repeat such behaviour. No police complaint filed, video shared online The woman told Dainik Bhaskar over the phone that she has not filed any complaint at Kaiserbagh police station. She said the accused had already been taught a lesson at the spot. However, to spread awareness and send a message to people who indulge in such behaviour, the video of the incident was shared on social media and has gone viral. Woman keeps identity confidential The woman spoke to Dainik Bhaskar on the condition of anonymity. She said she does not wish to come into the public spotlight but wants women to immediately oppose people who behave inappropriately with them.

stories.title: Doctor's wife dies by suicide in Lucknow:Husband breaks open door after returning from Sitapur; son is Army major
stories.summary: A health department senior assistant in Lucknow found his wife hanging inside a room after he returned home from duty in Sitapur on Tuesday evening. He knocked on the door for a long time, but there was no response from inside. Later, with the help of neighbours, he broke open the door and found his wife hanging from a ceiling fan with a noose. Neighbours informed the police following the incident. The police reached the spot, brought down the body and sent it for postmortem. A forensic team also inspected the scene and collected necessary evidence. Returned home at 4 PM, found door closed The incident took place at house number 8/141 in Jankipuram Sector-8. Anil Tripathi lives there with his family. He works as a senior assistant at the Women’s Hospital in Sitapur. Like every day, Anil had gone to work on Tuesday. When he returned home around 4 pm, the main gate was open, but the door of one room was locked from inside. He called out several times and knocked on the door, but received no response. Suspecting something wrong, he called his neighbours. The door was then broken open. Inside the room, his wife Asha Tripathi (47) was found hanging from the ceiling fan with the help of a saree. She was brought down and police were informed. Both sons are also doctors, one is a Major in the Army According to the family, Anil and Asha have two sons. Their elder son Dr Ashnil Tripathi is posted as a Major in the Indian Army in Gwalior. Their younger son Dr Asmit Tripathi is associated with Rama Medical College in Ghaziabad. Both sons and other family members were informed about the incident. Forensic team collected evidence As soon as the information was received, Jankipuram police and the forensic team reached the spot. The team examined the room and nearby areas and collected necessary evidence. Police sent the body for postmortem. No suicide note has been confirmed to have been recovered from the spot. Reason for suicide not yet clear Police said the reason behind the woman’s death is not clear yet. Family members and neighbours are being questioned. According to police, the initial investigation has not found any indication of an outsider entering the house. Further action will be taken based on the postmortem report and investigation findings.

stories.title: 'Yogi's police beat us badly, we won't return to UP':Robbers apologise from wheelchair after robbery in Varanasi
stories.summary: Two robbers who came from Bhopal to Varanasi for a robbery apologised while sitting on wheelchairs. They kept pleading before the police with folded hands, asking for one chance to reform. The accused, identified as Shabbir and Masallah, said, “Yogi’s police in UP beats people a lot. We will not come here again.” Police arrested both accused in an encounter early morning on August 3. Both sustained bullet injuries to their legs during the exchange of fire. They had allegedly looted 27 kg of silver from an employee of a jewellery trader on July 16. Police recovered 4 kg of the stolen silver after the encounter. ADCP Kashi Zone Vaibhav Bangar said both accused were produced before the court on August 4 and sent to jail. Before their court appearance, they kept apologising to the police. Both are members of the Iranian gang from Madhya Pradesh. Police are searching for their other associates. See 2 pictures... Committed robbery posing as Crime Branch officer Now see 2 pictures of the encounter Identified through 300 CCTV footage and crime records ADCP Vaibhav Bangar said police checked around 300 CCTV recordings after the robbery. The footage helped identify the accused and trace their route. Police suspected their links with the Iranian gang operating from Madhya Pradesh and began searching for the suspects. On Monday night, the Special Operations Group (SOG) arrested both accused after an encounter in Lautubir area under Lanka police station limits. The ADCP said the accused had taken help from Hafiz and Zulfeqar of the Iranian settlement in Mumbai for the robbery. Police are also searching for Shabbir’s wife Pakiza, who allegedly sold the stolen silver to jewellers. The accused had booked a Baleno car belonging to Aman Ali from Ranchi and travelled to Varanasi. After committing the robbery, they went to Prayagraj and abandoned the car there. They then travelled by bus to Jabalpur and later to Pipariya. Shabbir has 11 criminal cases registered against him, while Masallah has two cases against him. Iranian gang targets businessmen by posing as police According to police, members of the Iranian gang are nomadic and identify themselves as Iranians. They mainly operate in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand. The gang commits crimes under the cover of selling spectacles. Their language is also different from common speech, making it difficult for others to understand their plans. The gang’s modus operandi involves posing as police officers, Crime Branch officials or STF personnel to target people and traders. On the instructions of gang leaders Anuj Dehra and Mehndi Hasan, members carry out crimes in several states. After selling stolen jewellery, the gang members escape to another city or state. Police consider the ‘Iranian Dera’ in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, as the main hub of the gang’s network. Police said the Iranian gang has committed crimes in Varanasi earlier as well. On March 24, 2022, the gang allegedly stole a bag containing ₹8 lakh from a Ghazipur-based businessman on the Kabirchaura-Piyari road by pretending to conduct a police check.

stories.title: Ganga floods highways in UP, school washed away:Dam overflows, car swept away in Shamli, 3 dead; rain alert across 75 districts
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh’s monsoon has gained momentum again, with continuous rainfall causing rivers to swell across the state. The Ganga river has reached close to the danger mark in Bijnor and Farrukhabad. More than 45 villages are facing flood-like conditions, while water has entered over 40 government schools. River water is flowing over highways at several places. In Bijnor, the approach road of a highway was washed away due to the strong current, creating a 12-foot-deep pit. In Farrukhabad, barricading was done near the Chitrakoot Dip area and traffic movement on the highway was stopped. Heavy rainfall has been reported since Wednesday morning in 10 cities including Varanasi, Prayagraj, Kanpur and Noida. Around 30 cities including Lucknow, Barabanki, Prayagraj and Varanasi are witnessing cloudy weather. A rain alert has been issued for all 75 districts, with heavy rainfall expected in 65 cities. A day earlier, on Tuesday, rain lashed 57 cities including Lucknow, Kanpur, Prayagraj and Mathura. Banda recorded the highest rainfall at 69.3 mm, followed by Sultanpur with 61.7 mm. In Mathura, heavy rain led to four feet of waterlogging in an underpass, submerging scooters and bikes. In Shamli, a car was swept away due to strong water currents, while a school bus got stuck in an underpass and was pulled out with the help of a tractor. In Mirzapur, three people died in rain and lightning-related incidents. Two children drowned in a pit dug for road construction, while a 25-year-old man preparing for the NET examination died after being struck by lightning. Rain and flood situation across UP In Shamli, a school bus got stuck in a water-filled underpass after heavy rainfall on Tuesday. Villagers pulled it out with the help of a tractor. A car was swept away amid strong water currents during heavy rain in Shamli. In Bijnor, a section of the Bahsuma-Thakurdwara State Highway near Pandavnagar police outpost was washed away. In Farrukhabad, 24 villages under Amritpur tehsil are affected by floods. A dam in Sonbhadra started overflowing amid heavy rainfall. Meteorological department update Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said the monsoon system has become active over Uttar Pradesh. It is passing through Delhi, Lucknow and Patna, due to which several cyclonic systems have become active. He said monsoon winds have strengthened over the Gangetic plains, leading to heavy rainfall across the state. The entire state is likely to witness intense showers for the next four to five days. District-wise updates Varanasi: Heavy rain lashed the city on Wednesday morning as dark clouds covered the sky. The Ganga’s water level is rising at a rate of one centimetre per hour and was recorded at 61.92 metres at 6 am. Noida: The sky remained cloudy with 80% humidity. Intermittent rainfall is expected throughout the day, according to the weather department. Agra: Cloudy weather and cool winds provided relief from humid conditions. Light rain with strong winds is expected during the day. Bareilly: The city remained cloudy in the morning, with a rain alert issued for the day. The maximum temperature is expected to remain around 31°C. Kanpur: More than 50 mm rainfall was recorded in the last 24 hours. Continuous rain since late Tuesday night has caused waterlogging on roads. Chitrakoot: Farmers welcomed the rainfall, saying it will benefit crops including paddy, arhar, jowar, moong and sesame. They hope continued rainfall will improve agricultural output. Jalaun: Intermittent rain continued for nearly 22 hours, leading to waterlogging in streets and low-lying areas of Orai, Konch, Madhogarh and Kalpi. Lucknow: The city remained cloudy with chances of moderate to heavy rainfall. A wall near Lucknow City Station collapsed, damaging a car and six motorcycles. The weather department has issued an orange alert for the next two days. Agra: A portion of MG Road near Hariparvat intersection caved in, creating a deep pit filled with water. Traffic was diverted by police. Mirzapur: Two six-year-old children drowned in a water-filled pit dug for a six-lane road project. A 25-year-old NET aspirant also died after lightning struck him while he was working in a field. Shamli: A school bus returning after dropping students got stuck in a flooded railway underpass. It was later pulled out with the help of villagers and a tractor. Barabanki: The Ghaghra river has flooded villages under the Ram Sanehi Ghat area. Water has entered several houses, affecting hundreds of families. Lakhimpur Kheri: Erosion by the Sharda river continued, with another classroom of a government school washed away. Around 300 metres of the main road has already been submerged. Farrukhabad: Floodwater reached the Badaun-Farrukhabad State Highway. Police installed barricades at Chitrakoot Dip and stopped traffic movement. Around 33 villages are affected, impacting more than 23,000 people. Bijnor: Rising Ganga water levels flooded several villages in the Jilelpur area. The approach road connecting Chandpur and Hastinapur was washed away, breaking connectivity for several villages. Firozabad: Heavy rain caused waterlogging in roads, markets, hospitals and residential areas. Several areas reported knee-deep water. Rivers above danger mark in 18 districts The impact of continuous rainfall in the hills is now visible in Uttar Pradesh. Rivers are flowing above the danger mark in 18 districts, including Ayodhya, Azamgarh, Bahraich, Ballia, Balrampur, Barabanki, Basti, Deoria, Farrukhabad, Gonda, Gorakhpur, Kasganj, Maharajganj, Mau, Sant Kabir Nagar, Shravasti, Siddharthnagar and Sitapur. Authorities have increased monitoring and appealed to people to avoid going near rivers and remain alert. IMD warns of weaker monsoon India Meteorological Department Director General Dr M Mohapatra said signs of El Niño developing after the weakening of La Niña conditions in the Pacific Ocean could lead to reduced rainfall. He said the southwest monsoon may remain weaker than normal this year. Lower snowfall in the Northern Hemisphere between January and March could also impact monsoon activity.

stories.title: 3 Kanwariyas killed as container lorry crashes into bike:They were heading to Haridwar to fetch Ganga water; accident on expressway
stories.summary: In Meerut, around 4:30 AM on Wednesday, a speeding container truck ran over three Kanwariyas, killing them. The collision was so severe that the bike was completely damaged. All three Kanwariyas were thrown about 10 meters away on the road. The accident occurred near Bhojpur on the Delhi-Meerut Expressway. All three were going to Haridwar to fetch Ganga water on a bike. The deceased have been identified as Pradeep, Rajkumar, and Gyan Prakash – all from Aligarh. With the beginning of the Sawan month, the Kanwar Yatra is at its peak. Different facets of it are being seen on the roads of UP. Some are travelling disguised as aliens, while others are carrying their parents or elderly family members on their shoulders in a Kanwar. Arun Kumar, a Kanwariya from Delhi, is undertaking the Kanwar Yatra demanding justice for his brother after his murder. In Muzaffarnagar, he said, "We have come with the Kanwar to get justice for our brother. His memory will last a lifetime, but we want him to get justice and the accused to be encountered." He informed that 30-35 Kanwariyas are carrying Ganga water from Haridwar to Uttam Nagar, Delhi. Meanwhile, Kishan Ghosh from Delhi, who is undertaking the Kanwar Yatra dressed as an alien, said, "Often, sadness is visible on the faces of Kanwariyas while returning with water. They smile when they see me, and that makes me happy. I am also traveling with Ganga water on my back."

stories.title: Lucknow to get 18,113 affordable homes:LDA identifies land, project to benefit 90,000 people
stories.summary: The Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) has unveiled a major plan to provide affordable housing for low-income families in the city. Under the Zonal Development Plan, 18,113 affordable homes will be developed in Cluster-2, located between Sultanpur Road and Kanpur Road. The project is expected to directly benefit around 90,000 people. An LDA survey found a shortage of affordable housing in the Cluster-2 area. Based on this assessment, the authority has included a proposal for more than 18,000 new homes in the development plan. Construction sites have also been marked on the zonal development map. The proposed homes will have a built-up area of around 800 sq ft. They will be designed specifically to meet the needs of low-income and resource-constrained families. Around 53.83 hectares of land will be required for the project, and the necessary land has already been earmarked in the plan. LDA has designated the proposed housing sites for residential use in the Zonal Development Plan to ensure faster implementation of future projects. No new affordable housing planned in Cluster-1 According to the LDA, Cluster-1, located between Ayodhya Road and Sultanpur Road, already has sufficient housing. As a result, no proposal for additional affordable homes has been included for this area. What the LDA Vice-Chairman said LDA Vice-Chairman Prathamesh Kumar said the Zonal Development Plans for both Cluster-1 and Cluster-2 have been finalised. He said the required land and construction sites for affordable housing have been identified in the plan, making it easier to implement future housing projects.

stories.title: Woman accuses BJP MLA of tearing her clothes, groping her:Claims he threatened to rape her young daughter; Sultanpur legislator denies allegations
stories.summary: A woman from Uttar Pradesh’s Sultanpur has accused BJP MLA Vinod Singh of attempting to rape her and threatening to kill her. The woman alleged that the MLA called her to his house by threatening to get her daughter raped and then tried to sexually assault her. She claimed that the MLA touched her private parts, tore her clothes and threatened her. She said she managed to escape by pushing him away. During a press conference in Delhi on July 3, the woman alleged that the MLA threatened to destroy her if she did not comply with his demands. She also claimed that people were following her and she was being threatened with an acid attack and harm to her husband and children. The woman said she approached the police but no action was taken on her complaint. MLA denies allegations, calls them a conspiracy BJP MLA Vinod Singh rejected all allegations and claimed they were an attempt to defame him. He said a fraud and cheating case has been registered against the woman’s husband and that his wife was being used to make false allegations to avoid arrest. He said he has faith in the court and the truth would come out during the investigation. Read the woman's full allegations verbatim The woman claimed that she and her family lived in an apartment in Lucknow’s Hazratganj area, where the MLA lived on the fourth floor. She alleged that the MLA had been harassing her for the past three to four months and used his gunner Dhananjay Yadav to call her. According to her, the gunner threatened her and said that if she did not listen to the MLA, she and her 10-year-old daughter would be sexually assaulted. She said she went to the MLA’s house due to fear for her daughter’s safety. She alleged that on June 3 night, the MLA was intoxicated and tried to assault her, but she managed to escape by pushing him away. Woman claims she received threats after incident The woman alleged that after the incident, the MLA threatened her and claimed he had harmed several people in the past. She said she informed her family and shifted from the apartment to a rented house in Gomti Nagar. She also alleged that she started receiving calls after the MLA returned from Sultanpur. Woman alleges police did not register FIR After complaining to the Women's Commission, an FIR was filed against her She said - I did not work in the MLA's office Allegations against the manager too, demand for FIR against the MLA Now read what MLA Vinod Singh said on the whole matter-

stories.title: Administrative rift surfaces at KGMU:Executive Council flags delay in decisions, seeks Vice-Chancellor's intervention
stories.summary: The administrative tug-of-war between the Vice-Chancellor and the Registrar at KGMU has now come out in the open. On Tuesday, a meeting of the Executive Council was held. In the meeting, members of the Executive Council expressed strong displeasure over the delay in implementing the decision regarding the regularisation of employees at the Registrar's level. Members alleged that several important decisions taken in May 2026 have not been implemented even after three months. In this regard, members of the Executive Council submitted a written request to the Vice-Chancellor, demanding intervention. Displeasure expressed over delay The meeting of the Executive Council was held under the chairmanship of Vice-Chancellor Dr Sonia Nityanand. In the meeting, senior member Dr OP Singh stated that several decisions of the Executive Council have been deliberately withheld. He specifically raised the issue of employee regularisation. According to the council, orders in this regard should have been issued in May. However, the order has not yet been issued by the Registrar's office. The delay is causing harm to the employees. They are not receiving the benefits of regularisation. All members of the council supported Dr OP's objections. The council unanimously demanded immediate compliance with all pending decisions. Additionally, the Vice-Chancellor was asked to ensure effective administrative control over the Registrar, so that there is no unnecessary delay in the council's decisions in the future. University will appeal The meeting also discussed the case of Dr KP Singh, who was dismissed from the post of former Associate Professor in the Microbiology Department. The High Court had quashed the order of his dismissal from service and directed a fresh departmental inquiry and an opportunity for cross-examination. On this, the Executive Council unanimously decided that the university would file a special appeal in the division bench after the order of the single bench. It was also decided to avail the services of a senior advocate to effectively present the university's case in court.

stories.title: Dubai agrees to arrest Shubham Jaiswal:MEA submits 39,000-page warrant for fugitive in cough syrup trafficking case
stories.summary: The path has been cleared for the arrest of fugitive mastermind Shubham Jaiswal in the ₹2000 crore codeine cough syrup smuggling case. After issuing a Red Corner Notice for the arrest of Shubham, who had taken refuge in Dubai, the Ministry of External Affairs has now handed over a 39,000-page provisional warrant to the Dubai government. Based on this, the Dubai government has agreed to arrest Shubham Jaiswal. It is worth noting that the Indian government had cancelled the passport of the codeine cough syrup mastermind. However, he is living in Dubai on the basis of having a Dubai Golden Visa. The Golden Visa is valid for ten years. Arrest soon As soon as Dubai's security agencies arrest Shubham, a team of CBI and Uttar Pradesh police officers from India will travel to Dubai to secure his extradition and bring him to India. Following this, the cases registered against Shubham will be heard. Interpol active with Dubai Police Dubai Police and intelligence agencies are monitoring Shubham's passport, visa credentials, bank accounts, and local hideouts. Interpol has issued a Red Corner Notice for Shubham at immigration counters in international airports of all 195 member countries.

stories.title: Chandrashekhar fields candidates from 1% population groups:Makes surprise bet on 17 seats; does it upset SP-BSP's caste equation?
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh politics cannot be viewed separately from the lens of caste. Political parties also make decisions based on caste equations when selecting candidates. Among the 45 candidates announced by the Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) last Friday (July 31), 17 are faces whose population in that region is less than other castes. In such a situation, questions are being raised about Chandrashekhar's political understanding. Chandrashekhar adopted Mayawati's strategy in candidate selection Chandrashekhar had announced in-charges for 45 assembly seats. Currently, they have been made assembly in-charges. However, all of them are campaigning in the area as candidates. This method of selecting candidates is similar to BSP's strategy. In BSP too, there has been a trend of later declaring assembly in-charges as candidates. Now Chandrashekhar also appears to be moving forward with the same strategy. If we talk about caste equations, out of 45, the highest number, 18 Dalit faces, have been given a place. Among these, 5 seats are general. After this, 16 OBC, 10 Muslim, and 1 Sikh candidate have been made in-charge. Now, let's talk about those 17 candidates of Chandrashekhar whose caste population is the lowest in their own constituency 1. Bet on Prajapati face in Jafrabad, population less than 1% On Jaunpur's Jafrabad assembly seat, the party has made Jiyalal Prajapati the in-charge. He belongs to the OBC category. His selection is under discussion given the caste equations of the seat. The population of Prajapati voters in Jafrabad is less than 1%. Meanwhile, Thakurs are 23%, Jatavs 14%, Yadavs 13%, and Brahmins 10%. Nishad, Patel, and Vaishya voters are also more than 5%. If we talk about political history, most MLAs from Yadav, Kshatriya, and Brahmin communities have been elected here. Assembly in-charges for another 18 seats 2. Gurjar face made in-charge for Bah seat, population only 1% Sarala Singh Gurjar has been made in-charge for the Bah assembly seat in Agra. She belongs to the OBC category. Questions are being raised about her selection given the caste equations of the seat. In Bah, the population of Brahmin and Thakur voters is about 21-21%. After this, Jatavs are 18% and Nishads are 15%. However, the population of the Gurjar community is only about 1%. Looking at the political history of the seat, Kshatriya MLAs have been elected here 12 times, which is the highest. 3. Bet on Sanjeev in Meerut Cantt, with 24% Vaishya and only 2% Pal population On the Meerut Cantt assembly seat, Azad Samaj Party has appointed Sanjeev Pal as in-charge. He belongs to the OBC category. Looking at the caste equations of the seat, the Pal community's population here is only about 2%. In Meerut Cantt, Vaishya voters are the highest at 24%. Besides this, Punjabis are 12%, Brahmins and Jatavs are 9-9% each, while Jats and Valmikis are 7-7% each. The political history of this seat is also special. 10 seats where the party is trying to consolidate the Muslim-Dalit vote The last 8 MLAs from here have been elected from the Vaishya community. In such a situation, questions are being raised about the decision to put forward a face from the less populated Pal community. 4. In Sikandrarao, 13-13% Lodhi-Thakur, 3% Yadav population gets a chance On Hathras's Sikandrarao assembly seat, Azad Samaj Party has appointed Bijendra Singh Yadav as in-charge. He belongs to the OBC category. On this seat, the Yadav voters' population is only about 3%. In Sikandrarao, Lodhi and Thakur are 13-13%, Jatav 12% and Muslim 10%. Meanwhile, the population of Dhangar and Kushwaha communities is 8-8%. In the 90s, 4 MLAs from the Yadav community were elected, but after that, 5 MLAs from the Thakur community and one from the Brahmin community were elected. In such a situation, what is the party's strategy behind promoting a Yadav face, this is an important question. 5. 18% Muslims in Palia, trust shown in Sardar Manohar Singh The party has appointed Sardar Manohar Singh as in-charge for the Palia assembly seat of Lakhimpur Kheri. He belongs to the Sikh community. The population of Sikh voters in Palia is only about 3%. On this seat, Muslims are 18%, Kurmi 16%, Brahmin 15%, Tharu 14% and Jatav 12%. Meanwhile, in political history, Dalit MLAs have been elected from this seat 7 times so far. In such a situation, it is natural for questions to arise about the party's caste equations regarding the gamble on a face from a 3% Sikh population. 6. Tulsi Ram, from Govind Nagar with 44% Brahmin and 5% Valmiki population, made in-charge The Azad Samaj Party has appointed Tulsi Ram Valmiki as the in-charge for the Govind Nagar assembly seat in Kanpur Nagar. He belongs to the SC category. The Valmiki community's population on this seat is about 5%. In Govind Nagar, Brahmin voters are the highest at 44%. Meanwhile, the Muslim and Kurmi communities each have a population of about 5%. So far, Brahmin MLAs have been elected 14 times and Bhumihar MLAs 3 times from this seat. In such a situation, the party's strategy to bring forward a face from the Valmiki community is under discussion. 7. In Lucknow Cantt, a bet on Aniket, from a population with 22% Kayastha and 3.5% Dhanuk Aniket Dhanuk has been made in-charge of the Lucknow Cantt assembly seat. He belongs to the SC category. The party may make him its candidate in the election. The Dhanuk community's population on this seat is about 3.5%. In Lucknow Cantt, Kayasthas are 22%, Brahmins and Yadavs are 19-19% each, and Punjabis are 14%. Muslim voters are about 8%, while Kurmis and another backward class are about 5-5% each. Talking about political history, Brahmin MLAs have been elected here the most, 12 times. 8. Rohania: Anud Yadav, from a 5% Yadav population, is the candidate in a seat with 26% Bhumihars Azad Samaj Party has made Anud Yadav in-charge of the Rohania assembly seat in Varanasi. He belongs to the OBC category. The population of Yadav voters on this seat is about 5%. In Rohania, Bhumihars are 26%, Kurmis 21%, Baniyas 10%, Brahmins and Jatavs 9-9% each, and Rajbhars 7%. After the seat was formed in 2012, MLAs from the Patel community have been elected 3 times and from the Bhumihar community once. 9. Trust in Raja Ram, who has 18% Brahmin, 8% Nishad population in Ayah Shah Raja Ram Nishad has been made in-charge of the Ayah Shah assembly seat in Fatehpur. He belongs to the OBC category. The population of Nishad voters on this seat is about 8%. In Ayah Shah, Brahmins are 18% and Thakurs are 12%. Meanwhile, the population of Muslim, Yadav, Paswan, Baniya, and Raidas communities is less than 6%. After the seat was formed in 2008, MLAs from the Vaishya community have been elected 3 times and from the Pal community once. In such a situation, it remains to be seen which equation the decision to bring forward a Nishad face will affect. 10. Bet on a candidate with 7% Yadav population, excluding 19% Jatav in Madhuban Azad Samaj Party has appointed Shiv Sagar Yadav as in-charge for the Madhuban assembly seat in Mau. He belongs to the OBC category. The Yadav community's population on this seat is about 7%. In Madhuban, Jatavs are 19%, Brahmins 14%, Muslims 9%, and Kurmis 8%. MLAs from different castes have been elected from this seat. 11. 16-16% Brahmin-Jatav in Rudhauli, Mohd. Akib appointed in-charge The party has appointed Dr. Mohd. Akib as in-charge for the Rudhauli assembly seat in Basti. He belongs to the Muslim community. The Muslim voter population on this seat is about 13%. In Rudhauli, Brahmins and Jatavs are 16-16%, Kurmis 14%, and Mauryas 11%. Pasi, Vaishya, and Yadav voters are also present in good numbers. In political history, MLAs from the Kurmi community have been elected 5 times and from the Vaishya community 2 times here. An MLA from the Brahmin community has also been elected once. In such a situation, it is natural for questions to arise about the party's strategy of promoting a Muslim face. 12. 14% Brahmins in Tamkuhi Raj, Advocate Raqib Alam appointed in-charge Azad Samaj Party has appointed Advocate Raqib Alam as in-charge for the Tamkuhi Raj assembly seat in Kushinagar. He belongs to the Muslim community. The Muslim voter population on this seat is around 9%. In Tamkuhi Raj, Brahmins are 14%, Vaishyas 12%, Jatavs 9%, and Mauryas 8%. Talking about political history, MLAs from the Vaishya community have been elected the most number of times from here. In such a situation, it is an important question as to which social equation the decision to put forward a Muslim face will affect. 13. 17% Thakurs in Zamania, trust shown in Javed Iqbal Javed Iqbal Ansari has been made in-charge of the Zamania assembly seat in Ghazipur. He comes from the Muslim community. The population of Muslim voters here is about 12%. In Zamania, Thakurs are 17%, Yadavs 14%, Jatavs 13%, Bhumihars 11%, Brahmins 9%, and Kushwahas 8%. From this seat, MLAs from the Yadav community have been elected the most, 4 times. Besides this, MLAs from the Thakur and Dalit communities have also been elected once each. In such a situation, it will be interesting to see which party's equations will be affected by bringing forward a Muslim face. 14. Bet on Kunj Bihari, with 14% Lodhi and 11% Yadav population in Babina Kunj Bihari Yadav has been made in-charge of the Babina assembly seat in Jhansi. He comes from the OBC category. The population of Yadav voters on this seat is about 11%. In Babina, Lodhi are 14%, Kushwaha 12%, and Yadav and Ahirwar/Jatav (SC) are 11-11%. Meanwhile, Brahmins are 8% and Baniyas are 5%. From this seat, MLAs from the Ahirwar/Jatav (SC) community have been elected 5 times. Additionally, MLAs from the Thakur community have been elected 2 times, and from the Lodhi community once. In such a scenario, what equation does the Azad Samaj Party want to achieve by fielding a Yadav face? This is an important question. Following SP's formula, Chandrashekhar fielded Dalit candidates on unreserved seats Chandrashekhar has copied SP's 2024 formula by fielding Dalit candidates on unreserved seats. It is being discussed that this time SP is preparing to field Dalit candidates on such non-reserved seats where the Dalit population holds decisive influence. Similarly, Chandrashekhar wants to cultivate the Dalit-Muslim equation by fielding candidates from the same community on Muslim-majority seats. Senior journalist Syed Qasim says - Muslims have been at the centre of Chandrashekhar's politics. The Nagina seat from which he is an MP has a 62 per cent Muslim population. Apart from Nagina, all his candidates could not even save their deposits. In the assembly elections, even Chandrashekhar himself could not save his deposit. In the by-elections, his party was certainly in third place on 2 seats, but then BSP was not in the fray. Therefore, it will be interesting to see how many Dalits will leave BSP and how many Muslims will leave SP to join Chandrashekhar in 2027.

stories.title: Officer's daughter turns conwoman to get rich:Pockets loan money; writes in diary, 'I will become a billionaire'
stories.summary: 'I, Garima Singh, will become a billionaire by April 2026. This is my goal. All my loans will be cleared from April to May. My target is to earn ₹100 crore from April to May. Garima Singh is a crorepati. Thank you, God.' These lines were written in a diary by Garima Singh, daughter of Gorakhpur's Station Superintendent. To fulfill her goal of becoming a crorepati, Garima defrauded more than 10 people of ₹1.67 crore in the name of arranging loans and getting them waived. On Monday, 3rd July, the police of Gorakhpur AIIMS station arrested Garima Singh and her father. The police have recovered a diary from Garima's possession. In it, she used to write daily about her goal of becoming a crorepati. Started fraud to fulfill the desire of becoming a millionaire Dhruv Narayan Singh, a resident of Mahadevi Jharkhandi Colony in AIIMS police station area, is a Railway Station Superintendent in Sahjanwan. He married his daughter Garima Singh to Bhanu Pratap Singh of Sukrauli, Kushinagar in the year 2020. Bhanu Pratap was a contractor. Garima has one son who is 3 years old and another who is 3 months old. When the contracting work weakened, Bhanu came to live with his wife at his father-in-law's house 2 years ago. Dhruv Narayan Singh said, " His daughter had a desire to become rich from the beginning. In this situation, she planned to commit fraud. For this, she read news articles, and read about people who commit fraud on the internet and YouTube. Then, she planned to commit fraud in the name of getting bank loans. She first made her own people victims. Then I also started helping my daughter. Those I knew in the railway, who had taken loans or who needed to take loans. I introduced all of them to my daughter.'' Police said that Garima Singh used to search for two types of people. First, those who needed loans. Second, those who had already taken loans. Garima Singh used to brainwash people to take loans. She would say, ‘You take the loan, I will pay the installments.' Whatever loan amount she got withdrawn from the bank, she would give 10-20 percent to the loan taker. She would get the remaining amount transferred to her own bank account. Now read how the case was uncovered On 1st August, Satyaprakash Singh, who works in the railway, reached AIIMS police station. He told the police that Dhruv Narayan Singh is a Station Superintendent like me. I had a car loan. Dhruv Narayan introduced me to his daughter, Garima. Garima told me that I would get your loan closed in a snap. For this, you will have to take a personal loan. That amount will have to be deposited in my account. I will pay its monthly EMI. Taking my documents, Garima got a total loan of ₹1.67 crore sanctioned from 6 banks - ICICI, HDFC, Yes Bank, SBI, SMFG and Bandhan Bank. She started saying that now I will repay the entire loan. I will also get your car loan waived. She sent about ₹10 lakh to my account as well. She said that this is your profit. Until your loan is not finished, I will keep paying the EMI. Paid EMI for 3 months, then backed out Satyaprakash said, ''Garima deposited the loan EMI for 3 months. Then I started getting calls from the bank. Then I contacted Garima. She would put me off every time. She said don't worry, everything will be done. When she didn't pay the EMI, then I filed a complaint against her.'' Police have registered a fraud case against Garima Singh, her father Dhruv Narayan Singh, husband Bhanu Pratap Singh, his associates Vishal Yadav, Rajendra Kumar, Chandraprakash, Dinkar Mani Tripathi and Sanjay Singh alias Jayprakash Singh. Police arrested father and daughter Garima Singh also defrauded railway employee Mohan Singh, Brahmanand Singh, Dr. Dilip Singh, Dr. Paramatma Singh, Sadhana Mall, Sugreev Singh and Sandeep Pandey. All of them have filed complaints at the CO office. AIIMS police station arrested a father and daughter on Monday. The police team is conducting raids in search of others. The police claim that the absconding accused will be arrested soon. SP City Nimish Patil said that complaints from more people are coming forward. In this case, the father and daughter have been arrested and sent to jail. Action will be taken after investigation in other cases as well.

stories.title: Will BJP bow to Brij Bhushan?:Dominates 25 seats and Rajput vote bank; what's next after acquittal in sexual harassment case?
stories.summary: First, read 2 statements 1. 'If any allegation against me is proven, I will hang myself.' May, 2023 2. 'I will definitely return once to the Lok Sabha from where I was removed with dishonor.' December, 2025 Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh made these statements after sexual harassment allegations were leveled against him and then his ticket was cut in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Now, the court has acquitted him of all charges. In this situation, Brij Bhushan's influence in UP and the BJP has increased once again. Now the questions are Which direction will Brij Bhushan's political career go? How did one decision change the political equations of UP? How beneficial is Brij Bhushan for the BJP in UP elections? We will know in today's UP Explainer Question-1: Will the party Brij Bhushan joins benefit in the elections? Answer: Yes, Brij Bhushan's political significance is not limited to one seat or district. Over the past three decades, he has built such a network across the entire Devipatan division and surrounding districts that transcends BJP and caste boundaries. This is why he is counted among the most influential leaders of eastern UP, beyond the party. stories.title: Ban on Kamil-Fazil degrees approved:Yogi cabinet clears proposal; Jewar airport to be linked with Ganga expressway
stories.summary: A cabinet meeting was held on Tuesday at Lok Bhawan under the chairmanship of CM Yogi Adityanath. Many major decisions were approved in it. 'Kamil' (graduate) and 'Fazil' (postgraduate) degrees will not be awarded in madrasas. A new expressway will be built to connect Jewar Airport with the Ganga Expressway. Now, workers will have to be paid double overtime for working more than the stipulated time. Also, at least 50% of the employees' total salary will be basic salary. This will stop the system of paying salaries in the name of allowances. Deep Tech Hubs (U-Hubs) will be built in Lucknow and Noida. The crop insurance scheme for farmers will also continue next year. The government says that these decisions will benefit education, employment, technology, roads, and farmers. Key decisions of Yogi Cabinet- No graduate and postgraduate degrees to be awarded in madrasas The Cabinet has approved an amendment to the UP Madrasa Education Council Act, 2004. Following this, 'Kamil' (graduate) and 'Fazil' (postgraduate) degrees will not be awarded in madrasas. This change is being made in accordance with the Supreme Court's decision of November 5, 2024. The court had deemed the provisions related to these two degrees unconstitutional. U-hubs to be built in Lucknow and Noida The government will establish U-hubs (Deep Tech Hubs) in Lucknow and Noida. Here, research will be conducted on new technologies like AI, Quantum Technology, Semiconductors, and Biotech. Startups and investment will also be promoted. In the first phase, centers will be built in both cities across 25,000 square feet each. Double overtime for working beyond prescribed hours The Cabinet has approved the Uttar Pradesh Wage Rules-2026. Under this, laborers will receive double overtime for working beyond the prescribed hours. Additionally, it will be mandatory to keep 50% of employees' salaries as basic pay. This will provide laborers with greater benefits from PF and other facilities. New development authority for Prayagraj-Chitrakoot The government will establish a new regional development authority by combining Prayagraj, Chitrakoot, Fatehpur, Banda, Kaushambi, and Hamirpur. This aims to promote planned development, better roads, and new employment opportunities in these districts. Development board to be formed for nomadic communities The Uttar Pradesh Nomadic Development Board will be formed for the development of denotified, nomadic, and semi-nomadic communities. This board will survey these communities, prepare their records, and help them avail the benefits of government schemes. Scope of Vishwakarma Shram Samman Yojana expanded The government has added 14 new trades to the scheme. Now, a total of 25 trades will be included in the scheme. Those undergoing training will receive a loan of up to 10 lakh rupees, 15% subsidy, and a modern toolkit. There will be a provision to disburse the loan within 15 days of bank approval. New expressway to be built up to Jewar airport A 74.46 km long greenfield expressway will be built in Bulandshahr to connect Jewar Airport with the Ganga Expressway. It will be six-lane, which can be expanded to eight lanes in the future. Approximately Rs 8,585 crore will be spent on this project. Agreement with HCL foundation for 5 more years The agreement with HCL Foundation for the 'Samuday' project running in Hardoi district has been extended for the next five years. Under this project, work related to education, health, agriculture, livelihood, and sanitation is being carried out. Crop insurance scheme to continue The government has decided to continue implementing the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) and Weather-Based Crop Insurance Scheme in the year 2026-27 as well. Farmers will pay 2% premium for Kharif crops and 1.5% for Rabi crops. The remaining amount will be jointly contributed by the central and state governments.
