stories.title: Mayawati expels nephew’s father-in-law:BSP supremo sacks Ashok Siddharth after repeated warnings, rules out any return
stories.summary: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) supremo Mayawati has expelled Ashok Siddharth—the father-in-law of her nephew Akash Anand—from the party. Speaking on Sunday, the BSP chief stated that Siddharth had failed to mend his ways despite repeated warnings, adding that he would never be readmitted into the party ranks. In a sweeping organisational crackdown, Mayawati also expelled Randhir Singh Beniwal. Beniwal served as a BSP national co-ordinator and oversaw party affairs across Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, and Jammu Kashmir. Second Expulsion in 18 Months This marks the second time in 18 months that Mayawati has expelled Ashok Siddharth. He was previously ousted on 12 February 2025 over allegations of factionalism, before being reinstated six months later in September 2025. Siddharth previously held charge of BSP operations across Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, and Delhi. Mayawati had stripped him of these state responsibilities on Saturday, triggering media speculation that he might be reassigned to lead party affairs in Uttar Pradesh. Accusations of Misinformation Trigger Final Ouster Addressing the reports on Sunday, Mayawati posted on X (formerly Twitter) to clarify that Siddharth was stripped of his duties due to unreformable behaviour. She accused him of orchestrating a conspiracy to mislead party workers by leaking false reports about a potential return to Uttar Pradesh politics, stating that this breach of discipline necessitated his permanent expulsion. Ramji Gautam Promoted; Cadres Warned Against Saboteurs Following the expulsion of Ashok Siddharth and Randhir Singh Beniwal, BSP supremo Mayawati has reappointed Rajya Sabha MP Ramji Gautam as the party's in-charge for Punjab. He will hold the position through the upcoming Punjab Assembly and Lok Sabha elections. In a further realignment of state responsibilities, Madhya Pradesh in-charge Rajaram has been handed additional oversight of Delhi, Kerala, Gujarat, and Karnataka. Mayawati Enforces Strict Structural Boundaries Clarifying party policy on executive roles, Mayawati stated that party office-bearers or co-ordinators hailing from Uttar Pradesh who hold key responsibilities outside the state will strictly not be assigned any organisational duties within UP. Concurrently, the party has stripped Nitin Singh—a close associate of Ashok Siddharth who served as his deputy across three states—of his responsibilities in Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu. Call to Safeguard Majority Ambitions Reissuing a stern warning to rank-and-file workers, Mayawati urged party cadres to remain vigilant against malicious elements and conspirators. She noted that such individuals are actively working to undermine the BSP's campaign to form a full-majority government. Prior Expulsions for Factionalism and Indiscipline Last year, in 2025, BSP supremo Mayawati had similarly ousted Ashok Siddharth and his close confidant, Nitin Singh, over allegations of fostering factionalism within the party structure. At the time, Mayawati publicly accused both leaders of orchestrating anti-party conspiracies. The internal crackdown escalated on 2 March when Mayawati stripped her nephew, Akash Anand, of his official post, before expelling him from the party the following day. However, following a formal apology, Akash was reinstated into the party fold on 13 April. Ashok Siddharth was subsequently readmitted six months later. Demonstrating a rapid return to influence, he was placed at the very top of the national office-bearers' list in February 2026, before his latest and final expulsion. Only Mayawati Has Authority to Finalise Candidates BSP supremo Mayawati had explicitly clarified that the absolute authority to select election candidates rests solely with her. She emphasised that Akash Anand and other senior leaders only announce candidates' names at cadre conventions, acting strictly on her directives. In line with this protocol, Akash Anand is scheduled to visit Hathras on 10 August to formally announce the BSP candidate. Strict Oversight Imposed on Akash Anand Clarifying Akash Anand's operational role within the organisation, Mayawati laid down two binding conditions: Nationwide Review Meetings Subject to Full Reporting: While Akash Anand is tasked with conducting review meetings across the country, Mayawati must be kept fully informed of every movement. State in-charges have been directed to send detailed progress reports directly to Lucknow or Delhi. Prior Clearance Mandatory for UP Programmes: Should Akash Anand plan any tour or public programme within Uttar Pradesh, both he and the attending party co-ordinators must obtain explicit prior approval from Mayawati. Ashok Siddharth: The eye surgeon who turned politician Born on 5 January 1965, Dr Ashok Siddharth is an ophthalmologist by profession, holding a diploma in eye diseases from Maharani Laxmi Bai Medical College. During his tenure in government medical service, he actively served as an assembly, district, and zonal president within BAMCEF. In 2007, while posted at the Gursahaiganj Primary Health Centre in Kannauj, he resigned from public service to join the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP). He served as a Member of the Legislative Council (MLC) on a BSP ticket twice—first in 2009 and again in 2016—before being elected to the Rajya Sabha in 2016, where he served until 2022. Within the BSP, he held prominent organisational roles, including Kanpur-Agra zonal co-ordinator. In addition to serving as BSP National Secretary, Siddharth held state charge across five key regions, including Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Kerala. His wife, Sunita Siddharth, served as the Vice-Chairperson of the Uttar Pradesh Women’s Commission from 2007 to 2012. Known as a low-profile strategist, Siddharth historically operated as a key behind-the-scenes operative within the party. Randhir Singh Beniwal: Sacked Months After High-Level Appointment Hailing from Saharanpur district, Randhir Singh Beniwal is a prominent leader from the Jat community who joined the BSP in 1990. stories.title: Fourth-grade boy beaten to death in Gorakhpur:Child waylaid by 8 to 9 youths while he was on his way to uncle's shop
stories.summary: Nine-year-old Saras Singh, who was injured in a fight that took place on Saturday night at Bela intersection in Pipraich police station area of Gorakhpur, died during treatment. His 15-year-old maternal cousin, Shivkumar, is seriously injured and is undergoing treatment at BRD Medical College, Gorakhpur. After the incident, there is an atmosphere of grief and anger in Madhopur village. Family members have raised questions, accusing the police of not taking timely action. According to information, Raju Singh, a resident of Madhopur village, had filed a complaint at Pipraich police station about a month ago against some people, accusing them of molesting his daughter. Family members allege that after the complaint, the accused party was angry, and due to this, tension persisted between both sides. Family members say that if the police had taken effective action in the molestation case in a timely manner, perhaps the incident that occurred on Saturday night could have been avoided. However, the police are investigating the matter and all allegations are being probed. Attacked by surrounding them at Bela intersection It is reported that around 9 PM on Saturday night, Raju Singh's 15-year-old son Shivkumar and his brother-in-law Arvind Singh's 9-year-old son Saras Singh were going towards Bela intersection. Saras Singh used to live and study at his aunt's house in Madhopur after his mother's death. It is alleged that during this time, some residents of Kewatan Tola, Madhopur, surrounded both children. After this, they attacked both with sticks, iron rods, and bricks/stones. In the attack, both teenagers were seriously injured and fell on the road. Upon receiving information about the assault, nearby people reached the spot, after which the attackers fled from there. Local people informed the police and family members about the incident. Death during treatment at Medical College After the incident, both injured children were taken to Community Health Centre Pipraich. Seeing their serious condition, doctors referred them to BRD Medical College Gorakhpur. According to family members, 9-year-old Saras Singh died during treatment around 2 AM. Meanwhile, Shivkumar's condition remains serious. He is being treated under supervision at the medical college. As soon as the news of Saras's death was received, there was an uproar in the family. Family members are in a bad state, crying inconsolably. Mourning has also spread throughout the village. The deceased's family members alleged that despite informing the police about the incident, the police arrived late at the scene. They say that instead of taking immediate action, the police tried to calm the matter down and facilitate a compromise. Family members alleged that if the police had taken the ongoing dispute seriously and acted on time, this incident would not have happened. However, police officials say that a fair investigation of the matter is being conducted and no culprit will be spared. Police engaged in search for accused After the incident, the police have intensified the investigation of the case. Following the death of the minor, preparations are being made to add necessary sections to the case. Police are raiding potential hideouts to arrest the accused. Considering the tension in the village, police forces have been deployed. Officials have appealed to the villagers to maintain peace. Pipraich Station House Officer Vivek Trivedi stated that all aspects related to the incident are being investigated. Further action will be taken based on the medical report, statements of eyewitnesses, and other evidence. He said that if the investigation confirms the minor's death due to the attack, then relevant sections will be added to the case, and strict action will be taken against the accused.

stories.title: 17-year-old girl sexually exploited in Gorakhpur:Youth arrested for luring victim to room with marriage promise, fled after she became pregnant
stories.summary: A case has come to light in the Gulriha police station area of Gorakhpur where a 17-year-old minor girl was raped on the pretext of marriage. During physical relations, the minor became pregnant. As soon as this information was received, the accused fled. Based on the complaint filed by the victim's mother, Gulriha police have registered an FIR against the accused youth and arrested him. Details of the case According to police, a 17-year-old minor girl living in a village in the area has alleged that Vinay, a resident of Jungle Ekla Number-Two, Tola Hatwa, trapped her in a love trap and promised to marry her. After this, the accused had physical relations with the victim several times. Following this, the victim became pregnant. The victim alleges that upon learning about the pregnancy, the accused switched off his mobile phone and broke contact with her. After this, the minor told the entire incident to her mother. On Saturday, the mother reached Gulriha police station with her daughter and filed a complaint against the accused. CO Gorakhnath Ravi Singh informed that based on the complaint, an FIR has been registered against the accused under relevant sections and the POCSO Act. The accused has been taken into custody and is being interrogated.

stories.title: 57 UP districts on rain alert:10-foot snake enters kitchen in Lakhimpur, 6 Bijnor villages flooded as bullock carts wade through waist-deep water
stories.summary: Monsoon activity is set to pick up pace again in Uttar Pradesh starting today (Sunday). Over 30 districts, including Lucknow, Kanpur, and Gorakhpur, are witnessing overcast skies alongside gentle breeze. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for 57 districts, warning of heavy rainfall in Gorakhpur and eight surrounding districts. Meanwhile, heavy relentless rainfall in the hilly region has pushed 10 rivers in UP — including the Ganga, Ghaghra, and Saryu — above the danger mark. In Lakhimpur Kheri, a 10-foot-long Russell's Viper slithered into the kitchen of a home on Saturday morning at around 11:00 AM. Following an alert, a Forest Department team reached the spot and safely rescued the venomous snake. In Bijnor, the swollen Ganga River has inundated six villages, leaving 12 others completely marooned like islands. Water levels on roads have reached up to 3 feet to 4 feet, forcing villagers to wade through waist-deep water using tractors and bullock carts. Floodwaters are also flowing over the state highway near the Ganga bridge. Similarly, in Varanasi, the rising Ganga has submerged the steps of several key ghats, with floodwaters entering 50 to 60 temples. Prior to this, 29 districts recorded rainfall on Saturday, with Mirzapur receiving the highest precipitation at 13 mm. Atul Kumar Singh, a meteorologist based in Lucknow, stated: "Over the next 24 hours, the monsoon trough will rapidly shift towards Uttar Pradesh, triggering an increase in monsoon activity across the state. Light rainfall is expected across most parts of the state, except for seven to eight districts. Heavier rainfall is set to begin tomorrow, with widespread, intense downpours likely across the entire state until August 6–7.

stories.title: 'I want my soul to keep wandering':Bodybuilder shoots himself dead in Saharanpur after writing, 'Don't let my wife touch my body'
stories.summary: A 52-year-old degree college clerk died by suicide in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur district on Saturday evening after shooting himself with a homemade firearm at his residence. The victim, identified as Devdutt Sharma—who was also a bodybuilder—took the extreme step at around 7:00 PM at his home located within the Sarsawa police station limits, approximately 30 kilometres from the city centre. Hearing the gunshot, Devdutt's wife rushed to the spot and found him lying in a pool of blood. He was immediately rushed to a medical college hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Before committing suicide, Sharma sent a lengthy WhatsApp message to his niece explaining his actions. "I can no longer tolerate the humiliation," the message read. "It is better to die once than to die every day. I am not a coward, but this humiliation has killed my soul from within. Do not let my wife touch my body." In his final note, Sharma also outlined specific instructions regarding his last rites, expressing a desire for his soul to remain restless. "Do not use cow dung cakes for my cremation, nor spend much money on it. No religious ceremonies should be performed for the peace of my soul; I want my soul to keep wandering. Take care of your mother," he wrote. Local police have launched an investigation into the matter. Family background Devdutt was a resident of Railway Road. His parents passed away several years ago. He was the elder of two siblings; his sister, Rajni (45), was married to Saharanpur resident Sachin Sharma, who passed away three years ago. It was to Sachin's 21-year-old daughter, Neha Sharma, that Devdutt sent the message prior to committing suicide. Devdutt married Seema Rani (49) 33 years ago. Apart from his wife, he is survived by two sons. The elder son, Abhishek, works in Dubai, while the younger son, Aditya, is studying forensics in Chandigarh. Aditya is also a powerlifter who recently won a gold medal in Dehradun by lifting 135 kg in the 74 kg category. Ran gym for 26 years alongside clerical job Devdutt had been running a facility named 'Rock Gym' behind his house since the year 2000. For the past two years, he was also employed as a clerk at Balaji Group of College in the city on a monthly salary of ₹17,000. He would manage the gym after returning from his college duties. Previously, Devdutt had also worked at Tilak Ram Saini Girls College and Elamchand Saini Girls College. Watch 3 reels of Devdutt below: Neighbours rushed after wife raised alarm A neighbour, Sushil, stated that Devdutt Sharma had gone to the gym on Saturday evening. According to his wife, Devdutt returned home from the gym around 7:00 PM and shot himself point-blank with a firearm. "His wife, Seema, came screaming into the gym," Sushil said. "I rushed inside and found Devdutt lying on the floor with a gunshot wound and a firearm lying next to him. We then took him to the hospital in a car, where he died." Following information about the incident, Station House Officer (SHO) Pravesh Kumar Sharma arrived at the scene alongside a police contingent and a forensic team. The forensic experts collected evidence from the spot, while officers questioned residents. Providing details on the matter, Circle Officer Pawan Kumar stated: "Prima facie, it appears to be a case of suicide. Investigations revealed a suicide note sent by the deceased to a relative, which is currently being verified. The victim's wife and family members will be questioned, and further legal action will be taken based on the findings of the complete probe."

stories.title: 6 UP students die by suicide after NEET paper leak:CJP seeks ₹1 crore compensation, families say no one contacted them so far
stories.summary: Three months after the NEET paper leak, families of six students in Uttar Pradesh who died after the exam controversy say neither the government nor protest organisers have contacted them, despite a public assurance of compensation. On 3 May, after the NEET paper leak, 24 students across India reportedly died by suicide. Six of them were from Uttar Pradesh. Their families claim the students were under severe stress due to the paper leak and the re-examination. A 35-day protest was held at Delhi's Jantar Mantar. Following activist Sonam Wangchuk's fast and demonstrations by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned. Among the demands on which the CJP ended its protest was compensation of ₹1 crore for the families of students who had died. The Centre reportedly agreed in principle. However, when Dainik Bhaskar contacted the six affected families in Uttar Pradesh, all said that no government official or CJP representative had approached them. Read the pain of these 6 families from UP in Sunday Big Story... Hamirpur: Shruti Sahu, 20 Shruti had been preparing for NEET in Kota for the past two years and appeared for the exam for the second time. Her father, Mahendra Pal, said she had performed well in the original exam. After the paper leak, she returned home and appeared for the re-examination on 21 June from Hamirpur after getting her centre changed. After the second exam, Shruti said the paper was tougher than the first. Based on the answer key, she expected around 550 marks, but her result was much lower. Her family said she became deeply distressed afterwards and, despite their efforts to support her, she died on 18 July. Mahendra said Shruti was the eldest of four siblings. Her mother had died during the COVID-19 pandemic. Has anyone contacted the family? Her father said only the police visited. No other official or organisation has contacted them. Maharajganj: Chanchali Bharti Chanchali was the only sister among two brothers. Her elder brother is a doctor, and she wanted to follow the same career. Her father, farmer Amarjeet, said she appeared for the re-exam on 21 June and seemed happy afterwards, saying the paper had gone well. The following day, after returning from the fields, he later learnt that she had died. A note addressed to her brother said, "Forgive me, brother. I won't be able to do it." Has anyone contacted the family? The family said neither district officials nor any social organisation had approached them. Ghaziabad: Jatin, 22 22-year-old Jatin had been preparing for the NEET medical entrance exam for several years. Two days before the re-examination, on June 19, he died by suicide. Police recovered a one-minute video from his mobile phone in which he said he was taking the step of his own free will because he had lost all attachment to life. Jatin's father, Rajesh Kumar, is posted as an Inspector in the Food Department in Saharanpur. His mother and younger sister live in Ghaziabad. According to the family, he was never under any pressure from them regarding his studies. Did anyone contact the family? Rajesh Kumar said they had not received any information about compensation and that no one had visited their home. Sitapur: Hrithik, 21 Twenty-one-year-old Ritik had appeared for NEET for the third time. His father, Anoop Mishra, runs a brick kiln, while his mother is a homemaker. Anoop said Ritik was happy after the exam and was confident he would secure admission this time. However, after the paper leak led to the exam being cancelled, he became deeply distressed. The uncertainty over the leak and the re-examination weighed heavily on him. On May 15, he died by suicide. Has anyone contacted the family? His father said no one had reached out to them. Azamgarh: Srishti Yadav, 18 Srishti studied at a military school in Bihar and had returned to her home in Azamgarh about three months before NEET. Her father had died during the COVID-19 pandemic, and her mother Asha Devi is a government school teacher. The family said she became distressed after seeing the re-exam cut-off and later died. Has anyone contacted the family? Her mother has been unwell, and the family said no official had visited them. Shivani Yadav, 17 Shivani had appeared for NEET for the first time after completing Class 12. Her father Ranjeet Kumar said she was happy with her performance but became deeply upset after the exam was cancelled due to the paper leak. She died on 16 June. Has anyone contacted the family? Her father said no one had come to meet or support the family. Shivani had scored excellent marks in her ISC Class 12 examinations earlier this year. Now know what the families of the deceased children said Father said- Government's failure snatched away my daughter Shruti Sahu's father Mahendra from Hamirpur is devastated by his daughter's death. He says, "My wife passed away during the Covid pandemic. After that, I had to take care of the family on my own. Shruti was the eldest of my four children. She was brilliant in studies and was confident of clearing NEET. But when the exam was cancelled, she was completely shattered. She appeared for the re-exam, but the stress became unbearable. After returning home, she died by suicide." Mahendra says, "My daughter's life was lost because of the government's failure. The government should understand that a child works hard for an entire year to prepare for an exam. When a paper leak happens, it breaks them completely. No one from the administration has contacted me so far. After losing my daughter, our family is completely shattered." Apart from Shruti, Mahendra has two daughters, Jagriti and Kavya, and a son, Tarun. Neither the government nor the Cockroach Party contacted us Amarjit, the father of Chanchali Bharti from Maharajganj, says he is heartbroken by his daughter's death. When asked whether the administration had spoken to him about compensation, or whether anyone from the Cockroach Party had contacted the family, he said, "More than a week has passed since my daughter's death, but no one has contacted us. No one has spoken to our family." We also spoke to Rajan, the cousin of Srishti Yadav from Azamgarh. He said, "We did not take part in the protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, but we were closely following all the developments. After Srishti's death, neither the Cockroach Party nor any official from the district administration contacted us." After that, we spoke one by one to the families of all six deceased students. Every family gave the same response — neither the government nor the local administration has contacted them regarding compensation. Chanchali's mother breaks down repeatedly every time she looks at her daughter's photograph. Protest ended on promise of compensation Following the NEET paper leak, the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) staged a protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar for nearly 35 days. The party's spokespersons, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, held three rounds of talks with the Central government. During the discussions, the party placed three key demands: Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on July 24. Health Minister JP Nadda, speaking on behalf of the government, assured the protesters that no action would be taken against them. The government also agreed in principle to provide compensation. However, it did not clearly state whether the amount would be ₹1 crore. Cockroach Party chief Abhijit Deepak, spokesperson Saurabh Das and Ashutosh Ranka have also not clarified when the compensation will be paid.

stories.title: WATCH | Constable carries gym-themed Kanwar:Devotees arrive with supercar-inspired Kanwars, some on foot
stories.summary: The Kanwar Yatra is in full swing across Uttar Pradesh, with roads filled with devotees carrying Kanwars of all shapes and sizes. While some are drawing attention with supercar-themed Kanwars reportedly worth ₹8 lakh, others are undertaking the pilgrimage on foot with their daughters seated on the Kanwar. In Shamli, a group of Shiva devotees from Haryana arrived carrying a 13-foot-tall Kanwar. Meanwhile, five-year-old Ritik and 12-year-old Abhishek have also become a major attraction for their devotion during the yatra. A devotee, Bobby Yadav, is walking with a Kanwar carrying 201 litres of Ganga water to offer Jalabhishek to Lord Shiva. He said he is making the pilgrimage with the wish that Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav becomes Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister again. Watch the colourful Kanwar Yatra across Uttar Pradesh in the video.

stories.title: UP polls to see 12 parties from five states:Owaisi, Chandrashekhar and Pallavi could alter poll equations; decoding smaller parties' strategy
stories.summary: As many as 12 regional parties from five states are preparing to contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. From Bihar's JD(U), LJP and VIP to Maharashtra's Shiv Sena (UBT) and NCP (SP), several parties from outside the state are looking to test their political strength in UP. The BJP could face a challenge not only from parties from other states but also from emerging regional players within Uttar Pradesh. Leaders such as Chandrashekhar Azad, Pallavi Patel and Swami Prasad Maurya are also preparing to create new political equations. Small parties can change results in close contests Every election sees several smaller parties entering the fray with influence among specific communities or in particular districts. While these parties may win only a few seats, they can affect the outcome of several constituencies by securing even 1,000-2,000 votes. Political analyst Prof. Sanjay Kumar says major parties sometimes use smaller parties to their advantage. According to him, large parties may encourage smaller outfits to field candidates capable of dividing the opposition's vote. By cutting into the vote share of the main contenders, these parties can alter the victory margin and ultimately determine the winner. Owaisi eyes around 200 muslim-dominated seats Asaduddin Owaisi's All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) is preparing to contest around 200 Muslim-dominated constituencies in Uttar Pradesh. Owaisi has already addressed rallies in Bahraich, Bijnor and Saharanpur, districts where Muslim and Dalit voters form a significant part of the electorate. By promoting the slogan "Jai Bhim, Jai Meem," AIMIM could challenge the Samajwadi Party's traditional electoral arithmetic in these areas. In the 2022 UP Assembly elections, AIMIM secured between 14,000 and 36,000 votes in five constituencies—Mubarakpur, Sambhal, Firozabad, Khadda and Kundarki. The party's presence was also cited as a factor in close contests on seven seats—Aurai, Bijnor, Sultanpur, Moradabad Nagar, Shahganj, Nakur and Kursi, where the SP lost by relatively narrow margins. Chandrashekhar focuses on 18 Dalit-Muslim dominated seats Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad's Azad Samaj Party is preparing to contest all 403 Assembly seats in Uttar Pradesh. However, its primary focus is on around 18 Dalit-Muslim dominated constituencies in western UP. These include Nagina, Najibabad, Dhampur, Chandpur, Barhapur, Behat, Deoband, Gangoh, Rampur Maniharan, Saharanpur Rural, Kairana, Thana Bhawan, Purqazi, Meerapur, Hastinapur, Kithore, Moradabad Rural and Kundarki. Chandrashekhar himself could contest from the reserved Hastinapur seat. His party is looking to benefit from the weakening of the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) in western Uttar Pradesh. Pallavi Patel looks to build her own political base The political legacy of Apna Dal founder Dr Sonelal Patel has put his daughters, Anupriya Patel and Pallavi Patel, on opposite political paths. Anupriya Patel allied with the BJP in 2014 and subsequently helped Apna Dal emerge as the third-largest party in the UP Assembly in terms of MLAs. Pallavi Patel is now attempting to expand her own political influence. Her party, Apna Dal (Kamerawadi), is looking at around 12-15 seats across Pratapgarh, Jaunpur, Varanasi, Mirzapur and Sonbhadra, including Sirathu. It remains to be seen whether Pallavi Patel will contest the 2027 polls with the Samajwadi Party or again align with Owaisi and Swami Prasad Maurya, as she did in 2024. If she contests independently, political observers expect the Kurmi vote to fragment, potentially affecting the outcome in several constituencies. Raja Bhaiya plans candidates on all 403 seats Raja Bhaiya, chief of Jansatta Dal Loktantrik, is also preparing to field candidates across all 403 Assembly constituencies. His strongest influence is considered to be in Pratapgarh and adjoining areas. His political positioning and influence among Thakur voters could potentially impact the BJP's electoral prospects in some constituencies. Other smaller parties that could impact UP's electoral equations Peace Party Led by Dr Ayub Ansari, the Peace Party is considered influential in around 20 constituencies across Gorakhpur, Basti, Sant Kabir Nagar, Siddharthnagar and Mau. The party won four seats in the 2012 Assembly elections. Apni Janata Party Led by Swami Prasad Maurya, the party is considered to have influence in around four to five constituencies in Kushinagar, Deoria and Rae Bareli. Mahan Dal Led by Keshav Dev Maurya, Mahan Dal has influence in Shakya-dominated constituencies across western and central Uttar Pradesh. In the previous election, the Samajwadi Party allotted the party two seats under an alliance arrangement. Rashtriya Ulama Council Led by Maulana Aamir Rashadi Madni, the party has influence in Azamgarh and surrounding Muslim-dominated districts. Janwadi Party (Socialist) Led by Sanjay Chauhan, the party has influence in four to five districts of eastern Uttar Pradesh. Members of the Nonia community form its core voter base. The Samajwadi Party had allotted it one seat under an alliance in the previous election. Rashtriya Adhikar Morcha (RAM) The party was formed by Alankar Agnihotri, who resigned as Bareilly City Magistrate amid controversies surrounding alleged disrespect to a Shankaracharya and the "choti" controversy. For the 2027 elections, the party plans to field candidates in Brahmin-dominated constituencies. The bigger question: Who will benefit from the vote split? With national parties, established regional players and a growing number of smaller caste- and community-based outfits preparing for the 2027 UP Assembly elections, the contest could become increasingly fragmented. For smaller parties, winning a large number of seats may not be the immediate objective. Their ability to cut into the vote share of larger parties and influence close contests could itself give them considerable political relevance.

stories.title: Lover hacks girlfriend’s husband with 17 strikes:Came to take wife home, accused attacked him with blade
stories.summary: In Muzaffarnagar, on Saturday at 7 am, a lover hacked his girlfriend's husband to death with a chopper. The accused attacked the young man 17 times with a chopper in 16 seconds. After that, he fled from the scene. Nearby people informed the wife about the incident. With the help of people, the wife took her husband to the hospital. Due to his critical condition, doctors referred him to Meerut, where he died during treatment. The incident took place in the Budhana area. Police investigation revealed that the husband had come to his in-laws' house to pick up his wife. The deceased was a resident of Meerut. He had come to his in-laws' house in Nai Basti, Budhana, on August 4. He used to work in Surat. He was also going to take his wife to Surat. It was over this matter that he argued with his wife's lover. Watch 3 footages of the attack Lover seen roaming with a chopper in hand A video related to this incident has also surfaced. In which it can be seen, the lover is seen roaming in the street with a chopper in his hand. The husband is also seen coming behind him. After this, the lover runs towards the husband. A fight breaks out between the two. During the fight, the husband falls into a drain. After this, the lover continuously attacks the husband with the chopper. Wife's Affair After Marriage According to the police, Talib was married to Meena, a resident of Nai Basti in Budhana, 7 years ago. They also have two children. Talib was a resident of Meerut. After marriage, he started living with his wife in a rented room in Budhana. He worked in Surat. He used to visit Budhana occasionally. Meanwhile, Meena had an affair with Hashim, who lived in Nai Basti. Hashim used to frequent Meena's house. Talib became aware of this. Since then, there have been several disputes between Talib and Hashim. Talib also started living in Budhana for most of the time. He used to go to Surat sometimes. When Talib came to Budhana on August 4, he asked his wife Meena to come to Surat as well. Meena told this to her lover. Hashim did not want Meena to go to Surat because of this, Hashim and Talib started arguing on the morning of August 8. After this, Hashim murdered Talib. Accused will be arrested soon, says Budhana Town In-charge Budhana Town In-charge Lalit Kasana stated that in the preliminary investigation, the reason for the murder has been revealed to be an illicit relationship. There was a dispute between the husband and the lover over this matter. People from the vicinity have been interrogated. Police teams have been formed for the arrest of the accused. Raids are being conducted at possible hideouts.

stories.title: Man tied up and beaten for meeting married girlfriend:Thrashed with sticks, women hit him with slippers; girlfriend also beaten
stories.summary: In Kanpur Dehat, a lover who went to meet his married girlfriend was severely beaten by people. First, he was tied with a rope and beaten, then laid on the ground and hit 20-25 times with a stick on his soles. The women of the house hit him with slippers. The girlfriend, who came to save her lover, was also beaten. The incident took place on Friday morning in Khirwan Dera village, Derapur police station area, about 25 km from the district headquarters. The young man had arrived late on Thursday night to meet her. When the neighbours found out, they locked the house from outside in the morning. A video of the lover and his married girlfriend being beaten has also surfaced. On the information of the villagers, the police arrested the lover. See pictures Know the full story... Pawan (25), a resident of Khirwan Dera village, works as a labourer. He belongs to the Banjara community. On Thursday night, he went to meet a married woman from the village at her house. In the morning, when neighbours found out, they latched the door from the outside. The frightened woman hid Pawan in the wardrobe of the room. The woman's in-laws had gone to work in the fields. Upon returning home, they started searching for the young man, but he was not found. After searching for about three hours, they opened the wardrobe and found Pawan hidden inside. The in-laws pulled Pawan out and severely beat him. After that, they tied his hands and feet with a rope in the courtyard. He was made to lie on the ground and beaten on the soles of his feet with sticks. The women of the house also hit him with slippers. When the woman tried to save Pawan, her in-laws also assaulted her. After beating him for a long time, the in-laws handed the young man over to the police. The police took him to the station and conducted a medical examination. After this, he was challaned for disturbing the peace and released. Love marriage six years ago The woman had a love marriage about six years ago with Shankar, who lives in the same village. She has two children. It is being reported that for the past two months, the woman's closeness with Pawan had increased. Both are from the Banjara community.

stories.title: Govt teacher kills wife, flees after stabbing her at home:Father alleges affair with another woman
stories.summary: A government teacher murdered his wife by stabbing her with a knife in Fatehpur, UP. After the incident, he fled from the scene. On Saturday at 9 am, there was a dispute between the two over some matter. It escalated so much that it led to physical violence. The husband brought a knife from the kitchen in anger. He attacked his wife repeatedly. The wife fell to the ground covered in blood. When people nearby heard the screams and arrived, the husband had already fled. Police who arrived after being informed took the woman to a nearby hospital. There, doctors declared Shalini Yadav (29) dead. The incident occurred in the Nasirpir locality of the Kotwali area. Police are searching for the accused husband, Dilip Kumar Yadav. Husband and wife lived in a rented house The accused husband Dilip Yadav is an assistant teacher at the primary school in Chak Alipur. He lives in a rented house in the Nasirpir area. On Saturday, he did not go to school. Shailini's father, Dharam Singh Yadav, who reached the spot, said, "My son-in-law Dilip has murdered my daughter. The son-in-law was having an affair with another woman. They used to quarrel over this matter.''

stories.title: BJP announces new regional morcha in-charges:Ramesh Singh gets Kashi, Abhijat assigned Gorakhpur; Priyanka named ST Morcha vice-president
stories.summary: Ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the BJP is strengthening its organisational team with a fresh round of appointments. The party today (8 Aug) announced six new regional in-charges and seven front in-charges, assigning them responsibilities for the upcoming Assembly and Panchayat elections. State vice-president Ramesh Singh has been appointed in-charge of the Kashi region, associated with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, while state general secretary Abhijat Mishra will oversee the Gorakhpur region, the political base of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. State general secretary Dilip Patel has been given charge of the Awadh region, while state general secretary Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan will oversee the Western region. Geeta Shakya has been appointed in-charge of Braj, while Shankar Lodhi will handle Kanpur. Seven leaders assigned charge of party fronts State general secretary Rajesh Chaudhary has been appointed in-charge of the Youth Front, while state general secretary Sanjay Rai will oversee the Backward Classes Front. State vice-president Kameshwar Singh has been given charge of the Women’s Front, while state vice-president Dharmendra Singh will handle the Scheduled Caste Front. BJP state vice-president Priyanka Rawat has been appointed in-charge of the Scheduled Tribe Front, Shankar Giri will oversee the Farmers’ Front and Devesh Kori will handle the Minority Front. Govind Shukla gets charge of BJP headquarters Former state general secretary and MLC Govind Narayan Shukla has been appointed in-charge of the BJP state headquarters. He is the only former office-bearer to have been given responsibility at the state headquarters. His long experience in managing election campaigns, particularly during Assembly polls, is believed to have led to his appointment. Yatendra Sharma to oversee media department State minister Yatendra Sharma has been appointed in-charge of the BJP’s media department. Earlier, Manish Dixit was appointed as the department’s convener, while Devendra Pratap Singh was made the party’s chief spokesperson. Complete list of BJP's newly appointed office-bearers… Ramesh Singh gets bigger role despite no previous stint in state team The BJP has elevated state vice-president Ramesh Singh by appointing him in-charge of the Kashi region. Singh is considered close to a regional RSS functionary. The responsibility of regional in-charge is generally assigned to state general secretaries, making Singh’s appointment notable as he is a state vice-president. Despite holding a key organisational post now, Singh had not previously been part of the BJP’s state team. Regional in-charges to play key role in candidate selection The BJP has appointed one in-charge for each of Uttar Pradesh’s six regions to oversee organisational activities, campaigns and preparations for the upcoming Assembly elections. Regional in-charges are expected to play an important role in the selection of Assembly candidates. Their views are considered when panels of prospective candidates are discussed before the party finalises its nominees.

stories.title: Drone flies near Yogi’s stage, triggering police alert:Youth detained, probe underway; CM showers flowers on Kanwariyas in Meerut
stories.summary: A suspected drone was spotted near the stage where Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was attending an event in Meerut on Saturday, triggering a security alert. Police immediately seized the drone and detained the man who was allegedly operating it. Meerut SSP Avinash Pandey said the man claimed he was unaware of the rules governing drone operations. Police are checking his social media profiles and examining the footage recorded by the drone. Further action will be taken after a forensic examination, the SSP said. CM showers flowers on Kanwariyas Earlier, at around 12.30 pm, Adityanath showered flowers on Kanwariyas in Meerut. Standing on the stage, the Chief Minister showered petals on Shiva devotees carrying Kanwars as they moved forward chanting “Bol Bam” and “Har Har Mahadev”. Flowers were also showered from a helicopter during the event. The Kanwar Yatra has drawn large crowds across Uttar Pradesh during the month of Sawan. A large number of devotees have been seen on major Kanwar routes, including the Delhi-Dehradun Highway, since morning. Devotees carrying Kanwars and holy Ganga water have continued their journey towards their destinations. 70-year-old man cycles 100 km daily Among the pilgrims is 70-year-old Pramod Kumar from Delhi, who is carrying a Kanwar on his bicycle. Kumar said he had been travelling to Haridwar by bicycle to collect Ganga water for the past 10 years. He cycles around 100 km every day during the journey. In Muzaffarnagar, a Shiva devotee was seen undertaking the journey while wearing a blindfold. Ankit from Sonipat reached Shamli carrying a Kanwar decorated with 10 pigeons. 'Kanwar Yatra symbolises social and national unity' Adityanath welcomed the devotees taking part in the Kanwar Yatra and said the state government was fully prepared to ensure their safety and provide them with a warm welcome. He said devotees undertaking the journey on foot out of their faith in Lord Shiva represented devotion, dedication, social unity, social equality and national unity. The Chief Minister said the pilgrims were travelling beyond state boundaries and creating an atmosphere of enthusiasm and celebration. He added that flowers would continue to be showered on Kanwariyas for the next two days. Devotees from several states join the yatra Adityanath said a large crowd had gathered at Shiv Chowk in Muzaffarnagar and that he had the opportunity to shower flowers on devotees in Meerut. He said millions of Kanwariyas from Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan, Punjab and Himachal Pradesh, along with devotees from western Uttar Pradesh, were participating in the pilgrimage. Major religious sites along the route include Baba Augharnath Temple in Meerut, Baba Dudheshwar Nath Temple in Ghaziabad and Pura Mahadev Temple in Baghpat. Police continue drone investigation Police said a government-operated drone and another drone were flying during the Chief Minister's programme. The operator of the second drone was detained immediately. The man, who is from the Medical police station area, told police that he was unaware of the rules regarding drone operations. Police are examining his social media activity and the footage recorded by the drone. Further legal action will follow the forensic examination.

stories.title: Mayawati targets SP over PDA:Says it once meant backwards, now means Pandit; calls it opportunistic politics
stories.summary: Bahujan Samaj Party's national president Mayawati took a dig at SP chief Akhilesh Yadav. She said that Akhilesh, who earlier stated that the first 'P' in PDA meant 'Pichda' (backwards), is now interpreting 'P' as 'Pandit' (Brahmin) due to political self-interest. This is political opportunism. SP had organised a Brahmin conference on August 5, the birth anniversary of Janeshwar Mishra. In this, it had stated that the 'P' in 'PDA' meant 'Brahmin' and 'Peedit' (oppressed). BSP is also focusing on connecting Brahmins with the party this time. It has also declared several Brahmin candidates. The state has a Brahmin population of over 12 per cent. They have a decisive impact on more than 100 seats. This is why, before the elections, every party is organising various events to bring Brahmins into their fold. 'Earlier it was backward, now it's Pandit' BSP chief Mayawati, taking a dig on Saturday, said that SP had so far explained 'PDA' to mean Pichda (Backwards), Dalit, Alpasankhyak (Minority). But now, when the upper-caste society, especially the Brahmin community, is rapidly joining the BSP and the BSP is also giving them tickets, the SP has become nervous. For this reason, 'P' has now been changed to 'Pandit'. She said, "This is a living proof of their political deceit and trickery." 'BSP is for everyone, SP is narrowly casteist' Mayawati said that BSP is an Ambedkarite party that operates on the principle of 'Sarvajan Hitay, Sarvajan Sukhay' (for the welfare of all, for the happiness of all). On this basis, the BSP government ran four times in UP. On the other hand, SP changes colours like a chameleon for its narrow casteist politics and electoral self-interest. She said that such politics might benefit an individual for some time, but it cannot benefit the entire society. Therefore, people from all sections of society need to be cautious of SP's deceptive politics. This is both the demand of the time and in the interest of all sections of society.

stories.title: Flowers showered on those who threw slippers at Pappu Yadav:Roadshow held in open jeep, ‘Jai Shri Ram’ slogans raised
stories.summary: The two men accused of attacking Bihar MP Pappu Yadav with slippers were given a grand welcome in Bulandshahr on Friday (7 Aug) after being released on bail. Supporters garlanded the duo before they travelled in an open jeep in a 7-km roadshow from Bulandshahr to Nathla Hasanpur village. Supporters showered flowers during roadshow As the open jeep moved through the route, supporters showered the two men with flowers and raised slogans of 'Jai Shri Ram'. They later reached their village, where drums and trumpets were played during their welcome. Despite the rain, a large number of supporters were seen dancing and raising slogans. BJP district president Vikas Chauhan and several party workers also welcomed the duo, while their family members embraced them. Slipper attack followed protests over Pappu Yadav's Parliament remarks The incident came days after Pappu Yadav allegedly staged a 'chanda chori' demonstration in Parliament while dressed as a sadhu on July 31. Protests were subsequently held against him in several cities, including Lucknow. A Hindu nationalist leader had also announced a reward of ₹51 lakh for anyone who beheaded the MP. Both accused handed over to police after attack On August 2, Sumit Giri, a Bulandshahr resident, allegedly attacked Pappu Yadav along with his associate Happy Sharma. During the incident, Yadav reportedly caught Sumit, while his supporters allegedly assaulted Happy. Both men were subsequently handed over to the police. Sumit Giri is the BJP city minister, while Happy Sharma is the party's Mandal general secretary. See 3 pictures ‘Pappu Yadav was enraged when questioned over remarks on Sanatan Dharma’ Sumit Giri and his associate Happy Sharma alleged that Pappu Yadav became angry when they questioned him over remarks they considered insulting to Lord Shri Ram, worshipped by millions of Hindus. They further alleged that Yadav and his associates assaulted them. Sumit later lodged a complaint at Tilak Nagar Police Station in Delhi, accusing Yadav and his associates of assault and alleging that his gold chain and watch were taken during the incident. Mother broke down after BJP leader’s arrest Following Sumit Giri’s arrest, his mother broke down while speaking about her son. She said she only wanted him to return home safely and had no interest in politics. According to her, Sumit had left home saying he was going to his office. In an emotional appeal, she urged that her son be released and allowed to return home safely. First, know about the accused Sumit-Happy: Now see the pictures of the attack on the MP July 31: Pappu Yadav stages symbolic Ram Temple donation protest in Parliament On July 31, the 10th day of the Monsoon Session, Pappu Yadav arrived at Parliament dressed as a sadhu in saffron robes and carrying a donation box. He staged a short symbolic play on the Parliament premises to protest what he described as the alleged misuse or theft of Ram Temple donations. Pappu Yadav played the role of a priest and sat on the ground with the donation box. Rahul Gandhi and several other MPs then symbolically gave him donations. ‘Caught stealing’, opposition MPs stage symbolic action During the performance, Pappu Yadav was shown keeping the donated money with himself instead of putting it into the box. Opposition MPs, including Ayodhya MP Awadhesh Prasad, then staged a symbolic assault after allegedly catching him ‘stealing’ the donations. As part of the protest, Pappu Yadav was also seen touching Awadhesh Prasad’s feet. See pictures of the protest in the Parliament premises- Many opposition MPs put donations in the donation box. August 1: FIR registered against Rahul Gandhi, Awadhesh Prasad and Pappu Yadav An FIR was registered in Varanasi against Congress MP Rahul Gandhi, Samajwadi Party MP Awadhesh Prasad and Independent Bihar MP Pappu Yadav over their symbolic act in Parliament involving alleged theft of offerings. The complaint was filed by Jagadguru Balak Das, head priest of Patalpuri Math, at Kotwali Police Station. Meanwhile, in Lucknow, Anurodh Rai, national president of the Sanatan Raksha Sangathan, issued a warning against Pappu Yadav and alleged that Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav were also opposed to Sanatan Dharma. He demanded an apology and made a controversial threat against the leaders. He also announced a ₹51 lakh reward for anyone who beheads Pappu Yadav. August 2: Hindu groups protest outside Pappu Yadav’s wife’s residence Bajrang Dal workers and sadhus staged a protest outside the Delhi residence of Ranjeet Ranjan, Pappu Yadav’s wife and a Rajya Sabha MP. Reacting to the protest, Pappu Yadav warned that targeting his children or family members would escalate the matter. He said political or personal disputes should not involve children and family members. August 5: BJP leaders lodge complaint against Pappu Yadav Sumit Giri filed a complaint against Pappu Yadav at Tilak Marg Police Station, accusing him of assault, robbery and issuing death threats. stories.title: Ganga rises in Kashi, 84 ghats cut off:Water level rising 2 cm every hour, Manikarnika Ghat shrinks; monsoon reaches south UP
stories.summary: The water level of the Ganga in Kashi is continuously rising. This has broken the connection between the 84 ghats. The space available for cremation at Manikarnika Ghat is also continuously decreasing. The steps of many ghats have been submerged in water. This is making it difficult to go from one ghat to another. Although the flood situation in the city is not severe yet, the continuously rising water level is increasing the administration's concern. According to the Central Water Commission, the water level of the Ganga in Varanasi was recorded at 63.36 meters on Saturday. The water is rising at a rate of about two centimeters per hour. The commission has expressed the possibility of the water level continuing to rise for the next 48 hours. Water also reaching from MP and Chhattisgarh Along with the water coming from Prayagraj, water from the rivers of Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh is also reaching the Ganga. Its direct effect is visible on the water level of the river in Varanasi. Paths closed on ghats, stairs submerged in water Due to the rising water level, a large part of the stairs at many ghats has been submerged in water. The traditional path from one ghat to another has also been closed at many places. This is causing inconvenience to devotees, local people, and those commuting by boat at the ghats. At many ghats, including Tulsi Ghat, water has reached the stairs. With the rising water level, security has also been increased at the ghats. Cremation space reduced at Manikarnika The effect of the rising water level of the Ganga is also visible at the cremation ground on Manikarnika Ghat. Due to the rising water, the space available for cremation is continuously shrinking. People working at the ghat and relatives arriving with bodies are having to arrange cremations in a limited space. Barricading for the Safety of Kanwariyas Considering Sawan and Kanwar Yatra, the administration has started exercising special vigilance at the ghats. Barricading has been done at several places for the safety of devotees. The activity of the water police has also been increased. Boatmen are being instructed to operate their boats carefully, considering the strong current of the river and the rising water level. The administration is keeping an eye on the activities happening at the ghats and in the river. Intermittent rain expected for 48 to 72 hours Amidst the rising water level of the Ganga, the Meteorological Department has also predicted rain in the coming days. On Saturday, the temperature in Varanasi was around 29 degrees Celsius. The wind speed was recorded at about 11 kilometers per hour and humidity at 84 percent. According to meteorologist Prof. Manoj Srivastava, the monsoon trough has shifted from southern Uttar Pradesh to Bihar, Bengal, and Assam. This may lead to a decrease in rainfall activities in Purvanchal for now. However, there is a possibility of intermittent rain in the next 48 to 72 hours. Relief on Friday after heavy rain on Thursday After the heavy rain on August 6, the pace of rain in Varanasi remained subdued on Friday. Some areas experienced drizzle, but there was no heavy rain. Due to the decrease in rain, the temperature increased by about five degrees. On Friday, Varanasi recorded a maximum temperature of 35 degrees Celsius and a minimum of 27.1 degrees Celsius. Instructions to increase the capacity of flood relief camps After the water level of the Ganga rose, the district administration has also intensified flood relief preparations. On Friday, ADM (Finance) and In-charge Disaster Officer Sadanand Gupta held a virtual meeting with officials from departments related to flood control. In the meeting, relief and rescue preparations were reviewed to deal with the potential flood situation. The ADM instructed the Tehsildars of Rajatalab and Sadar Tehsils to inspect the flood relief camps. He also asked to identify 10 to 20 per cent additional sites beyond the existing capacity, so that affected people can be immediately moved to safe places if needed.

stories.title: Yogi to lead Tricolour march in Gorakhpur on August 10:Walk from Rani Lakshmibai statue to Maharana Pratap statue, spread ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ message
stories.summary: On August 10, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will lead a grand Tiranga Yatra in Gorakhpur, as part of the 'Har Ghar Tiranga' campaign being run on the occasion of Partition Horrors Remembrance Day (August 14) and Independence Day (August 15) in Gorakhpur. CM Yogi will lead a 3-kilometer long Tiranga Yatra on foot, from the statue of Rani Lakshmibai located in the Municipal Corporation premises to the statue of Maharana Pratap located at Railway Station Chowk. During this, he will also appeal to the people of the state to hoist the national flag at their respective homes. The state government has set a target of hoisting the national flag on 5 crore homes this year under the 'Har Ghar Tiranga' campaign. With this objective, Tiranga Yatras are being organized across the state. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will launch the campaign from Lucknow on August 9, on Kakori Train Action Day, while on August 10, he will participate in the Tiranga Yatra in Gorakhpur. Preparations for Tiranga Yatra in final stage Mayor Dr. Manglesh Srivastava informed that the preparations for the Tiranga Yatra by the Municipal Corporation are in their final stage. The yatra will start from the Municipal Corporation premises and reach Railway Station Chowk via Golghar Chauraha, Kali Mandir, and Yatayat Tiraha. The Chief Minister will first garland the statue of Rani Lakshmibai and offer floral tributes to the statue of Maharana Pratap at the conclusion of the yatra. The Chief Minister will walk the entire route carrying the tricolour flag. In view of this approximately 3-kilometre-long foot march, the administration has made extensive security arrangements. Preparations are being made to deploy police forces along the march route and to keep the traffic system smooth. This is the route of the Tiranga Yatra Har Ghar Tiranga Campaign

stories.title: 'System traps youth in a chakravyuh’, says Rahul Gandhi:Addresses students at Prayagraj; Cong claims over 2 lakh registrations
stories.summary: Congress MP Rahul Gandhi is addressing the students at the ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ event in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. In his address Rahul Gandhi said, “India has around 40 crore young people, and this is the country’s biggest strength”. He also said China is often discussed as a major power, but its strength is nothing compared with the potential of India’s youth. Rahul Gandhi arrived at the airport at around 1.30 pm and went straight to Swaraj Bhawan, where he met party leaders. He is accompanied by Priyanka Gandhi’s daughter, Miraya Vadra. Congress leaders claimed that more than 2 lakh students had registered for the event. The historic building was the birthplace of his grandmother and former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. It is now a museum displaying objects linked to the Nehru-Gandhi family and India's freedom movement. Students from 23 districts have been invited. The Congress claims that more than 2 lakh students have registered, but only around 5,000 people have arrived so far. Rahul Gandhi is expected to raise issues including unemployment, the NEET paper leak, irregularities in recruitment exams, and police lathi-charge on students, targeting the government over these concerns. Congress puts up 'No jobs, no throne' posters Congress workers put up posters across Prayagraj ahead of Gandhi's programme. The posters read: “If there are no jobs, the throne will shake.” Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai said the government was afraid of Gandhi. “Everyone in the government is afraid of Rahul Gandhi. BJP leaders are nervous because they have done nothing for students or in the national interest,” Rai said. ₹2 crore pandal set up for programme A pandal costing around ₹2 crore has been erected for the event. A VIP lounge has been set up at the rear, along with eight stalls for VIP guests. Tea and drinking water have been arranged for students at the venue. Dinner has also been arranged for some students. Free e-rickshaw services have been made available to help students reach the venue.

stories.title: Atiq Ahmed's youngest son Abaan laid to rest:Ali, Umar and Ahzam shoulder his bier during final journey
stories.summary: Atiq Ahmed's 21-year-old son Abaan has been laid to rest at the Kasari-Masari cemetery in Prayagraj. He was buried beside his father Atiq's grave. His three brothers, Ali, Umar and Ahzam, carried his bier during the final journey. Around 5,000-6,000 people attended the funeral, while more than 1,000 police personnel were deployed around the cemetery for security. Crowd breaks barricades as Abaan's body arrives Ahzam arrived at the cemetery carrying Abaan's body and was visibly emotional. A large crowd followed him and tried to enter the cemetery. When police stopped them, the crowd became unruly and broke through the barricades. At one point, a police officer used the butt of his rifle to push people back. Some youths still tried to enter the cemetery, prompting police to push them back and disperse the crowd. Police later restricted entry to family members and selected relatives. Shaista Parveen does not attend funeral Abaan's mother, Shaista Parveen, did not attend his funeral. She had also been absent from the funerals of her husband Atiq Ahmed and son Asad. Shaista has been absconding since 2023. Abaan died in a road accident in Jhansi on Thursday. He was travelling from Prayagraj to meet his brother Ali, who is lodged in Jhansi Jail. The Kasari-Masari cemetery, where Abaan was buried, also contains the graves of his grandfather Firoz Ahmed, uncle Ashraf and brother Asad. Ali and Umar attend funeral on parole Ali and Umar reached Prayagraj from Jhansi and Lucknow jails respectively after being granted parole by the Allahabad High Court. Police kept both brothers inside their vans until the final stage of the funeral. When they were brought out, Ali and Umar hugged each other before going to the mosque to offer prayers. They then joined the funeral and helped bury Abaan. Police allowed only family members and relatives to enter the cemetery during the burial. Ali and Umar meet family before returning to jail Ali and Umar are now meeting their family members at a mosque a short distance from the cemetery. The High Court had allowed the brothers to meet only their brother Ahzam and aunt as part of their parole conditions. Police have arranged the meeting outside the mosque, where a tent has been put up. The meeting will last for one hour. After that, police will take Ali back to Jhansi Jail and Umar to Lucknow Jail. This is the first time in four years that Ali and Umar have been granted parole. To know the latest update…please go through the live blog…

stories.title: Will UP hold panchayat polls before Assembly elections?:HC asks govt to hold elections within six months; deadline ends in November
stories.summary: 'The state government is obligated to conduct panchayat elections within 6 months. This period is ending in November 2026.' The Lucknow bench of Allahabad High Court said this on 5 August. Along with this, records have been sought from the government. So that it can be ascertained whether the delay in elections was due to circumstances beyond the government's control or whether the government failed to fulfill its responsibility of conducting elections on time. After this observation, questions are being raised; Did the government deliberately not conduct panchayat elections on time? Can panchayat elections be held before UP Assembly elections? We will know in today's UP Explainer... Question-1: Why were panchayat elections not held on time? Did the government do this deliberately? Answer: There are several political and administrative reasons behind this. The UP government has cited two administrative reasons for this in the Allahabad High Court... 1. The State Election Commission published the final voter list on 10 June, 2026; therefore, panchayat elections could not be held before 26 May, 2026. 2. The reservation system in the elections will be determined by the report of the Backward Classes Commission formed for reservation in panchayat elections. The report will take time to arrive. stories.title: Atiq’s son Ali says, ‘My brother has left me too’:'Haven't slept or eaten for two nights in Jhansi jail'
stories.summary: 'I am coming to meet; I got a bit late.' These 10 words belong to mafia Atiq Ahmed's younger son Abaan, which he said to a police inspector on the phone before reaching Jhansi jail. Just a few minutes later, Abaan died. Abaan was going to meet his brother Ali Ahmed, who is imprisoned in Jhansi jail, on Thursday. On the highway, while trying to save an animal, the car hit the divider. In the accident, Abaan and his friend Sonu died, while three friends were injured. When Ali received the news of his brother's death, he broke down crying. He said, 'Now my brother has also left me.' He kept tossing and turning all night. Kept crying. On normal days, Ali used to exercise in the morning. He also used to talk to some people. But, due to the shock, he remained confined inside his cell. He kept asking the jail officials who came every hour for security checks about the accident repeatedly. Jail sources said that on Friday morning he only had a light breakfast. After that, he did not come out even to eat food. Abaan used to come to Jhansi Jail almost every week to meet Ali loved his younger brother Abaan with all his heart. Abaan also loved him. He used to meet him about three to four times every month. During the meetings, LIU and constables were also present. Sources say that as soon as Ali and Abaan saw each other, they would embrace. They would meet like this for a few minutes. Their meetings took place under strict surveillance. For the purpose of meetings, Abaan would often stay at a hotel near the bus stand. On every visit, Abaan would bring novels and books for his elder brother to read. After the accident on Thursday, two books were found in the car - 'The Stationery Shop of Tehran' and 'The Idiot'. Ali told High Court Judge - Let me go to the funeral The family of Ali, imprisoned in Jhansi jail, and Umar, imprisoned in Lucknow jail, had filed a petition for parole in the High Court to attend Abaan's funeral. During the hearing on Friday, both were connected to the court via video conferencing. They said they wanted to attend their brother's funeral. Both assured the court that they will not speak to the media, will not post anything on social media, will not address any gathering, and will not participate in any other event. The court asked for strict compliance with these conditions. The High Court ordered that Ali and Umar be taken directly from jail to Kasari-Masari cemetery. There they have been permitted to meet their younger brother Ahzam and aunt Parveen Qureshi for one hour. This meeting will be under police supervision. After this, both will be sent back to jail. The court has also directed the state government and DGP to ensure the security and necessary arrangements for both. Jhansi jail administration wrote a letter to SSP to take Ali Atiq's sister Parveen Qureshi had filed a petition in the High Court for parole of Umar and Ali. Their advocate Mohammad Safdar Ali Kazmi presented this matter in court. The bench of Justice Ajay Bhanot and DC Samant ordered parole. Now the Jhansi jail administration has written a letter to the SSP to take Ali to Prayagraj under police security by providing a police guard. Abaan was going to meet his brother in jail, died in a road accident

stories.title: Kabaddi player with 4 medals killed over affair:Shot in the head and stomach after girlfriend's brother saw Instagram chats
stories.summary: A 22-year-old kabaddi player was shot dead in Shamli on Saturday. According to the infortmation, the player had an affair with his friend's cousin sister. The accused friend had seen their chat on Instagram. They had also fought 15 days ago. The kabaddi player Mohana alias Monu was a resident of Baghpat. He had come to Shamli on his bike in the morning to pick up labourers. That's when the accused, along with two friends, stopped him on the way. They assaulted him and shot him in the stomach. When Monu ran into a sugarcane field to save his life, the accused chased him. They knocked him down inside the field and beat him with kicks and punches. First, they strangled him. Then shot him in the head. The incident took place around 5:30 AM on Saturday in Nala Jungle village of Kandhla. 2 pictures related to the incident Complete incident in detail Mohana alias Monu, a resident of Kakripur village in Baghpat, used to play kabaddi and also took contracts for spraying medicine on crops. He had his own tanker, which he used to spray pesticides in the fields of nearby farmers. Father Surendra told the police that Monu left his home around 5:15 AM on Saturday to pick up laborers in Nala village. He did not return home for a long time, and worried about this, his family members were searching for him. Bike found on the road, body found in the field Monu's body was found in farmer Parvinder's sugarcane field near the canal bank. He had been shot in the head. Meanwhile, his bike was lying on the road 10 meters ahead. Parvinder immediately informed the police about the incident after seeing the body. Kandhla police, including ASP Sumit Shukla and CO Kairana Hemant Kumar, reached the spot. After this, the forensic team was also called to the crime scene. Police questioned the people living nearby. Police found a live cartridge and an empty shell at the spot. Monu-Kartik became friends at Kabaddi competition When the police investigated with the help of surveillance and by piecing together evidence, the needle of suspicion pointed towards Monu's friend Kartik. The police took him into custody just 4 hours after the murder. When interrogated strictly, Kartik confessed to the murder. Kartik told the police that his two friends and uncle were also involved in Monu's murder. He said that Monu and he were once very close friends. Both had played together in many kabaddi competitions. Both had also participated together in a competition held in Madhya Pradesh. Kartik traced Monu through his sister's Instagram Kartik stated that his sister had logged into her Instagram ID on his mobile some time ago. But she forgot to log out. During this time, Monu had sent messages to his sister. Kartik read them. The chat contained objectionable remarks about his sister. Kartik repeatedly asked Monu to understand and stop the conversation, but he did not comply. After this, he decided to teach Monu a lesson. Kartik planned Monu's murder. He also involved his friends Arjun, Satyam, and uncle Ompal in this. Shot in the head after strangulation Kartik already knew that Monu had taken a contract for spraying pesticides in the fields a year ago. For this, he used to pick up laborers every morning from Shamli's Nala and surrounding villages. Monu used to drop the laborers back in the evening by bike. Kartik told the police that he reached Monu with two friends on Saturday morning. Seeing them, Monu stopped, after which they started assaulting him. Arjun fired a shot, which hit Monu in the stomach. As soon as he was shot, Monu left his bike and ran to save his life. But he fell in a nearby sugarcane field. Kartik, along with his two friends, chased Monu and reached the field. There, they caught him and beat him again. Then they strangled him. Satyam shot him in the head. After murdering Monu, all three fled from the scene. Plan to settle in Delhi after murder Kartik said that after the incident, he had planned to go to Delhi with his two companions and live in a rented flat. He was also going to bear the entire expenses of both his companions. They were confident that they would easily escape after the murder. Won 4 medals at state level Mohana alias Monu had won one gold, two silver, and one bronze medal in state-level Kabaddi competitions. In divisional-level competitions, he had secured two gold, three silver, and four bronze medals. In district-level Kabaddi competitions, he had won a total of eight medals, including five gold.

stories.title: 13 accused arrested for gambling:Game was going on in a closed house, 1.58 lakh cash recovered
stories.summary: Police conducted a major operation against gamblers and arrested 13 accused in Agra's Jagdishpura police station area. Police recovered ₹1.58 lakh cash, 2 scooters, 1 motorcycle, and 25 mobile phones from their possession. ACP Lohamandi Gaurav Singh informed that on 1st August, the Jagdishpura police station team was conducting checking and patrolling in the area. During this time, information was received from an informer that some people were gambling in a closed house near Neelam Enclave, opposite Om Factory. Upon receiving the information, the police team reached the spot, conducted a raid, and arrested all 13 accused from the location. The arrested accused have been identified as Dharmendra Parihar, Satish Kumar, Sanjay Sharma, Dashrath, Vivek Kumar, Shivam, Dhruv, Govind Kumar, Bhavesh Jhamnani, Sunny, son of Janendra, Salman, Gaurav, and Dharmendra, son of Mahesh. All the accused are said to be residents of different police station areas of Agra. Police stated that a total of 52 playing cards, 25 mobile phones, 2 scooters, and 1 motorcycle were also recovered from the accused. Of the recovered cash, ₹1,53,460 was obtained from the gambling den and ₹5,070 was recovered during body search. A case has been registered at Jagdishpura police station in this matter.

stories.title: Protest against Nishikant Dubey in Varanasi:Congress workers dump his photo in drain; call his remarks on former PM 'derogatory'
stories.summary: Workers of the Indian Youth Congress metropolitan unit staged a protest on Saturday at 3 PM against the alleged indecent remarks made by BJP MP Nishikant Dubey about former Prime Minister Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru. The workers expressed their anger by symbolically protesting against the MP's photo and throwing it into a gutter. Police arrived at the spot during the protest The protest was led by metropolitan Youth Congress President Chanchal Sharma. State co-in-charge Narasimha Yadav was also present during this time. A police force was deployed during the protest, and attempts were made to stop the workers, but the workers registered their protest. Chanchal Sharma said that disrespectful comments against the country's first Prime Minister, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, are not acceptable. He demanded that the BJP take disciplinary action against Nishikant Dubey and seek a public apology from him. He said that if an apology is not made, the Youth Congress will continue its protest. These people participated in the protest The demonstration was attended by Anupam Rai, Om Shukla, Dheeraj Sonkar, Vineet Choubey, Md. Zeeshan, Ashwani Yadav, Utkarsh Pandey, Ashutosh Srivastava, Sujan Khan, Suraj Yadav, Jamal Ahmad, Siddharth Keshari, Sonu Tiwari and other workers.

stories.title: Fake 'Police Chowki' run in UP:Gang trapped people through nude video calls by girl; extorted money while posing as cops
stories.summary: A gang operated a fake 'Police Chowki' to blackmail people, just 3 km from a police station in Meerut. Police have arrested two accused, while two others are still absconding. The gang first trapped people by making them have nude video calls with a girl. After that, they would threaten to implicate them in false cases. Then they would call them to the fake police station and extort money from them. After a young man's complaint, the police conducted a raid on Friday night (31st July). A fake police station setup was found in the room. The case is from the Brahmpuri police station area. Young man filed complaint on 29th July On July 29, a young man arrived at Brahmpuri police station with a complaint. He told the police that the policemen at TP Nagar police post are blackmailing me. The inspector and constable have demanded money from me by threatening to implicate me in a false case. Based on the complaint, the police started an investigation. The police post that the young man mentioned was not found in police records. After this, Brahmpuri police station started a secret investigation into the entire matter. Police uniform and other items were also found Late Friday night, the police raided the location that was mentioned. The police were also shocked to see the scene inside the room. An atmosphere exactly like a real police post had been created. A table and chair like that of a post-in-charge were placed in the room. Pictures of Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar were hung behind. Two fake policemen present at the spot were arrested. During the search, police found uniforms and equipment used in police stations at the location. During interrogation, it was revealed that the accused used to intimidate people by posing as police personnel. Used to trap people by making nude video calls According to police, these people worked like cyber fraudsters. First, they would arrange a video call with a girl. The girl would become nude on the video call. She would talk dirty with the person on the other end for a few minutes. During this time, the video call was recorded. Later, the fake policemen would call the person who had the video call conversation and threaten them. Then, they would call them to the fake police station and extort money. 2 accused arrested, search on for 2 others Police have arrested 2 accused present in the fake police station in this case. 2 other accused are still absconding, and raids are being conducted to search for them. Police are also investigating how many people have fallen victim to this gang so far. Along with this, the role of the girl making nude calls is also being investigated.
