stories.title: 3 arrested, including JE, for taking ₹7.5 lakh bribe:Caught red-handed by Vigilance in Lucknow; had demanded ₹15 lakh
stories.summary: Lucknow Vigilance arrested 3 people, including a Junior Engineer (JE) of the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA), while allegedly accepting a ₹7.5 lakh bribe. The accused were caught red-handed at the LDA's Gomti Nagar office after the complainant, acting on the vigilance team's instructions, handed over the money. The arrested accused have been identified as Zone-5 JE Dinesh Kumar Verma, supervisor Chandra Prakash, and middleman Shravan Kumar. According to the complaint, they had demanded ₹15 lakh from the complainant in exchange for allowing construction of his house to continue. The complainant had approached the Superintendent of Police, Uttar Pradesh Vigilance Establishment, Lucknow Sector, alleging that the JE visited his under-construction building and threatened to stop the work unless the bribe was paid. After verification, the vigilance team laid a trap and arrested all three while accepting ₹7.5 lakh. They are now being questioned. The complainant was informed that an IGRS (Integrated Grievance Redressal System) complaint had been filed regarding the construction of his house. He was called to the LDA office on the pretext of resolving the matter. According to the complainant, after reaching the LDA office, JE Dinesh Kumar Verma and supervisor Chandra Prakash demanded a ₹15 lakh bribe, threatening action against the construction if he refused to pay. When the complainant said he could not arrange such a large amount, the deal was allegedly negotiated down to ₹7.5 lakh. The vigilance investigation revealed that the JE and the supervisor had enlisted Shravan Kumar, a private individual, as a middleman to collect the bribe. The three allegedly used the IGRS complaint to pressure the complainant into paying. During a confidential inquiry, vigilance officials claimed that mobile phone conversations and other evidence confirmed the demand for the bribe. After verifying the complaint, the vigilance team laid a trap. On Saturday, the complainant arrived with the agreed ₹7.5 lakh. As soon as the accused accepted the cash, the vigilance team arrested all three red-handed and recovered the entire amount. The vigilance team arrested the accused outside the Gomti Nagar LDA office and seized the full bribe amount from them.

stories.title: Bomb-making note found with student in Ayodhya:Wrote 'big blast, Holland Hall' while on duty at medical college; detained by police
stories.summary: A slip containing methods for making bombs has been found with a student at Ayodhya Medical College. It reads: Big Blast, Holland Hall. Along with this, several chemical formulas and their diagrams are also drawn. As soon as this information was received, police and security agencies became alert. The police have taken the student into custody. The student told the police that he was watching a film on his laptop during night duty. The film was teaching how to make bombs. He had noted down that method on the slip. Meanwhile, police investigation revealed that the slip contains notes of quite in-depth research about bomb-making methods, the structure of explosive devices, their size and intensity. Currently, the student has been taken to Ayodhya Police Lines. There, officers from SOG, STF, Special Branch, and IB are interrogating him. Slip reads: Big blast, chemical formula for making a bomb Sarfaraz, a resident of Balrampur, is a first-year student of Lab Technician (Paramedical) at Rajrishi Dashrath Medical College in Ayodhya. His father has passed away. Sarfaraz lives in a hostel near the medical college. Sarfaraz's duty in the X-ray lab is from 10 PM to 8 AM. On Friday night (July 31), Abhishek and Subhash were also on duty with Sarfaraz. After their duty ended at 8 AM, cleaning staff arrived to clean the lab. There they found a slip. He gave the slip to the staff who came on duty in the morning. The staff saw that the slip contained information including bomb-making methods, chemical formulas, big explosions, and their reactions. After this, the staff informed the police about this matter. Student questioned on several points The police who reached the spot were handed over the slip and recovered materials by the medical college administration. Then Darshan Nagar outpost in-charge Brijbhushan Pathak called Sarfaraz and took him into custody. After this, he was taken to the police lines for questioning. There, officers from SOG, STF, Special Branch and IB questioned Sarfaraz. Sarfaraz said, ''I couldn't sleep on Friday night. That's why I was watching the film Bhagat Singh on my laptop. It shows how to make a bomb. I also tried to learn that method. But, by then I felt sleepy and fell asleep. After that, the paper went into the hands of these people.'' Police have also taken Abhishek, who was on duty with Sarfaraz, into custody. The third student, Subhash, who is a resident of Sultanpur, left for his village on Saturday morning. As soon as information about the case was received, several investigation agencies became active. The student is being questioned on several points. An attempt is being made to find out why he made the slip. What was his motive behind this? Where did he write the chemical formula and research on the slip from? For now, no official statement has been issued by the police. Officials say that further action will be taken only after verification of facts.

stories.title: Descriptive pattern set for DDU odd semester exams:Vice-Chancellor confirms change to drive quality education
stories.summary: From the upcoming odd semester at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, graduation and post-graduation examinations will now be conducted in descriptive pattern. The Controller of Examinations office issued an official notification in this regard on Friday afternoon at around 12:30 PM. This decision has been taken after the recommendation of the examination committee and the approval of Vice Chancellor Prof. Poonam Tandon. With the implementation of the new system, question papers for most courses will now be descriptive. Vice Chancellor Prof. Poonam Tandon stated that descriptive examinations will enhance students' deep understanding of subjects, thinking ability, and writing skills. This change is an important step towards providing quality education under the National Education Policy (NEP-2020). The university believes that this will enable proper assessment of students' talent. No changes made in the system for these courses According to the notification, postgraduate and some technical/professional courses of graduation such as BBA, BCA, BHMCT, BSc Agriculture and B.Tech examinations will continue to be held in descriptive pattern as before. Meanwhile, semester examinations of all 'minor courses' of graduation and postgraduate will be conducted in MCQ (Multiple Choice Questions) pattern under the old system. Notification uploaded on website, preparation instructions The Controller of Examinations has given necessary instructions to all heads of departments, deans of the university and principals of affiliated colleges to prepare question papers according to the new pattern. Students and teachers can also view this notification by visiting the university's official website.

stories.title: ₹51-lakh bounty for Pappu Yadav’s head:Lucknow mock funeral sees effigy burned at Gandhi statue by protesters in Akhilesh-Rahul masks
stories.summary: In Lucknow on Saturday, the Sanatan Raksha Sangathan protested against Opposition leaders. They took out a funeral procession for MP Pappu Yadav. This procession went from Shri Ram Tower in Hazratganj to the Gandhi statue. Many workers of the organisation in the procession were wearing masks of Akhilesh Yadav and Rahul Gandhi, which were being hit with slippers. A large number of protesters marched forward chanting 'Pappu Yadav Murdabad', 'Rahul Gandhi-Akhilesh Yadav Murdabad' along with 'Ram Naam Satya'. Upon reaching the Gandhi statue, an effigy resembling Pappu Yadav's dead body was first beaten with slippers and then set on fire. During this, people from the organisation said that those who insult Sanatan Dharma will not be forgiven. The organisation also announced a reward of ₹51 lakh for anyone who brings Pappu Yadav's head. In the funeral procession, a person wearing Akhilesh Yadav's mask carried the effigy on his shoulder. 'Pappu's end has come' Anurodh Rai, National President of Sanatan Raksha Sangathan, said that people like Pappu Yadav were never part of Sanatan. “A reward of ₹51 lakh will be given to anyone who brings Pappu Yadav's head. The way Pappu Yadav insulted Sanatan in the Parliament premises yesterday by wearing saffron clothes has hurt our sentiments. Our entire society is enraged. The punishment for Pappu Yadav has begun. I want to warn him that the end of your sins has come and the time for punishment has arrived,” he said. Opposition Leaders Involved in Sin Anurodh Rai said that opposition leaders, especially Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav, are also completely anti-Sanatan. These people have also committed the same sin that Pappu Yadav did. In his attempt to insult Sanatan, these leaders were also equally complicit. “That is why we openly oppose them. We want to warn that too many sins have been committed. Now, if these people commit any kind of sin, the Sanatan Raksha Sangathan will pull out their tongues and tie them to a peg,” he said. 'Lord Ram was also insulted' Shailendra Kumar Dixit said that the drama Pappu Yadav performed by wearing clothes of Sanatan Dharma will not be tolerated. “Wherever Pappu Yadav is seen, his head will be shaved and he will be beaten with slippers. Whatever happened inside the house yesterday is also an insult to Lord Ram. It was tried to show there that everyone in the Ram temple is a thief. No one's politics will be as dirty as that of the opposition leaders present in Parliament," Dixit said.

stories.title: Rape, abetment to suicide case against Naib Tehsildar:Girlfriend takes life; mother alleges accused coerced her to sleep with senior officers
stories.summary: A case of rape and abetment to suicide has been registered against a Naib Tehsildar in Jaunpur. The lawsuit was filed on Thursday night, five months after the woman's death, based on a complaint from her mother. The deceased's mother alleged- The Naib Tehsildar had a relationship with my daughter by promising marriage. Then he started pressuring her to have relationships with his fellow officers. Distressed by the mental torture, my daughter took her own life. The incident is from Mirganj police station area, 55 km from the district headquarters. The accused Naib Tehsildar is currently posted in Kerakat Tehsil. The woman committed suicide by hanging herself at her maternal home on 9 March 2026. The details of the case A woman residing in a village in Mirganj informed the police in a complaint filed on Thursday that she had married her daughter in a village in Barsathi in 2014. After the marriage, her daughter had a girl child, who is about 10 years old now. According to the woman, her daughter's husband worked in Surat. About two years ago, in 2024, her daughter shifted to Sultanpur with her child. Her elder sister also lived in Sultanpur. The daughter started living in a rented room. During this time, she became acquainted with Vivek Srivastava, a resident of Gora Barik village in Sultanpur, who lived in the neighbourhood. At that time, Vivek was posted as a Kanungo in the Revenue Department. Later, he was promoted to the post of Naib Tehsildar. Proximity grew with frequent visits According to the complaint given to the police, Vivek and the woman's proximity gradually increased. The woman's mother stated that Vivek started coming to her daughter's room. He trapped her in his love by promising marriage. After this, he started spoiling her relationship with her husband. Instigated her to divorce her husband The mother alleges that Vivek told her daughter to divorce her husband, and that they would both get married. At that time, Vivek was unmarried. At his insistence, about a year and a half ago, the daughter filed a case in court for divorce from her husband. During this time, Vivek continued to visit her room. Made obscene videos under the pretext of taking her out About a year ago, Vivek was transferred to Machhlishahr in Jaunpur as a Naib Tehsildar. After this, the woman used to visit him there at intervals of 15-20 days. The mother alleges that everything was fine initially, but later Vivek started harassing her. He would take her out under the pretext of sightseeing and make obscene videos. Assault and Threat to Kill The mother alleged that Vivek pressured her to have relations with his colleagues posted in the tehsil. When she refused, he would assault her and threaten to kill her. Fed up with the harassment, the woman died by suicide by hanging herself at her maternal home on 9 March 2026. FIR Registered Against Naib Tehsildar Under These Sections: SP hands over investigation to SHO SP Rural Atish Kumar Singh said: A case has been registered against Naib Tehsildar Vivek Srivastava, posted in Kerakat, under several sections. The investigation of the case has been handed over to the Mirganj police station in-charge.

stories.title: Undercover cops bust major Varanasi cyber scam:Constables disguised as job seekers offered ₹8,000 role after working 3 days
stories.summary: Varanasi Cyber Crime and Bhelupur police busted a cyber fraud racket operating under the guise of a share trading company. The fake company was raided in its Mahmudganj office in Varanasi on Thursday evening. On Friday, a total of 32 accused were presented in court. The court released all arrested female telecallers on personal bonds of ₹25,000 each, while 11 male accused were sent to jail on 14-day judicial remand. To nab this gang, which had defrauded many people across the country to the tune of ₹1.25 crore, the police sent two constables here disguised as job seekers. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to DCP, Crime, Neetu Kadyan and a constable about how the fake company was busted. Cyber Crime received a complaint DCP Kashi Neetu Kadyan said, “A small complaint was filed against the arrested individuals. Our money was taken by a call centre operating in Mahmudganj in the name of a trading company. When we deployed a team, we found that boys and girls come here and make calls from here, displaying a SEBI registered board. After this, we planned a complete operation and nabbed them. In this, we sent two cyber crime constables as job seekers.” Constables went for three days, observed the working style When Dainik Bhaskar spoke to the constable, he said, “When the cyber crime team received the information, we first investigated NKD Associates. We checked its SEBI registration and found the number to be fake. So then I and another colleague went to their office posing as job seekers from Bihar.” “There we met Vinay Maurya. Vinay asked for our names, addresses, and the reason for our visit. So we told him that we were very troubled, we needed a job, and we had graduated. Vinay Maurya said there was a job. So we said we would come tomorrow and left from there, so that he wouldn't suspect anything,” he said. On the second day, Vinay offered a job for ₹8,000 The constable said, "When we arrived there on the second day, i.e., Tuesday, several employees also came to us and told us about the work, saying it was good work, just making calls and nothing else. It was there that we learned that more employees come to the office on Mondays and Thursdays. On this day too, Vinay met us and talked about a salary of ₹8,000 and incentives for the work. He said, ‘Come tomorrow and I will explain the work.’" Work explained on the third day The constable said, “When we reached there on the second day, very few employees were in the office. The number of girls among them was higher and all were busy making calls. After some time, the mastermind Vinay came and said that people need to be given tips for share trading. To this, we said that we have not passed the authorised examination for that.” “He said, ‘No problem, we will get it done, you start working.’ We were given a script and told to read it out to the caller. We said we would come tomorrow and left from there. We had all the evidence,” the constable added. Raid conducted on Thursday after lunch DCP Neetu Kadyan said, “The constables conducted reconnaissance there for three days. After that, we raided on Thursday, the day when the maximum number of employees are present. The raid was conducted after lunch on that day so that the entire team could be on the spot. From the spot, we arrested a total of 32 people, including 21 women and nine men involved in tele-calling.” Accused are residents of Mirzapur, Chandauli and Varanasi The DCP said all of the accused are residents of Mirzapur, Chandauli and Varanasi. “They fraudulently operated a firm named NKD Associates in a residential building, which was claimed to be registered with SEBI. People working here received salaries ranging from ₹8,000 to ₹16,000. They trapped customers through tele-calling for investment in share trading and made them invest.” DCP said accused do not have share trading qualifications DCP Neetu Kadyan said 21 girls were found at the spot during the police raid. All these girls were doing telecalling. All admitted that they were called through s. They were told that 'we are an institution licensed by SEBI'. None of the girls had any share trading qualification. A graduate boy or girl, without any course or experience, was working as a salaried merchant, calling people and committing fraud. They should have seen that no one had any kind of job letter. There was no HR, no research team in the company. "The boys and girls were only given a list of phone numbers and a script. They would have been victims if money had been stolen from their accounts. They themselves were taking money from someone. So they are becoming involved in the crime. They were receiving cash instead of salary in their bank accounts from these very funds," the DCP said.

stories.title: Lucknow man murdered at home:Family members assaulted too; wife alleges village head’s husband led attack with 18 men
stories.summary: In Gosainganj, Lucknow, the husband of the village head, along with 18 other, brutally beat a young man to death. The deceased's brother and wife were also attacked with sharp weapons, but both of them managed to survive. Two minor children and the wife of the deceased young man are in a terrible state, crying inconsolably. The incident is from Rasulpur Tikniyamau, under the Gosainganj police station area. On 31 July at 8 PM, Mohammad Haseeb, husband of Tikaniya's village head Iram, along with Ram Suchit, Chandrika Prasad, Sumit, Amit, Lalit, Avdhesh, Haresh, Ashok, Abhishek, Umit, Nannan, Kamlu, Udal, Faizan, Shiva, and two unknown individuals, arrived at the house of Azad (the deceased young man) in the same village, carrying rods, sharp weapons, and sticks. According to Azad's wife Anju, a complaint had been made to the village head's husband regarding the cleaning of the drain due to the blockage of the house's drainage system. He first chased them away, and then, after some time, attacked their house with his supporters. In this, his wife Anju, brother Rohit, and minor son were seriously injured. Entered with iron rods, machetes, and sticks Anju, the wife of the deceased Azad, has filed a complaint with the police, making serious allegations against several people, including Mohammad Haseeb, the husband of the village head. Anju alleges that the accused, angered by a complaint about drain cleaning, broke into their house, beat her husband to death, and also launched a deadly attack on other family members. Anju stated that the water from their house was not draining. Upon complaining about getting the drain cleaned, Mohammad Haseeb, the husband of the village head, along with his supporters, arrived at their house around 8 PM on Friday night. All the accused were armed with iron rods, sharp weapons (Banka), and sticks. As soon as the accused entered the house, they launched a relentless attack on her husband Azad, leading to his on-the-spot death. According to Anju, when she tried to save her husband, she was also subjected to a deadly attack, leaving her seriously injured. 'Attackers wanted to kill the entire family' Anju alleges that the attackers also attacked her son Pradeep and brother-in-law Sarju. “The attackers said, 'Finish them all',”Anju recalled. Her son and brother-in-law are seriously injured. Upon hearing the commotion, the accused fled the scene. Anju has filed a complaint against village head's husband Mohammad Haseeb and others for murder, attempted murder, assault by trespassing, and threatening. Based on the complaint, the police have registered a case against 16 named and two unknown individuals and have taken four people into custody for questioning. Complaint was filed at the police station earlier The deceased's brother, Ranjeet, alleged that the Pradhan's husband did not clean the drain on their side. We had filed a complaint at the police station today around 4 PM. The Pradhan's husband had threatened to kill us. In the evening, he attacked and killed my brother. Ranjeet said that his brother used to work as a labourer at a mill in the village. He has two children, Saloni and Vishal. Police took 4 accused into custody Police have taken the named accused Sumit, Abhishek, Ram Suchit, and Amit into custody. Police teams are continuously raiding to arrest other named accused. A case has been registered in the matter based on Anju's complaint. Police have sent the deceased's body for post-mortem. After the incident, police forces have been deployed in the village and surrounding areas to avoid any untoward situation. DCP South Mohd. Mushtaq said- Two parties clashed over a drain dispute. A young man from one side has died. Five people from both sides are injured. In the initial investigation, four people have been taken into custody. Strict action will be taken against the accused in the matter.

stories.title: ‘First and last mistake… I am just 15’:Girl booked over PM Modi remarks apologises; Dipke asks if case will be withdrawn
stories.summary: A 15-year-old girl who abused Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the Jantar Mantar protest has apologised publicly. In a video message, she said, "I am only 15 years old. This was my first and last mistake. I was misled." Meanwhile, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday asked, "Will the government also withdraw the cases?" On Friday night, the Prime Minister shared an Instagram reel saying, "I want to forgive the children who used abusive language against me and my mother." Girl seen with folded hands in the video The girl who abused the Prime Minister at Jantar Mantar has now issued a public apology. In a video that has gone viral on social media, she is seen with folded hands apologising for her remarks. She says she is only 15 years old. In the video, the girl says, "I had gone to Connaught Place with my friends. A student protest was taking place there, and some people around us were raising objectionable slogans against the Prime Minister. I got carried away by the atmosphere and the crowd." A case was registered against the girl in Noida on 30 July. Two pictures of the girl… July 23: Abuse PM Modi says, ‘I want to forgive misguided children’ PM Modi shared a reel on Instagram on Friday night, saying that some mischievous children at Jantar Mantar had used abusive language against him and his mother, but children make mistakes. He further said that childhood also provides an opportunity to correct mistakes. “These are misguided children; this is the time to show them the right path. I want to forgive them,” he said. This was PM Modi’s fifth video in the last nine days. The video, posted at 11 pm, received 13 lakh likes within 30 minutes. PM's fifth video in 9 days

Chitragupta Peethadhishwar Swami Sachchidanand Maharaj demanded the cancellation of his parliamentary membership. stories.title: Varanasi launches 10 new flights from today:Travel made easier to Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Vijayawada as three airlines boost operations
stories.summary: There is good news for passengers travelling from Varanasi's Lal Bahadur Shastri Airport. Starting today, August 1st, not one or two, but 10 new flights are going to commence directly from Varanasi Airport. With the launch of new flights, passengers will find it easier to travel to and from major cities like Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Vijayawada. Among these flights, Air India Express is going to increase the most flights. New flight services on these routes 22 flights daily Currently, 22 flights arrive and 22 flights depart from Varanasi airport every day. Thus, a total of 44 flights are being operated. After the addition of new flights, this number will reach 54. This is expected to increase the number of passengers at the airport. Earlier, there were 84 flights daily It should also be noted that at the beginning of the year, about 84 flights operated daily from Varanasi. Around 12,000 passengers commuted daily. However, due to the increase in air fuel prices, the number of flights gradually decreased. Currently, this number has reduced to 44 flights. Regarding this, officials of Varanasi Airport say that the commencement of new flights will benefit passengers and also promote tourism. A large number of devotees visit Kashi during the month of Sawan. In addition, the number of tourists coming from outside will also increase. Officials have expressed the possibility of more new flights starting in the coming days.

stories.title: UP weather crisis:Rain inundates Bareilly, 9 houses submerged in Ballia, wildlife invades Lakhimpur, high alert issued across 71 cities
stories.summary: The momentum of the monsoon has temporarily slowed in Uttar Pradesh. Barring a few parts of Western UP, rainfall has largely ceased across the rest of the state. Early on Saturday (6:30 AM), heavy downpours lashed Bareilly, while cloud cover accompanied by strong, cool winds persisted over several cities, including Lucknow, Kanpur, and Gorakhpur. Meanwhile, incessant rainfall in the upper hilly reaches has pushed ten rivers—including the Ganga, Ghaghra, and Saryu—to swell beyond danger levels. In Ballia, severe riverbank erosion by the Saryu River swallowed nine houses in a single day, forcing more than 100 families to abandon their homes and migrate to safer locations. In Lakhimpur Kheri, panic spread on Friday after a crocodile was spotted once again in a local canal. Just a week prior, a crocodile had preyed on a dog in the same vicinity. In a separate incident nearby, a 12-foot-long python became trapped in a net near a field. Responding to alerts, a Forest Department team rescued the reptile and safely released it into the jungle. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal has now moved towards Odisha and Chhattisgarh, temporarily stalling monsoon activity in Uttar Pradesh. Satellite imagery shows rain-bearing clouds absent from nearly 70 to 80 per cent of the state. Nonetheless, the weather department has forecast light rainfall across 71 districts today.

stories.title: Constable rapes and kills girl:Grandmother weeps over uniform as young sister denounces 'bad officer'
stories.summary: 'Police uncle is bad. He took Didi on his bike and sent her up. Papa is saying, she will never come back now. She used to teach me painting every day. Her bag is with me now. I will study from her notebooks and books.' The 10-year-old girl, victim of the brutality of Constable Abhishek Yadav (35) in Gorakhpur, is no longer in this world. Dainik Bhaskar's team reached her home on Friday (31 July). Here, her younger sisters, aged 5 and 7, were playing with her school bag. The girl's school dress and bag were kept in the verandah of the house. Looking at them repeatedly, the younger sisters were remembering their elder sister. Two younger sisters were wandering hungry and thirsty in the house. Passers-by would hand them packets of chips and leave. Meanwhile, the 13-year-old elder sister is attending to her mother at the district hospital. The girl's mother is admitted to the district hospital, and her brother has been born. However, instead of songs and celebrations, the house is filled with cries and screams. The elderly grandmother sitting inside the house starts screaming, remembering her granddaughter. She showed the girl's dress hanging on a rope to the Bhaskar reporter and burst into tears. She said, "My dear child has been snatched away." The father, who drives an e-rickshaw, is entangled in police proceedings. The girl studied in 5th class at a government school The 10-year-old girl, a victim of the constable's brutality, wanted to become a doctor. She studied in 5th grade at a government school in the Betiahata area. Her class teacher says she was very bright in studies. Whatever homework was given, she would complete it in school itself. If anything was asked, she would be the first to raise her hand to answer. On July 28, the constable abducted the girl and took her to the cremation ground. There, after raping her, the constable brutally murdered her. Even on the day of the incident, the girl had gone to school in the morning. When she returned home, she took off her dress and hung it on the veranda. She then put on a lower and t-shirt and started playing. In the evening, her elder sister was admitted to the district hospital due to chest pain. Her father and aunt were with the admitted child. Meanwhile, at home, the 10-year-old girl cooked food. Then, at night, she took her 7-year-old younger sister and went to the district hospital to deliver food. Her father said that she had to complete her homework, so she wanted to return home quickly. When she went to get water, the constable enticed her and made her sit on his bike. On the night of July 28 (Tuesday), the constable met the girl who had gone out to get water at the hospital. He enticed the girl on the pretext of dropping her home and made her sit on his bike. A 44-hour timeline was prepared from the CCTV footage installed at 7 city intersections, mobile location, and post-mortem report, in which every step was connected. This journey, which started from the hospital, ended with the discovery of the body at Chiutaha cremation ground and the cremation a few hours later. According to the investigation, the constable met the girl around 9:30 PM on Tuesday night. Police estimate that the abduction and incident began around 10:02 PM. After this, the constable took the girl on his bike and left the hospital. After committing the murder, the constable was seen returning on his bike at high speed CCTV footage played the most crucial role in the investigation. The accused's bike was continuously captured by cameras installed from the District Hospital to Shastri Chowk, Kacheri, Town Hall, Khoonipur, Laldiggi, and Domingarh Maheshrapul. In every footage, the girl is seen sitting behind the constable. At 11:07 PM, she was last seen alive near Domingarh Maheshrapur Bridge. After that, no picture of her was captured by any camera. The footage also revealed that after the incident, the constable reached his home in Police Lines via Mohripur, Bargadwa, Lachhipur, 10 Number Boring, Gorakhnath Overbridge, and Dharamshala. For this, one team was engaged in scanning cameras on the route from the District Hospital, and another team was scanning cameras from Gorakhnath to Maheshra Bridge. According to investigation officials, the constable appeared completely normal while going, whereas his bike's speed was quite high while returning. The police have secured all the footage as electronic evidence. Constable kept mobile switched off for 9 hours, a well-planned conspiracy The investigation revealed that Constable Abhishek Yadav switched off his mobile phone at 9 PM, just before the incident. He switched the phone back on at 6 AM on July 29 (Wednesday). In the Call Detail Record (CDR) and location analysis, the last active location of the mobile was found near the district hospital. The police have seized the mobile and sent it for forensic examination. Investigating officers believe that switching off the mobile before the incident points towards a pre-planned conspiracy to hide electronic evidence and evade police surveillance. Control Room Remained Active, Delay Occurred in Action at Outpost Level On Tuesday night at 12:52 AM, the child's father informed the control room. Within just 10 minutes, the police became active. At 1:03 AM, the control room team reached the hospital. Despite this, the local police outpost arrived at the scene around 11 AM on Wednesday. Half an hour later, the Kotwali police started the investigation. The FIR was registered on Wednesday at 2:02 PM. This delay at the initial stage is also being considered a crucial point of investigation. Meanwhile, about 36 hours after the abduction, the girl's body was found at Chiutaha cremation ground on Thursday (July 30) at 6:30 AM. Then at 7:30 AM, she was brought to the district hospital, where doctors declared her dead at 7:45 AM. The post-mortem was conducted at 2:30 PM. At 5:45 PM, the body was taken directly to Rajghat, where the last rites were performed. DNA Sent for Investigation CO Kotwali Onkar Dutt Tiwari said that a case diary is now being prepared to strengthen the prosecution. CCTV footage, mobile's digital trail, forensic evidence found at the crime scene, recovery memo, and witness statements will be made the main basis in the charge sheet. After the DNA and other scientific investigation reports arrive, the investigation will be finalized. The DNA samples of the girl and the accused constable have been sent to Lucknow for examination. Officials say that only important witnesses will be included to strengthen the chain of evidence in court. Action against Station In-charge and Outpost In-charge In the case of the kidnapping and murder of an innocent from the district hospital, SSP Dr. Kaustubh on Friday immediately transferred Kotwali Station House Officer Inspector Chhatrapal Singh to the police line. Meanwhile, Nagar Nigam Chowki in-charge woman sub-inspector Deepshikha was suspended for gross indifference and negligence found in her duties.

stories.title: BJP’s major election-year move:₹1,500 pension for women and elderly in UP to directly benefit 11.8 million people
stories.summary: Just before the UP assembly elections, the Yogi government has made a big political move. The government is preparing to provide significant relief to more than 1.18 crore pension beneficiaries in the state. These include the elderly, widows, destitute women, and persons with disabilities. In the monsoon session of the legislature, starting from August 4, Finance Minister Suresh Khanna will present a supplementary budget of about ₹20,000 crore for the financial year 2026-27. It will include a provision for an increase of ₹500 per month in these pension schemes. Pension will increase from ₹1000 to ₹1500 Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath had said in the assembly on February 13, 2016: The elderly and destitute women have the right to live with dignity. Therefore, they should receive ₹1500 per month in pension. Finance Minister Suresh Khanna will announce this in two days. However, due to political reasons, the Finance Minister did not announce it in the budget session. On June 15, 2026, the Chief Minister wrote a letter to the public. This occasion was 'World Elder Abuse Awareness Day'. In this, he announced a pension of ₹1500. To know when the increased pension will be available, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to an official of the Social Welfare Department. He states, "After the budget provision is made, the increased pension amount will be transferred to the accounts. Budget provision can be made in the supplementary budget. An official of the Department for Persons with Disabilities stated that the disability pension can also be increased by ₹500. Additional funds will also be allocated for the Rani Lakshmibai Scooty Scheme A provision of ₹400 crore was made in Budget 2026-27 for distributing scooters to meritorious girl students. However, the scheme includes the top 5 per cent of girl students from state/private universities and colleges. These girl students from families with an annual income of up to ₹12 lakh will also receive a helmet, 4 liters of petrol, free registration, and insurance along with the scooter. As the ₹400 crore amount is insufficient, a demand for additional funds will be made for this in the supplementary budget. Land acquisition worth ₹10000 crore for four new expressways and link routes The government is preparing to lay a large network of connectivity from West to Purvanchal before the elections. This is expected to create a favourable atmosphere in the election year. For the groundbreaking of new expressways to be built on EPC mode, 70% of the land is required. For this, a budget proposal of about ₹10000 crore will be made. Know what experts say 'Pension increased 5 times in Yogi government compared to SP' Political analyst Virendranath Bhatt believes - now less than 6 months are left for the elections. In the election year, the decision to increase the pension given to women by ₹500 can benefit the BJP. During the SP government, widow, destitute women, and disabled persons' pensions were given ₹300 every month. So far, the government has increased the pension by more than 3 times. If this amount is increased by ₹500 in the supplementary budget, it will be a 5-fold increase during the Yogi government's tenure.

stories.title: UP drought alert:28 districts face up to 78% rain deficit as questions loom over August–September recovery
stories.summary: Half of the monsoon season has passed, but 28 districts in UP are facing drought-like conditions. Among these, Purvanchal accounts for the highest number with 19 districts. According to official figures, the state received 27 per cent less rainfall than normal between 1 June and 31 July. Whereas, in April, the Meteorological Department (IMD) had predicted 8 per cent to 10 per cent less rainfall for this season (June 1 to September 30). There is also a significant difference in rainfall between Eastern and Western UP. Will the August-September rainfall quota be met, or will the drought conditions worsen? Question-1: What was the rainfall situation in the initial two months of monsoon? Answer- Question-2: Compared to June, July received much better rainfall, right? Answer: Yes, despite El Nino, July saw better rainfall compared to June. By the end of June, UP had received 60% less rainfall. Thirty-four districts of the state were in the grip of 'severe drought'. However, due to good rainfall in July, the number of severely drought-affected districts has reduced to 13. The rainfall deficit has also decreased to 27 per cent. El Nino is expected to strengthen further in August-September. Question-3: If El Nio has formed, how did July receive good rainfall? Answer: According to Dr. K.J. Ramesh, former Director General of IMD, there were two reasons behind this: First- The Pacific Ocean water near the Philippines warmed unusually. The cyclonic circulations that arose from this moved through Myanmar, forming strong low-pressure areas in the Bay of Bengal and supporting the monsoon. Second- A stronger-than-normal Western Disturbance, which drew heavy moisture from the Arabian Sea. This led to a flood-like situation in Assam. Due to these very systems, rainfall was also better in Western UP compared to Eastern UP. Western UP- It directly benefited from active Western Disturbances. Moisture from the Arabian Sea reached Western UP via Gujarat-Rajasthan. This is why the Saharanpur-Muzaffarnagar-Meerut belt has been experiencing continuous heavy rainfall recently. The rainfall deficit has narrowed to just 13-15 per cent. Eastern UP- The low-pressure area forming in the Bay of Bengal primarily impacts Odisha, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal, and Assam. By the time they reach Eastern UP, their effect diminishes. This is why Purvanchal has received 34 per cent less rainfall than its quota. Question- 4: How much rainfall is estimated for August-September? Answer: August- According to IMD's August-September forecast issued on July 31, there are indications of heavy rainfall in some parts of UP between August 2 and 4. Initially, eastern UP will receive slightly less rainfall. However, later the monsoon might intensify here. Some border districts of western UP (Uttarakhand-adjacent areas like Saharanpur, Bijnor) have a possibility of normal or slightly above normal rainfall. Across UP, including plain areas like Meerut, Moradabad, Bareilly, Agra, Aligarh, there are chances of below-normal rainfall in the remaining monsoon season. September- Atul Kumar Singh, a scientist at the Regional Meteorological Centre, states: UP is likely to receive 6% less rainfall than normal in August-September. Temperatures may remain above normal. This means that along with a deficit in rainfall, humidity and heat both may persist. Nights (minimum temperatures) may also be warmer than normal. The situation looks even weaker for Eastern UP. Apart from areas bordering the state's northeastern border (like districts bordering Nepal such as Balrampur, Shravasti), large parts like Gorakhpur, Varanasi, Prayagraj, Azamgarh are expected to receive less than normal rainfall. Temperatures are likely to remain above normal across Eastern UP. This means both day and night will be hot. This creates a more concerning situation for Eastern UP. stories.title: 'If you get pregnant, I’m not to blame':Maulana tells female reporter, 'If you follow the law, you are a stain on Muslims' | WATCH Halala sting Part-2
stories.summary: “Halala is a punishment for men, not for women. If you follow the police law, you will become a disgrace to the name of Muslim.” This is Maulana Rahmatullah, who is brainwashing a female reporter of Dainik Bhaskar in Gorakhpur, UP, so that she agrees to halala and establishes physical relations with the Maulana. In Part-1 of Operation Halala, you read how Maulanas are working like a gang for halala (i.e., when a divorced woman marries another man, completes the marriage, and gets divorced again so she can legally remarry her first husband) Today, in Part-2 of the Investigation, read how these Maulanas mislead Muslim women by misinforming them about the police, the law, and Quran to fulfil their sexual desires. Maulana Rahmatullah, who claimed to be from a Pir family, had asked us to bring a divorced woman. We called the Maulana. Introducing the female reporter as a divorced woman, we reached the Maulana's shop in Raiganj, Gorakhpur. Female Reporter: My husband divorced me. Only the two of us know this; still, do I have to undergo halala? Rahmatullah: It doesn't matter if only the two of you know. You are divorced; God is a witness to this. Despite the triple talaq, you people are together. This is a greater sin than that. Reporter: Can't we live together? Rahmatullah: It's not about living together. For example, you people are roaming together, aren't you? So my master says - if a divorce happens, she should immediately go into purdah. Reporter: I want to know with whom her marriage should be solemnised; how will this happen? Rehmatullah: Look, what happens is that most marriages are performed with Maulanas or scholars because they have children. It is not done with bachelors. It should be done with a man who will divorce her after one or two days, so that the trust with which the other person came remains intact. Now it depends on her whether she sits with him, sleeps with him, or does anything else. You cannot refuse. You cannot put him under pressure. Because after marriage, they become husband and wife. Female Reporter: If the nikah happens, will I have to live with you? Rahmatullah: It depends on us. If conditions are set, what will be the meaning of Sharia? That's why I'm saying, get halala done by a sensible man. Let me give an example - suppose the nikah happened. Now, if I live with you every day, my wife and children will ask where I live? We are afraid of that. One who isn't afraid will live a life of luxury. Now, it's not necessary that I call you and say, 'Come, I want to sleep with you.' It's up to our will whether we stay for 1-2 or 5 days. It means that just as you lived with your first husband, you should live with us. But it's not like you can say on the very first night that you don't want to live with us. That would be wrong. After this, Maulana Rehmatullah sent the Bhaskar reporter out and started talking to the female reporter alone. Female Reporter: We are spending money. We will spend some more money, but let there be no physical relations. Rehmatullah: No, that won't happen. That would be wrong. Actually, this is a punishment for the man. A woman sometimes finds a better husband even after triple talaq. Female Reporter: But, isn't this the right punishment for the woman? Rahmatullah: No, this is not a punishment for women. Female Reporter: Okay, a law has been made regarding triple talaq. Will that not cause any problem? Rahmatullah: Will you follow the Quran or the law? If you follow the law, then go follow the law. But then the same thing will happen; you will become a stain on the name of Muslims. Female Reporter: Will it not be a police matter? Rahmatullah: Nothing, when it's a matter between four people, where will the fifth come from? Female Reporter: What if she gets pregnant? Rahmatullah: If the wife says she doesn't want a child, the husband gets an abortion done. Then when I divorce you, what connection will I have with you? You are its owner. You know, you mind your own business. Then I am not a sinner. Experts said Halala comes under the category of rape Dr. Syed Rizwan Ahmed, an expert on issues related to the Muslim religion and a Supreme Court advocate, stated- When 'talaq' is pronounced three times in anger at once, it is called Talaq-e-Biddat. It is here that 'halala' is added. But 'halala' falls into the category of rape. The reason for this is that the conditions for rape clearly state that if a woman gives consent but does not have the desire or will, and physical intimacy occurs with her, then it is rape. Therefore, a case of rape can be filed even after marriage. Similarly, a woman might agree to halala, but she can never desire it. If she desires it, then she is not fit to be a wife. If she desires it with another man today, she will desire it with a third tomorrow.

stories.title: Ghaziabad sub-inspector Asmita Dey scripts history with judo gold:Judoka beat Canadian in final, thanks UP CM Yogi for police job
stories.summary: Ghaziabad's Sub-Inspector Asmita Dey won a gold medal at the Commonwealth Games-2026 on Friday. She defeated a Canadian player in judo. Asmita Dey is a resident of Tripura and is a Sub-Inspector in the UP Police. After winning the gold, Asmita Dey said, "I am in the UP Police. I want to thank CM Yogi ji because he gave me a job in the UP Police. This job gave me support. It is because of this that I reached here and was able to win the gold medal." Initially trailed, then made a spectacular comeback The start of the final match was not easy for Asmita Dey. Canada's Hady Quach took an early lead by scoring a yuko point. Asmita also received a shido penalty. Despite this, she did not give up and made a brilliant comeback to level the score at 1-1. No player could score a decisive point until the stipulated time, so the match went into golden score. Here, Asmita made a brilliant move at the right moment and scored a second yuko point, winning both the match and the gold medal. Before reaching the final, Asmita had put up a brilliant performance by defeating Scotland's Eva Ewing and Summer Shaw. Asmita said - Yogi ji's support gave me strength Asmita said - Her father passed away in December 2025. My father always supported me. After he left, I felt like everything was over. But two months later, the Asian Games trials took place, in which I secured the first position at the national level. After winning the gold medal, Asmita Dey said - This medal is very important for me, my state, and my country. I dedicate it to my coach and my father. I am very happy with this gold medal. This is for all those people who supported me. She also thanked CM Yogi. Chose Judo over 800-meter race Asmita Dey, a resident of Belonia, Tripura, was initially an 800-meter runner. During a district-level trial, her interest in Judo grew. After that, she left athletics and made Judo her sport, continuously working hard. Asmita trained under the supervision of coach Yashpal Solanki at the Sports Authority of India (SAI) Regional Centre in Bhopal. Currently, she is part of the Development Group of the central government's Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) and is representing India at the international level. Had to stay hungry to maintain weight Asmita also shared the struggle of random weigh-in (weight check) before the championship match. She said that she had to stay hungry in the morning. She said she couldn't eat much because, in a random weigh-in, as the weight should be less than 50 kg. When she woke up in the morning, her weight was 50 kg 300 grams and so she didn't eat anything. When her name came up for the random weigh-in, only then did she eat and drink after the formality was completed, and her fight was just one hour after that. DGP said - Asmita enhanced the pride of UP Police and the country Uttar Pradesh Director General of Police (DGP) Rajiv Krishna congratulated Asmita Dey on winning the gold medal. He said that Asmita Dey has brought glory to UP Police, the state and the entire country by winning gold in the women's 48 kg judo event. This is an excellent example of their success, discipline, hard work, and determination. This achievement is also a result of CM Yogi's policy of promoting sports talents. By providing jobs to players in UP Police through sports quota, they have got an opportunity to excel in both sports and service. India in 10th Position in Commonwealth Games India's performance in the Commonwealth Games 2026 is continuously improving. So far, Indian players have won 23 medals, including five gold, 10 silver, and six bronze medals. With this performance, India has reached the ninth position in the medal tally. India have reached the 10th position in the Commonwealth Games medal tally.

stories.title: UP Madrasas to lose Kamil and Fazil degree status:Existing qualifications also to be invalidated; Yogi cabinet set to clear 21+ proposals tomorrow
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government is set to prohibit madrasas from awarding Kamil (graduate-level) and Fazil (postgraduate-level) degrees, saying the move is in line with a Supreme Court ruling. A proposal to amend the Uttar Pradesh Madrasa Education Board Act, 2004 will be placed before the Yogi Adityanath Cabinet at its meeting on Tuesday. Minority Welfare Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar said- Kamil and Fazil degrees previously awarded by madrasas will also be invalidated. Decision based on SC ruling A senior official from the Minority Welfare Department said the proposal follows the Supreme Court's judgment of 5 November 2024 in the Anjum Qadri and Others vs Union of India case. The Supreme Court overturned the Allahabad High Court's earlier ruling, which had declared the Uttar Pradesh Madrasa Education Board Act, 2004 unconstitutional. While upholding the constitutional validity of the Act, the apex court clarified that madrasas cannot award formal higher education qualifications such as Kamil and Fazil, as these fall outside the regulatory framework of the University Grants Commission (UGC). Cabinet to meet on Tuesday; 21 proposals on Agenda The Cabinet meeting will be held at 9.30 am on Tuesday at the Chief Minister's official residence. Chief Secretary S.P. Goyal released the agenda on Monday evening, listing 21 proposals, with the possibility of additional items being added before the meeting. The Cabinet is also expected to consider a supplementary Budget exceeding ₹40,000 crore for the 2026–27 financial year. What are Kamil and Fazil degrees? Kamil A three-year course in Arabic, Persian and Islamic studies. Previously treated by the Madrasa Board as equivalent to a Bachelor's degree (BA). Fazil A two-year advanced course undertaken after Kamil. Previously treated as equivalent to a Master's degree (MA). U-Hubs Proposed for Lucknow and Noida The Cabinet is also expected to approve the establishment of U-Hubs in Lucknow and Noida. According to the Information Technology and Electronics Department, the state government has recently approved the creation of a Startup Mission Directorate. As part of this initiative, a government-owned company named U-Hub will be established. The centres will be developed at IIT Kanpur's Noida Centre and the IIT Lucknow campus. The primary objective is to provide infrastructure, mentoring and institutional support to technology startups looking to scale their businesses. The government has allocated ₹100 crore for the initiative during the current financial year. The Director of IIT Kanpur Incubation Centre has also been appointed Director of U-Hub for a three-year term. Other key proposals before the cabinet The Cabinet is also expected to consider approval of the Sheera Policy 2026, implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana for Kharif and Rabi crops, and the creation of the Prayagraj–Chitrakoot Regional Development Authority for the integrated development of the region. Main agenda items Crop insurance schemes: Approval for implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana and the Weather-Based Crop Insurance Scheme for Kharif 2026 and Rabi 2026–27. Seven multi-purpose hubs: The Public Works Department will acquire land and transfer it free of cost to the Housing and Urban Planning Department for construction of seven multi-purpose hubs. New service rules: Introduction of the State Property Department Service Rules, 2026. HCL Foundation agreement: Proposal to extend the government's partnership with the HCL Foundation for community development projects by another five years. Prayagraj–Chitrakoot Development Authority: Creation of a new authority for the planned development of the region. Nomadic Development Board: Formation of a board for the social and economic development of denotified, nomadic and semi-nomadic communities. Vishwakarma Shram Samman Yojana-2: Amendments to the scheme and inclusion of new provisions. Jewar Link Expressway: Proposal to construct a 74.467-km six-lane greenfield expressway connecting Jewar Airport with the Ganga Expressway. Molasses law amendment: Introduction of the Uttar Pradesh Molasses Control (Amendment) Bill, 2026. Labour Code Rules, 2026: Implementation of new labour regulations. Withdrawal of old legislation: Proposal to withdraw the Building and Other Construction Workers (Amendment) Bill, 2020 from the Central Government. Madrasa law amendment: Amendments to the Madrasa Education Board Act, 2004 in line with the Supreme Court judgment. Kamil and Fazil degrees: Formal recognition of these qualifications will be discontinued. Mining service rules: Implementation of the Department of Geology and Mining Service Rules, 2026. U-Hubs in Lucknow and Noida: Establishment of technology hubs focused on deep-tech and high-potential startups. Relief for electronics company: Proposal to extend the deadline for iQOO Solutions to commence its project. CAG reports: Presentation of several Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) reports relating to state finances, MGNREGA, the Jal Jeevan Mission and other departments. Supplementary Budget: Presentation of supplementary grants and the Appropriation Bill for the 2026–27 financial year.

stories.title: Dalit man urinates on Shiva idol:Says, 'Do whatever you can'; police pick him up from home two hours later
stories.summary: In Bulandshahr, a 55-year-old Dalit man urinated on a Shivling on the first Monday of Sawan. The accused said, ‘Do whatever you want to do’. A youth from the village made a video of him and made it viral on social media. The incident occurred around 7 AM. Police reached the village 4 hours after the video surfaced. The elderly man and the person who made the video were taken from their homes. A case has also been registered against both. Complete incident in 3 pictures He reached near the idol of Shiva built near the temple's spire. He told the young man, ‘Here, make a video.’ Read the full incident in sequence Shiva temple 35 years old Bohich village is located in Shikarpur police station area, about 25 km from the district headquarters. There is a 35-year-old Shiva temple here. A large idol of Lord Shiva is installed on the temple's roof. There are stairs to go to the temple's roof. Hari Prasad Kumar (55)'s house is 200 meters away from the temple. He is a mason. On Monday morning around 7 AM, he reached the temple. He went up the stairs and urinated near the feet of Lord Shiva's idol. His entire act was recorded on phone by Pappu (45), a resident of the same village. Accused said that what will you do? After urinating, Hari Prasad got up from there and said to Pappu, who was making the video, I peed, what will you do? Make the video viral. What can anyone do? About 2 hours after this incident, around 10 am, anger spread among the people of the village and surrounding areas. People expressed strong displeasure over this incident that occurred on the first Monday of Sawan and demanded strict action against the accused. Police reached village as soon as video went viral As soon as information about the video was received, Shikarpur police immediately swung into action. Around 12 PM, the police team reached the village and took accused Hariprasad and Pappu, who made the video, into custody and brought them to the police station. Police have started questioning both of them. SSP said - Strict action will be taken SSP Dinesh Kumar Singh stated that both accused have been taken into custody and are being interrogated. After investigating the matter, strict action will be taken based on evidence. He appealed to the public not to pay attention to rumors and to maintain peace. Police are also investigating what was the motive behind making the video viral. Was it planned? Also, it is being investigated whether any other person played a role in making the video viral on social media or not. After the incident, police surveillance has been increased in the village as a precautionary measure.

stories.title: Dog fights with Cobra to save owner's life, dies:Battles with snake for an hour in Ballia, scummbs to death after killing
stories.summary: A Labrador dog in Ballia sacrificed its life to save its owner's family from a cobra. Around 2 AM on Sunday night, the dog spotted a cobra outside the house. The cobra was hissing with its hood spread. After this, the dog started barking continuously. During this, the cobra attacked the dog. Then the dog also grabbed the cobra. The snake kept attacking, but the dog did not let go. The struggle between the two continued for about an hour, while the family members watched and made videos of this fight. Finally, the dog killed the cobra. However, in this fight, the dog also fell victim to the cobra's venom. After 30 minutes, the dog also died. A video of this entire incident has also surfaced. The incident is from the Belthara Road area. First, watch the dog-cobra fight Now know the full story Danish lived with his family in Ubhanv village. He runs a brick kiln. Danish had a Labrador dog named Tommy at his home for 8 years. On Sunday night, a cobra snake was trying to enter Danish's house. Tommy first spotted the cobra. After this, Tommy started barking continuously. Hearing Tommy's noise, Danish and his family also woke up. Meanwhile, Tommy himself confronted the cobra. According to Danish's family members, a fierce struggle ensued between Tommy and the snake for about an hour. Tommy severely gripped the cobra. The cobra also put all its might to escape from Tommy's clutches. In this sequence, the cobra bit Tommy several times. But, Tommy did not give up. He killed the cobra. Tommy also died half an hour after killing the cobra During the fight with the cobra, the effect of the poison rapidly increased in Tommy's body. Half an hour later, he also passed away. The family says that if Tommy hadn't shown bravery, the snake would have entered the house and bitten anyone. Tommy saved the entire family by sacrificing his life. Tommy had been living as a family member for the past 8 years. Every member of the family is deeply shocked by his death. On Monday, the family bid a tearful farewell to Tommy. Many family members became emotional while burying him.

stories.title: No bulldozer action on Jauhar University as of now:Moradabad Commissioner's Court halts demolition of 38 buildings after 2.5-hour hearing
stories.summary: No demolition action will be taken against the 38 buildings of Rampur's Jauhar University while the matter remains pending before the court. The order was issued by the court of Moradabad Divisional Commissioner Anjaneya Kumar Singh at 4.45 pm on Monday, following a hearing that lasted around two and a half hours. The next hearing has been scheduled for 10 August. Earlier stay on demolition order The Commissioner's Court had previously heard the matter on 27 July, when it stayed the demolition order issued by the Vice-Chairman of the Rampur Development Authority (RDA) and the District Magistrate against the university's 38 buildings. The next hearing was then fixed for 3 August. University challenged RDA order The university management filed an appeal before the Commissioner's Court on 20 July, challenging the demolition order issued by the RDA Vice-Chairman. The hearing was originally scheduled for 28 July. However, following the death of an advocate in Moradabad, the day was declared a day of mourning. As a result, the university's counsel, Junaid Ejaz, moved an application on 27 July, requesting an earlier hearing. The Commissioner accepted the application and stayed the demolition order. Jauhar Trust challenges demolition order Junaid Ejaz, counsel for Jauhar University, said the Rampur Development Authority had issued the demolition order on 15 July, prompting the university to file an appeal before the Commissioner's Court. According to Ejaz, Monday's hearing lasted for about one hour and 45 minutes, during which both sides presented detailed arguments. After hearing the submissions, the matter was reserved for orders. He further said the Commissioner had orally observed that no demolition would take place while the appeal remained pending. The Divisional Commissioner has also sought a response from the RDA on the issues raised in the appeal and may summon additional records, including approved building plans, from the university if required. RDA says only two buildings were approved RDA Vice-Chairman Ajay Kumar Dwivedi issued an order on 15 July, declaring 38 of the university's 40 buildings to be unauthorised and directing that they be demolished. According to the RDA, the Jauhar Trust had obtained approval for only two buildings, while construction plans for the remaining 38 buildings had never been sanctioned. As the university campus falls within the jurisdiction of the Rampur Development Authority, all construction is governed by RDA regulations. Government Lawyer: No written order yet Government counsel Dinesh Chauhan said both parties presented their arguments before the court on Monday. He said the university's lawyer argued on behalf of the institution, while he represented the state government. After hearing both sides, the court reserved its decision but had not yet issued any written order. Chauhan added that the court may pass a final order, seek additional reports or issue further directions, and all subsequent action would depend on the written order. He stressed that only a written judicial order has legal validity and that it would be inappropriate to draw conclusions based solely on oral observations until the court formally issues its decision.

stories.title: SP to donate ₹47,000 to Ram Mandir:Dimple Yadav counts cash in Parliament; Ayodhya MP displays bundle of notes, says 'This will not be stolen'
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party (SP) MPs staged a protest outside Parliament at Makar Gate over the alleged theft of offerings from the Ayodhya Ram Temple. During the demonstration, SP leaders collected donations from MPs belonging to the INDIA bloc. The donations were then counted in full public view. MP Ram Shiromani Verma counted the cash with assistance from Dharmendra Yadav, while Akshay Pratap recorded the names of donors in a register. Dimple Yadav oversaw the counting process, and Ayodhya MP Awadhesh Prasad supervised the exercise. A total of ₹47,100 was collected. Dharmendra Yadav said every rupee had been accounted for to ensure complete transparency. The money was then handed over to Awadhesh Prasad, who said the entire amount would be sent directly to the Ram Temple in Ayodhya. Understand the protest in 6 pictures- Awadhesh Prasad: 'Not a single penny will be stolen' Speaking to the media, Awadhesh Prasad displayed bundles of cash and said- This money will not be stolen. It is an offering for the temple of Lord Shri Ram. Every one of our MPs has contributed. I take full responsibility that not a single penny from this amount will be stolen. Earlier on Monday, both Houses of Parliament witnessed noisy scenes, forcing the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha to be adjourned for the entire day. Dimple Yadav targets BJP and RSS Dimple Yadav accused the BJP and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) of trying to impose their ideology on women. Referring to a recent protest movement, she claimed it had ended after assurances that no FIRs would be registered against students or young women. However, she alleged that cases were later filed, accusing the government of reneging on its promise and betraying the public. Questions raised over Ram temple donations Dimple Yadav also questioned the management of donations made to the Ram Temple. She asked where anonymous cash donations, precious metals and other offerings had gone, and which organisations were benefiting from them. She questioned why the government had not disclosed these details publicly and why members of the temple trust had not been removed despite the allegations. According to her, public confidence in the government had eroded, and the government was fully responsible for the alleged donation theft and land-related irregularities. SP distances itself from Pappu Yadav's protest The Samajwadi Party distanced itself from the separate protest staged by Independent MP Pappu Yadav inside the Parliament complex. SP MP Ram Gopal Yadav said- That was wrong. Saints have nothing to do with the alleged theft at the Ram Temple. It should not have happened. He added that the party would raise the alleged theft of temple donations inside Parliament, describing it as a serious issue. Pappu Yadav stages protest dressed as a Sadhu On the 10th day of the Monsoon Session, Independent MP Pappu Yadav arrived at Parliament dressed as a saffron-clad sadhu carrying a donation box. A symbolic street play was staged inside the Parliament complex to protest against the alleged theft of Ram Temple offerings. Pappu Yadav, dressed as a priest, sat on the ground while Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and several opposition MPs placed donations into the collection drive. During the protest, Pappu Yadav was also seen keeping some donated cash with himself instead of placing it in the donation box. He was also seen touching the feet of Ayodhya MP Awadhesh Prasad. FIR registered against Rahul Gandhi, Pappu Yadav and Awadhesh Prasad An FIR has been registered in Varanasi against Congress MP Rahul Gandhi, SP MP Awadhesh Prasad and Independent MP Pappu Yadav over the protest concerning the alleged theft of Ram Temple offerings. The complaint was filed by Jagadguru Balak Das, head priest of Patalpuri Math, at the Kotwali police station.

stories.title: Video|Pole falls on schoolgirl's head, dies within 3 seconds:Friend narrowly escapes; was returning home from local shop
stories.summary: A Class 9 student walking along a road in Hardoi dies within three seconds after an electric pole snaps and falls on her head. Her friend, who is walking beside her, hears the pole cracking and steps forward just in time, escaping unharmed. The girl remains trapped under the pole for about 25 seconds before passersby use bamboo to lift it and pull her out. However, she has already succumbed to her injuries. The incident occurs in Bhihgaon, Behta Gokul, at around 6:30 pm on Sunday, and CCTV footage of the accident emerges today. 2 visuals of the accident Understand the entire incident sequentially Ajay Shukla lives with his family in Bhigaon, under the Behta Gokul police station area. Besides his wife Sadhana, there are 6 children in the house. Among them, Ragini (14) was the second eldest. She was a class nine student at Chandrasen Singh Munni Devi Inter College. Pandey Kirana Store is about 200 meters away from Ragini's house. Here, on Sunday evening, a DCM truck arrived loaded with Gyandhara feed. The DCM driver was moving the vehicle forward to unload the goods. Just then, an overhead electricity cable got entangled in the DCM's angle. The wire was pulled with such force that the electricity pole bent towards the road and broke. Just then, Ragini came into its path. She had gone out with her friend Kamini to buy something from this very shop. What is visible in the video? Both friends were walking hand-in-hand. As soon as the wire stretched and the sound of the pole breaking came, Kamini screamed and let go of Ragini's hand, moving forward. Meanwhile, Ragini, out of fear, remained standing in her spot to save herself. In just three seconds, the pole broke and fell directly on her head. As soon as it came under pole, her head burst. After the accident, there was chaos at the spot. Fearing electrocution, people initially stood at a distance. After about 25 seconds, two people lifted the pole with the help of bamboo. One person pulled the student out from under the pole. As soon as the news of the accident was received, the student's family members rushed to the spot. Mother started crying The entire family was in a state of distress, crying inconsolably. Mother Sadhana started crying, clinging to her daughter's body. She kept saying that she had just sent her daughter to get some things. After the accident, hearing the commotion, the DCM driver abandoned the vehicle and fled the scene. The police sent the body for post-mortem. Station House Officer Markandey Singh said- Police are also including CCTV footage in the investigation. A complaint has been received from the family members. Action will be taken against the accused DCM driver.

Haryanvi dancers perform at BJP MLA's event in Mathura:Supporters shower cash on two performers; children were also present
stories.summary: Haryanvi dancers performed at an event linked to BJP MLA Meghshyam Singh in Mathura, where supporters were seen showering notes on the performers. Several videos of the programme surfaced on Monday, showing two dancers performing on stage. However, BJP District President Harishankar Yadav denied it was an official party or MLA event, claiming it had been organised by local residents. The programme was held on 1 August in Janu village, where Govardhan MLA Meghshyam Singh attended a foundation stone-laying ceremony for development projects worth around ₹2.5 crore. Haryanvi dancers Sanjana Chaudhary and Bhavna Bhati were invited to entertain the audience. See pictures of the Haryanvi dancer- Now know what is visible in the video- The foundation stone-laying ceremony was organised for development works worth approximately ₹2.5 crore in Janu village under the Govardhan Assembly constituency. As part of the event, two Haryanvi dancers performed on stage. The videos show large crowds, including men, women and children, watching the performances. DJ music, including songs with explicit lyrics, was played throughout the programme. At several points, members of the audience joined the dancers on stage, while children were also seen climbing onto the platform. Many attendees recorded the performances on their mobile phones. Foundation stones for the development works were visible in front of the stage, while several people were seen showering bundles of banknotes on the performers. MLA could not be contacted In this matter, an attempt was made to contact BJP MLA Meghshyam Singh to know his side, but it was not possible to speak with him. No reaction has come from his side either. Meanwhile, supporters of the MLA say that it was merely an entertainment program. It should not be viewed from a political perspective. Meanwhile, BJP Metropolitan President Harishankar Yadav Raju said, "This was not a party program. It must have been organized by local people. Neither the MLA nor party workers were present in it. I cannot say anything about what the local people did." People said - one should find some way to entertain oneself After the video surfaced, various reactions are being seen on social media regarding it. In the comment box of a video shared on a Facebook account named Rajesh Kumar Satyamev, a user wrote, "The MLA's heart must be appeased somehow." Meanwhile, another user wrote, "The MLA did not dance." Another user called it having a negative impact on the youth.

stories.title: Mother-son held hostage in broad daylight:Thieves loot jewellery worth lakhs and ₹15,000 cash at gunpoint in Kanpur
stories.summary: Armed robbers carried out a daylight burglary in Kanpur's Chakeri area on Monday, holding a woman and her 16-year-old son hostage at gunpoint before fleeing with jewellery worth lakhs of rupees and ₹15,000 in cash. The incident took place at around 12 noon at the home of Rachna Tripathi in C Block, Shyamnagar. The robbers allegedly threatened Tripathi and her son, Devansh, with firearms before ransacking the house and escaping with valuables. Following the incident, ADCP (East) Shiva Singh, Chakeri police and a forensic team reached the scene. Police have launched an investigation.

stories.title: Father kills daughter over marriage to soldier:Strangles her with dupatta in Agra, sends wife and son away; sits beside body
stories.summary: An honor killing has occurred in Agra. Here, a father strangled his 22-year-old daughter to death. The reason is that the daughter had a court marriage with an ITBP jawan. On Sunday night at 12 AM, the father beat his daughter in front of his wife and son, then strangled her with a chunari (scarf). After the incident, he sent his wife and son away and sat crying near the body himself. Meanwhile, hearing the screams, the police were called. When the police went inside, the daughter was lying on the floor in a pool of blood. When the police asked the accused father the reason for the incident, he confessed to the crime. He said - 4 months ago, his daughter had a love marriage against the family's wishes, which is why he killed her. Currently, the police have arrested him. The entire incident is from the Jaitpur police station area, 80 km away from the district headquarters. The victim's name is Ankita Sharma (24). Family lives in a rented house Vimal Sharma had been living in a rented house in Nahtauli village of Jaitpur for the past 15 years. Vimal worked at a shop. His family included his wife Sita, son Ankush, and daughter Ankita. Ankita had an affair with Amit Pachauri, a resident of the village. Amit is deployed as a soldier in ITBP. Both wanted to get married, but the family was not ready for it. Going against her family, Ankita had a court marriage with Amit 4 months ago, against her family's wishes. After the marriage, Amit returned to duty, while Ankita continued to live with her parents. Her family members were upset about her love marriage. According to the police, Vimal went to his daughter's room at 12 AM on Sunday night and assaulted her. During this, neighbors heard Ankita screaming and informed the police by dialing 112. When the police arrived at the scene, Ankita's body was found in the room. DCP East Abhishek Agarwal said- The body has been sent for post-mortem. The accused is being interrogated. Further action will be based on the investigation and post-mortem report.

stories.title: BJP's Tiranga Yatra to reach 20 lakh people:Processions across 110 Lucknow wards and 2,515 booths to promote patriotism and respect for the national flag
stories.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) will launch a large-scale Tiranga Yatra campaign in Lucknow from August 9. The campaign will cover all 110 wards, 25 mandals and 2,515 booths across the city. The party aims to reach around 20 lakh people through public outreach during the campaign. BJP workers will organise Tiranga Yatras, conduct door-to-door visits and inform people about the achievements of the Central and Uttar Pradesh governments. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will inaugurate BJP state vice-president Neeraj Singh, who is the state in-charge of the Tiranga Yatra campaign, said the formal launch will take place on August 9 under the leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. The main Tiranga Yatra will begin from the Chief Minister's residence at 5 Kalidas Marg and conclude at the Assembly (Lok Bhawan). Senior BJP leaders, public representatives, party workers and a large number of citizens will participate in the yatra. Will deliver government achievements to every household According to the BJP, workers will inform people about development projects, welfare schemes and major achievements of the Central and state governments since the BJP came to power at the Centre in 2014. The campaign will also spread the message of patriotism, national unity and respect for the Tricolour among citizens. Public Outreach Campaign at Every Booth After the main Tiranga Yatra, separate rallies will be organised across all 110 wards, 25 mandals and 2,515 booths in Lucknow. Workers at every booth will conduct door-to-door outreach and interact with local residents. The party aims to connect with around 20 lakh people through the campaign and further strengthen its organisation at the booth level. BJP has assigned responsibilities to office-bearers of all mandals and booths for the campaign.
