stories.title: One call saves ₹5.12 lakh in Varanasi:₹5.64 lakh siphoned off in 30 minutes; funds frozen after complaint to 1930, FIR registered
stories.summary: A man from Kumbhapur village in Varanasi's Badagaon police station area became a victim of online fraud. Cyber criminals withdrew ₹5,64,197 from his bank account in six transactions within just half an hour. As transaction messages started arriving on his mobile phone, the victim informed his family members. Without wasting time, they immediately called the cyber helpline. After providing the required details, the team managed to put ₹5,12,495 on hold, bringing relief to the family. The entire matter is from last week The incident took place on July 27 when sudden transactions started from the bank account of Ramesh Singh, a resident of Kumbhapur village. Ramesh said the fraudsters first withdrew ₹50,000 from his account. After this, ₹49,470, ₹81,351 and ₹1 lakh were deducted in multiple transactions. As he continued receiving messages, the fraudsters made two more withdrawals before he could take any action. They transferred ₹2,14,376 and later another ₹69,000 from his account. After this, Ramesh informed his family members, who immediately called the cyber helpline number 1930. The cyber team contacted the bank after receiving the complaint and got ₹5,12,495 frozen, preventing further loss. Police register case, begin investigation On Sunday evening, Ramesh submitted a complaint at Badagaon police station, demanding action against the fraudsters. Police have registered a case against unidentified accused under Section 318(4) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Officials are collecting bank transaction details to trace the cyber criminals. Badagaon Station House Officer Praveen Kumar Singh said that if money starts getting deducted from a bank account without the account holder's knowledge, people should not panic and must immediately report it by calling 1930.

stories.title: BSP hunts for candidates in Gorakhpur:Eyes rival party hopefuls; focus on five seats
stories.summary: With the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections approaching, the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) has intensified its search for candidates in Gorakhpur. Alongside strengthening its organisation, the party is identifying winnable faces for every Assembly constituency. The BSP is also reaching out to leaders from other parties who are unlikely to secure tickets from their own organisations. Party functionaries said details of potential candidates from every Assembly seat are currently being collected. Once the names are shortlisted, the list will be sent to the party leadership in Lucknow. No final decision has yet been taken for any constituency in the district. The BSP is simultaneously working on organisational strengthening and election preparations in Gorakhpur. After appointing three district presidents over the past five years, the party has also undergone organisational changes. District president Santosh Kumar Jigyasu said the organisational work is almost complete and the focus has now shifted entirely to selecting Assembly candidates. He said several aspirants have emerged from every constituency and their profiles are being assessed before recommending the strongest and most electable names to the state leadership. Maximum focus on these seats The BSP is currently focusing on Chillupar, Sahjanwa, Bansgaon, Khajni and Pipraich Assembly seats. All these constituencies are currently represented by BJP MLAs. With leaders from both BJP and Samajwadi Party also seeking tickets, the BSP is keeping an eye on those who have a low possibility of getting nominations from their own parties. A party office-bearer said several leaders have been seeking tickets for multiple elections but have not received an opportunity. This time, many of them are preparing to contest at any cost. Senior BSP leaders are also in talks with several such leaders. BSP was strong in 2007 and 2012 The BSP has had a strong electoral presence in Gorakhpur in the past. In the 2007 Assembly elections, when the BSP formed the government in Uttar Pradesh, the party won the Chillupar, Bansgaon, Kaudiram and Pipraich seats in the district. The Kaudiram Assembly seat was later removed during delimitation. In the 2012 Assembly elections, the BSP again held four seats in the district — Sahjanwa, Chillupar, Bansgaon and Chauri Chaura. The party is now trying to repeat its earlier performance in the upcoming Assembly elections.

stories.title: AI to be taught in 41 polytechnic engineering branches:Syllabus updated across state institutes; new curriculum to take effect from upcoming session
stories.summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) will now be a compulsory subject for students pursuing three-year diploma engineering courses in government, aided and private polytechnic institutes across Uttar Pradesh. From the 2026-27 academic session, AI has been included in the syllabus of all 41 diploma engineering programmes. Students in the first and second semesters will study the subject to prepare for evolving technologies. Updated syllabus will be implemented from new session Dr F.R. Khan, Director of the Institute of Research, Development and Training (IRDT), Kanpur, said the syllabus for all 41 diploma engineering courses has been revised to include a new AI unit. After being vetted by AKTU, the revised syllabus was sent to the Board of Technical Education, where the curriculum committee approved its implementation from the new academic session. He said a basic understanding of AI has become essential for students of every engineering discipline because of changing technological requirements. New units of IT and AI will be included The newly introduced unit has been titled Introduction to IT and AI. Besides introducing students to Artificial Intelligence, it will also cover cyber security and modern digital technologies. Experts said AI is no longer limited to computer science and information technology, but is increasingly being used in mechanical, electrical, civil, electronics and other engineering fields. Theory followed by practical training Students will study AI theory during the first and second semesters before moving on to practical sessions that teach them how to use AI tools. The syllabus includes topics such as Cyber Security Principles and Threats, Basic Protection Mechanisms, Cyber Security Practices, Fundamentals of AI, Prompt Engineering, Machine Learning and Deep Learning. During practical sessions, students will learn to use AI for preparing documents, creating videos and developing other forms of digital content.

stories.title: 5 silver crowns stolen from Panchmukhi Hanuman idol:Thieves take crowns and canopies from all temple idols after cutting four channel-gate locks
stories.summary: A theft took place at the Panchmukhi Hanuman Temple in Lucknow's Mahanagar area around 2 am on Sunday night. Thieves allegedly cut the temple lock and escaped with silver crowns and canopies worth lakhs. The theft came to light when the priest reached the temple to open it around 5:30 am and found the locks broken. Police and a forensic team later inspected the spot. Temple priest Dinesh Kumar Dixit said he found the locks lying open and the shutter partially raised. On entering the temple, he discovered that the silver crown and canopy of Lord Ganesha were missing. Further inside, he found that the silver crowns and canopies adorning the idols of Lord Ram, Lakshman and Sita had also been stolen. Five crowns of Panchmukhi Hanuman ji missing The priest then removed the curtain covering Panchmukhi Hanuman and found that all five silver crowns and the canopy placed over the deity were also missing. According to the priest, articles worth around ₹35-36 lakh were stolen. The thieves also took away the temple's CCTV system and DVR, making it difficult to identify them from the temple's own surveillance footage. The complaint has been filed by Pawan Kumar Sharma, son of the temple's founder, R.P. Sharma. Police said an FIR is being registered based on the complaint and nearby CCTV cameras are being examined to identify the accused.

stories.title: 'How many of you are Gen Z?':Avanish Awasthi asks at Lucknow job fair; recruitment underway for 2,780 posts
stories.summary: A mega job fair is being organised at Lucknow's Indira Gandhi Pratishthan (IGP) on Monday by the Regional Employment Office and IBM-1M1B Foundation. Skill Development Minister Kapil Dev Agrawal inaugurated the job fair. Around 20 private companies are participating in the fair and recruiting candidates for 2,780 posts. Selected candidates will receive salaries ranging from ₹10,200 to ₹35,000 per month. See 3 pictures of the mega job fair Companies offering hundreds of job opportunities At the auditorium, Shri Sai Power and Equipments Private Limited will recruit candidates for 500 posts. Apart from this, Airtel Payments Bank and Nykaa FMCG will recruit for 250 posts each. Iron Mountain, Premier Plasmotec and Randstad will hire for 200 posts each. Modpro Engineering, INEL Power Systems and Jai Bharat Maruti will recruit candidates for 150 posts each. Utkarsh Small Finance Bank, Polymedicure Limited, SATA Vikas India and Tata Motors will offer 100 posts each. DD Cinemas, Lenskart, ICS Food Services, Teleperformance, Niyokta Financial Services, Mega Mind Solutions Private Limited and Yuva Shakti Foundation will recruit for 50 posts each. Candidates from 10th pass to graduates eligible Candidates who have passed Class 10, Class 12, ITI, diploma, BE-BTech and undergraduate courses can apply according to their qualifications. Applicants between 18 and 35 years of age will be eligible for the recruitment process. A large number of candidates reached the venue for interviews, with a 200-metre-long queue seen outside the counters. Vikas, an ITI pass candidate, said he came from Barabanki for the interview. He received information about the job fair through WhatsApp. Free employment fair District Employment Officer Pragya Tripathi said candidates will have to register and apply through the Rojgar Sangam portal. Applicants must bring their biodata, original educational certificates and photocopies to the venue. The employment fair is completely free, and no fee will be charged at any stage of the recruitment process.

stories.title: Gorakhpur city buses resume after 5-hour strike:Conductors end protest after RM's assurance, give 24-hour deadline
stories.summary: Gorakhpur city bus services remained suspended from Monday morning as conductors went on strike over demands including payment of wages below the prescribed standard. The conductors parked buses at the Mahesra charging point station and started a protest. They sat on a dharna demanding that their issues be resolved. However, after Regional Manager (RM) Lav Kumar held talks with the conductors, the protest ended after nearly five hours. Three representatives were selected to present their demands. The authorities have given time till Tuesday to discuss the matter with SS Trading Company and resolve all issues. The first bus resumed operations at around 11 am. Thousands of passengers affected due to strike The strike caused inconvenience to thousands of passengers across the city. City buses usually start operating from 5 am, and students, office-goers and other daily commuters depend on them. Due to the sudden suspension of services, passengers faced difficulties in reaching schools, workplaces and hospitals. People waiting at Mahesra, Mohaddipur, railway station, Kachahri and other routes had to wait for hours. Many passengers were forced to rely on autos and e-rickshaws, which increased their travel expenses. Students and working professionals said their daily schedules were disrupted, with many reaching colleges and offices late. Pictures of the charging station Conductors allege new company paying lower wages The conductors alleged that after the previous company's contract ended, the responsibility of salary payments was given to a new company. They claimed the company was paying wages below the fixed standards despite all terms being decided earlier. They said complaints were made to officials, but no solution was provided. Due to this, all conductors reached the Mahesra depot on Monday morning, parked the buses and started their protest. Conductors say: Fulfil demands first, then we will resume duty The protesting conductors said it had become difficult to manage household expenses amid rising inflation. They said children's education expenses and family needs depend on their salaries. They demanded that the fixed salary be paid and an assurance be given for timely payments in the future. 27 city buses operated with around 80 conductors Gorakhpur currently has 27 city buses operating on different routes, with around 80 conductors deployed. All conductors parked the buses at the Mahesra charging point and joined the protest. Initially, no senior official had reached the spot, but later discussions were held to end the strike. stories.title: 'SP leaders are shouting as if their money was stolen':Keshav Prasad Maurya says, '100 chuhe khaake billi haj ko chali'; SP MLCs storm well
stories.summary: The first day of the Uttar Pradesh Legislature's Monsoon Session on Monday witnessed a heated confrontation in the Legislative Council over the alleged theft of offerings from the Ram Mandir. Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya attacked the Samajwadi Party (SP), saying- Sup bole toh bole chalni bhi bole jisme bahatar ched.The SP once identified itself with Babur. In 1990, it was these very people who got Ram devotees killed. The remarks triggered strong protests from SP MLCs, who left their seats and entered the Well of the House, raising slogans of “Chanda chor, gaddi chhod”. Maurya responded with another jibe, saying- 100 chuhe khaake billi haj ko chali. SP legislators hit back, saying- You stole Mandir offerings and then went on a pilgrimage. Keshav Maurya: 'They cannot tolerate the Grand Ram Mandir' As the protests continued, Maurya further said- "They cannot bear the sight of the grand Ram Mandir in Ayodhya. Mandirs will also be built in Mathura and Kashi. They are shouting as if their own donations have been stolen. They haven't contributed even a single rupee, yet they are talking about theft of offerings. Such shamelessness." SP-Congress protest outside Assembly Earlier on Monday at around 10.30 am, SP and Congress legislators staged a protest outside the Assembly over the alleged Ram Mandir offering theft and the NEET paper leak. SP legislators carried a donation box filled with small coins and held placards reading- "Is it NEET or CHEAT?" "Loot in the name of Lord Ram." SP chief Akhilesh Yadav posted on X- "The beginning itself is explosive." CM Yogi targets Opposition before session Before the House convened, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath addressed the media and criticised the Opposition. He said- Those who harmed farmers' interests during their tenure are now pretending to champion farmers. Look at their double standards. These are the same people who ordered firing on Ram devotees. Today they speak about the Ram Mandir. The public is watching them. House pays tribute to senior SP MLA Alam Badi Before legislative business began, the Assembly adopted a condolence motion following the death of Alam Badi, the oldest SP MLA in the House. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Leader of the Opposition Mata Prasad Pandey and leaders from all parties paid tribute by reading the condolence resolution. The House observed a two-minute silence. The Chief Minister said the state had lost “an accomplished politician and social worker.” Following the tribute, Assembly proceedings were adjourned. See pictures of SP's protest- Day-wise schedule of Assembly session The UP Assembly monsoon session will run from August 3 to August 6, with different proceedings planned for each day. August 3: Tributes will be paid to deceased legislators in the House. August 4: Ordinances, notifications, rules and other important documents will be placed before the House. New bills may also be introduced. At 12:20 pm, demands for the 2026-27 supplementary budget will be presented. August 5: Legislative business will be taken up, including discussions on bills related to new laws. August 6: Discussions on supplementary budget demands will be held, followed by voting. The appropriation bill related to the supplementary budget will also be introduced, discussed and voted on. Other legislative work will also continue.

stories.title: Family kills one snake, another bites siblings:Only son dies, daughter is on ventilator; mother says, 'It comes as doom for our family'
stories.summary: "I was sleeping on the bed with both my children. Around 3:30 am on Sunday, a snake bit my four-year-old daughter. She started crying loudly. I immediately picked her up and took her to my mother-in-law. Two minutes later, my six-year-old son also screamed. When I went near him, I saw a black snake wrapped around him. It had bitten him at three to four places. If I had taken my son along with my daughter at that time, he would have been alive today. But I could not see the snake earlier. Two-three days ago, a pair of snakes had entered the same room, and family members had killed one of them. The other snake came like a threat of death and bit my children. My daughter is still fighting for her life." Saying this, Jhansi resident Neha Kushwaha (26) broke down in tears. Her six-year-old only son Mayank died due to the snake bite, while her four-year-old daughter Pragati is on a ventilator at a private hospital. Mayank's body was buried at 7 pm on Sunday. The incident took place in Badagaon town, around 20 km from Jhansi city. Now understand the entire matter in a sequential manner- Mayank went to school for the first time Neha lives in the Hardaulpura locality of Badagaon. Her family includes her children, father-in-law Balram Kushwaha, mother-in-law Pushpa and husband Pradeep. Pradeep works at Apex Factory. Crying, Neha said, "This year, we admitted Mayank to LKG. Pragati would also sometimes go to school with him. The entire family loved both children. Everything was going well." Snake bit after father left for duty Mayank's uncle Harcharan Kushwaha said, "My younger brother Pradeep left for work around 3 am on Sunday. The rest of the family members were sleeping. Suddenly, the snake bit both children." "After hearing their screams, we rushed to the room. We called Pradeep back home and immediately took both children to the medical college. During treatment, Mayank died at around 9:30 am. Pragati's condition is critical and she is undergoing treatment." Mother says 'my son has left me' After Mayank's body reached home following the post-mortem, his mother hugged him and started crying. She repeatedly lost consciousness while mourning. As soon as she regained consciousness, she kept saying, "My son has left me. If I had even the slightest idea that there was a snake in the room, I would never have slept there with my children." Neha said Mayank had started going to school for the first time this year, while Pragati had not yet been admitted. Family searched for snake throughout the day Ward councillor Sushil Kumar Kushwaha said, "After the incident, the family does not even have the courage to enter the house. Snake catchers were called. At one point, the snake was seen outside the room, but within moments it hid inside a hole." The family saw the snake entering a hole inside the house but did not see it coming out.

stories.title: Woman doctor dies after jumping from 5th floor:Father says she was depressed after divorce 18 months ago
stories.summary: A woman psychiatrist died after allegedly jumping from the fifth floor of a residential building in Ghaziabad on Sunday evening around 7 pm. She suffered severe head injuries after falling from the building. Nearby residents rushed her to a hospital, where doctors declared her dead. According to police, the woman had been suffering from depression after her divorce from her husband around 18 months ago. Her body has been sent for postmortem examination. The incident took place in Raj Nagar Extension under Nandgram police station area. Divorce had taken place one and a half years ago Dr Hamika Agrawal (40) lived alone in Officer City-2 Society in Raj Nagar Extension. She was a psychiatrist by profession and counselled patients. She ran a clinic near Ghaziabad bus stand. Her father, Dr R Chandra, is also a psychiatrist and lived in another society in Raj Nagar Extension. Dr R Chandra said his daughter got divorced from her husband around one-and-a-half years ago. After that, she went into depression and was undergoing treatment. He said that on Sunday evening, she jumped from the fifth floor of the building. A resident of the society immediately took her to Yashoda Hospital in his car, but doctors declared her dead. Police questioning family members ACP Nandgram Ziauddin said the preliminary investigation revealed that Dr Hamika Agrawal was living alone in her flat, while her parents stayed at another location. He said family members are being questioned as part of the investigation.

stories.title: Gorakhpur turns devotional on first Sawan Monday:Devotees offer bel leaves, temples echo with Bol Bam chants
stories.summary: On the first Monday of Sawan, a huge crowd of devotees gathered at Shiva temples across Gorakhpur. From early morning, devotees started arriving at major Shiva shrines including Mukteshwar Nath Temple, Mahadev Jharkhandi Temple, Mansarovar Temple, Munjeshwar Nath Temple and other religious sites. Long queues of devotees were seen outside temples since dawn. The temple premises echoed throughout the day with chants of "Har Har Mahadev" and "Bol Bam". Thousands arrive to offer water on Shivling Although Sawan began on July 30, the first Monday of the holy month saw special enthusiasm and devotion among devotees. Women performed Jalabhishek of Lord Shiva praying for the happiness and prosperity of their families and the long lives of their husbands. Young devotees offered prayers seeking a better future, success and fulfilment of their wishes. Devotees offered Gangajal, milk, belpatra, dhatura, bhang, flowers and fruits to Lord Shiva and performed rituals. A spiritual atmosphere prevailed at the temples throughout the day as devotees arrived with enthusiasm for darshan of Lord Bholenath. Temple administration made special arrangements Mahant Ramanand Upadhyay of Mukteshwar Nath Temple said the first Monday of Sawan is considered extremely sacred for Shiva devotees. Thousands of devotees performed Jalabhishek on the occasion. He said special arrangements were made by the temple administration to ensure smooth darshan for devotees. According to him, the wishes of those who worship Lord Shiva with true devotion are fulfilled. Considering the heavy crowd, police and administration remained alert. A temporary police post was set up inside the temple premises by Rajghat police station. Barricading was also done to ensure devotees could get darshan easily. Adequate police personnel were deployed for security. Police officials offer prayers, inspect security arrangements Kotwali Circle Officer Omkar Dutt Tiwari and Rajghat Station House Officer Gaurav Verma visited the temple along with their team. They offered water on the Shivling and sought blessings. They also inspected security arrangements with temple priest Mahant Mukteshwar Nath Ramanath. Major Shiva temples of Gorakhpur and their beliefs Mukteshwarnath Temple: Where Lord Shiva Saved from Lions Located on the banks of the Rapti river in Gorakhpur city, Mukteshwar Nath Temple is believed to be around 400 years old. According to belief, the king of Bansi once came here for hunting when lions surrounded him. To save his life, the king prayed to Lord Shiva, following which a miracle happened and the lions left the place. Overwhelmed by the experience, the king decided to build a Shiva temple there. On his orders, Baba Kashinath from Maharashtra established the temple. A place called "Muktidham" is located near the temple, which is believed to be the reason behind its name. A large number of devotees visit the temple during Sawan and Mahashivratri. Mahadev Jharkhandi Temple: Shivling appeared after a dream Mahadev Jharkhandi Temple of Gorakhpur is also an ancient and famous Shiva shrine. Thousands of devotees visit the temple during Sawan. According to belief, the temple area was once a dense forest. One day, landlord Gabbu Das saw Lord Shiva in his dream, who told him that a Shivling was hidden at a particular place on his land. When the place was excavated, a Shivling was found there. A temple was later built at the site. Devotees believe that offering Jalabhishek here provides relief from troubles and difficulties. A grand fair is also organised here on Mahashivratri. Mansarovar Temple: Devotion began after King Mansingh's dream The history of Mansarovar Temple is also linked to a divine dream. According to belief, King Mansingh saw Lord Shiva in his dream, who instructed him to build a temple in the middle of a forest. The king built a temple and a large pond at the same place. The temple has a deep connection with Gorakshapeeth. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath renovated the temple and gave it a new look. On Vijayadashami, the Peethadhishwar of Gorakshapeeth starts the Vijay procession from here, and the tilak ceremony of Lord Ram is also performed here. Munjeshwar Nath Temple: Where milk flowed from a stone Located in Bhauvapar village of Gorakhpur district, Munjeshwar Nath Temple is another major centre of faith. It is believed that the area was once the capital of the Sataasi kingdom. Once, while workers were clearing bushes, their spade hit a stone and a stream of milk started flowing from it. The workers informed the king, who ordered excavation at the site. A Shivling was found there. Lord Shiva later appeared in the king's dream and instructed him to build a temple. The temple got its name Munjeshwar Nath because the Shivling was found from bushes known as "Munj". How to worship Lord Shiva during Sawan During Sawan, devotees should wake up early, take a bath and wear clean clothes. After this, they should perform Abhishek of the Shivling with water, Gangajal, milk, honey and Panchamrit. Devotees should offer belpatra, dhatura, white flowers and fruits to Lord Shiva. Lighting lamps and incense while chanting "Om Namah Shivay" is considered auspicious. Keep these things in mind Keeping a fast on Sawan Monday is considered auspicious. Devotees are advised to consume satvik food and avoid non-vegetarian food, alcohol and other tamasic items. People should avoid arguments, maintain respect and kindness towards everyone, and pay special attention to cleanliness and purity of the place of worship. On the first Monday of Sawan, all major Shiva temples in Gorakhpur remained crowded throughout the day. The city witnessed a grand display of devotion, faith and reverence towards Lord Shiva.

stories.title: BJP leader's mother cries after Pappu Yadav attack:Says in Bulandshahr, "I only want my son to return home safely"
stories.summary: The mother of BJP leader Sumit, who allegedly attacked Bihar's independent MP Pappu Yadav with a slipper, broke down on Sunday and appealed for her son's release. She said, "I only want my son to return home safely. I do not want anything else. I have nothing to do with politics. He had left home saying he was going to the office. I appeal that my son should be released." Sumit, a resident of Bulandshahr, had allegedly attacked Pappu Yadav along with his associate Happy Sharma. Pappu Yadav caught Sumit, while his supporters allegedly thrashed Happy. Amid the chaos, Happy escaped, while Sumit was handed over to the police. Sumit is the BJP's city minister, while Happy is the party's mandal general secretary. Both are also involved in contract work. See pictures of the attack on the MP What happened during the attack On Sunday evening, Pappu Yadav was holding a press conference at his residence when someone threw a slipper at him. Pappu immediately got up and caught the attacker. During this, his supporters started beating the accused. Pappu tried to stop his supporters, but they continued assaulting the accused. The attacker, wearing a pink shirt, was held by Pappu Yadav beside him before supporters later pulled him away. Police faced difficulty while taking the accused into custody. Pappu Yadav later showed a knife to the media, claiming the accused had brought it with him. Accused's companion said - We did not go with a knife According to police, Sumit, who allegedly attacked Pappu Yadav, is a resident of Sahpani village in Bulandshahr. His father's name is Phool Giri. The 34-year-old currently lives in Ghaziabad, where he works in manufacturing iron goods. Happy Sharma is a resident of Nethla Hasanpur village in Bulandshahr. His father's name is Munesh Kumar Sharma. His elder brother Sumant is a ration dealer. Happy has been associated with the BJP for a long time. On June 5, he shared a post on Instagram, following which Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak congratulated him. Akhilesh spoke to Pappu Yadav, wrote - BJP resorted to violence Pappu Yadav asks, “What is my crime?” After the attack, Pappu Yadav told the media, "Some people keep saying every day — kill me, burn me, we will give ₹51 lakh. We caught one person and handed him over to the police. An FIR has been registered against him. The attack happened in front of you. What is my crime? The crime belongs to Brij Bhushan Tiwari and Champat Rai." Happy Sharma claims they did not carry a knife Happy Sharma, who allegedly threw the slipper, said there was a protest by saints outside Pappu Yadav's residence. He and Sumit Giri Goswami had gone there to support the saints, but by the time they arrived, the protesters had already been removed. He said they then went to meet Pappu Yadav. After security checks, they entered while a press conference was underway. Happy claimed they told Pappu Yadav that wearing saffron clothes like a saint and placing an image of Lord Ram near the feet of Ayodhya MP Awadhesh Prasad was wrong. He alleged that Pappu Yadav's supporters then started beating them and took Sumit inside the house. On the allegation that they carried a knife, Happy said they only threw slippers and shoes after being beaten and did not carry any knife. He claimed the knife was brought by others and shown to the media. See pictures of the protest in the Parliament complex- Akhilesh Yadav speaks to Pappu Yadav, alleges BJP involved in violence Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav spoke to Pappu Yadav over the phone and took details of the incident. Writing on X, Akhilesh said, "Violence is born out of fear of defeat. BJP is frustrated. That is why after targeting the country's children, it is now getting deadly attacks carried out on MPs as well." He said the incident of an attacker reaching a press conference with a knife was serious and also raised questions over lapses in the MP's security. July 31: Pappu Yadav staged Ram temple donation theft protest in Parliament On the 10th day of the Monsoon Session, Pappu Yadav entered the Parliament premises dressed as a saint and carrying a donation box. A short play was performed protesting alleged theft of Ram temple donations. Pappu Yadav, dressed as a priest, sat on the ground, after which Rahul Gandhi and other MPs donated money to him. Pappu Yadav allegedly kept the donated money with himself instead of putting it in the donation box. Later, MPs including Awadhesh Prasad staged a symbolic act of catching him stealing and beat him symbolically. During the protest, Pappu Yadav was seen touching the feet of Ayodhya MP Awadhesh Prasad. FIR registered against Rahul Gandhi, Pappu Yadav over protest On August 1, an FIR was registered against Congress MP Rahul Gandhi, SP MP Awadhesh Prasad and independent Bihar MP Pappu Yadav over the symbolic protest on Ram temple donations. The FIR was filed by Jagadguru Balak Das, the head of Patalpuri Math, at Kotwali police station in Varanasi. Meanwhile, in Lucknow, Sanatan Raksha Sangathan national president Anurudh Rai warned that Pappu Yadav's "sins have ended" and claimed the time for punishment had arrived. He also targeted Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav, alleging they were against Sanatan beliefs. He threatened action if they did not apologise and announced a ₹51 lakh reward for bringing Pappu Yadav's head. August 2: Hindu groups protest outside Pappu Yadav's wife's residence On Saturday, Bajrang Dal workers and saints protested outside the Delhi residence of Pappu Yadav's wife and Rajya Sabha MP Ranjeet Ranjan. Reacting to the protest on Sunday, Pappu Yadav warned that if his children and family were targeted, "a Mahabharata bigger than Mahabharata" would happen. He said they do not involve children in political fights and that they had not received such weak values.

stories.title: Lucknow sees heavy rain on first Monday of Sawan:Monsoon active again, orange alert issued as dark clouds cover city
stories.summary: Lucknow's monsoon has become active again. On the first Monday of Sawan, rain started around 3 am and continued for nearly three hours. The intensity reduced after 6 am, but dark clouds remained over the city even at 8 am. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an orange alert for rainfall during the day. So far this monsoon season, Lucknow has received 180.6 mm rainfall against the normal average of 330.3 mm. This means the city has recorded 45% less rainfall than normal. However, weather officials said heavy rain activity is expected to continue from August 3 to August 6. See 5 pictures- Waterlogging reported in several areas Continuous rainfall has led to waterlogging on roads and low-lying areas across the city. Water accumulated near the Shaheed Path stretch in Kamta. Similar conditions were reported on the service lane of Shaheed Path in Vibhuti Khand. The road leading to Budheshwar Mahadev temple was also waterlogged. Despite heavy rain, a large number of devotees reached the temple on the first Monday of Sawan. In Sarojini Nagar, light rain continued in the morning after heavy showers early in the day. People stepped out carrying umbrellas. Rain disrupts morning routine in Lucknow as devotees continue temple visits Rain continued across Lucknow on Monday morning, with showers affecting several areas of the city. At Budheshwar Mahadev temple, devotees continued arriving in large numbers despite the rain. Several Kanwariyas participating in the Bol Bam tradition were seen performing the temple parikrama amid the showers. In Sarojini Nagar, light rain continued in the morning, with people stepping out carrying umbrellas for essential work. Heavy rainfall since early morning also caused waterlogging on the route leading to Budheshwar Mahadev temple. However, the rain did not stop devotees from reaching the shrine. Rain also continued in the Para area, where showers started around 3 am and continued till morning. Dark clouds remained over Lucknow, with visuals from the Sitapur-Lucknow Highway showing cloudy skies. Temperature expected to remain around 33°C The maximum temperature in Lucknow is expected to remain around 33°C on Monday, while the minimum temperature may stay at 27°C. On Sunday, the city's maximum temperature was recorded at 35.2°C, which was 1.9°C above normal. The minimum temperature stood at 28.2°C, around 2.4°C above normal. The maximum humidity was recorded at 88%, while the minimum humidity remained at 67%. Monsoon trough moving towards Uttar Pradesh Meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said the monsoon has become active again and heavy rainfall has started in the region. He said the spell of intense rain is expected to continue from August 3 to August 6. According to him, the monsoon trough is rapidly shifting towards North India, including Uttar Pradesh. At the same time, monsoon winds coming from the Bay of Bengal have also strengthened, increasing the possibility of continued rainfall.

stories.title: UP's paper leak law is stricter than Centre's:State allows life term despite Centre's new 10-year jail law; will state law become redundant?
stories.summary: The Centre's new anti-paper leak Bill became law after receiving the President's assent on July 31. It will come into force across the country once the Central government issues the Gazette notification. The new law provides for a maximum punishment of 10 years' imprisonment. However, Uttar Pradesh's anti-paper leak law, which has been in force since 2024, provides for life imprisonment in certain cases, making it appear stricter. If such a stringent law already exists, why are paper leak incidents still not stopping? Here's today's UP Explainer. Question-1: When and how was the paper leak law made in UP? Answer: The Uttar Pradesh government enacted the Uttar Pradesh Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act in 2024. The law was drafted after the RO/ARO and UP Police Constable recruitment paper leaks in February 2024. With the Lok Sabha elections just two months away, the Opposition made paper leaks a major issue in Uttar Pradesh. During the election campaign, the NEET-UG paper leak also surfaced in May. When the Lok Sabha election results were announced on June 4, the BJP's tally in Uttar Pradesh dropped from 62 seats to 33. The party also failed to secure a majority on its own at the Centre. The paper leak controversy was considered one of the contributing factors. With the support of several alliance partners, the BJP-led Central government implemented the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act across the country on June 21. Following the same model, the UP government issued an ordinance on June 25, which was later passed by the state legislature and enacted into law. According to Section 2(6) of the UP law, it covers all Uttar Pradesh government recruitment examinations, including those conducted by UPPSC, UPSSSC, UPPRPB and UPPCL, Class 10 and 12 UP Board examinations, and examinations conducted by all government and private universities and institutes in the state. Section 3(2) clearly states that examinations such as UPSC, SSC, NEET, JEE, Railway recruitment, Banking examinations and examinations conducted by Central universities and institutes are outside the scope of the UP law. These are governed by the Central legislation. The Centre has now amended its own Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024. Initially, only the second shift of the UP Police Constable Recruitment Examination-2024 was believed to have been leaked. Later, investigations revealed that papers from both shifts had been compromised Question-2: What is the provision for punishment for paper leak in UP law? Answer: The law provides different punishments depending on the role and level of involvement of the accused. If a candidate is caught cheating personally, they will be expelled from the examination, their result will be withheld and they will be barred from appearing in any examination for one year. However, no criminal case will be registered against them. Anyone involved in leaking question papers, sharing confidential information, entering an examination centre without authorisation or manipulating the evaluation process can face two to ten years' imprisonment along with a fine ranging from ₹2 lakh to ₹5 lakh. Those who assist candidates or influence examinations through threats or inducements can face three to ten years' imprisonment and fines between ₹3 lakh and ₹10 lakh. Members of solver gangs can face seven to fourteen years' imprisonment and fines ranging from ₹10 lakh to ₹25 lakh. Repeat offenders can be sentenced to life imprisonment along with fines between ₹50 lakh and ₹1 crore. Anyone endangering the life of an official connected with an examination authority in order to disrupt the examination can be sentenced to life imprisonment and fined between ₹50 lakh and ₹1 crore. All offences under the Act are cognisable and non-bailable. Trials will be conducted directly in Sessions Courts, while investigations can only be carried out by officers of DSP or ACP rank. Property acquired through such offences can also be attached. Any examination centre found involved in mass cheating can be permanently debarred. Question-3: How different is the Central Government's new law from UP's law? Answer: Person involved in paper leak Solver Gangs and Organized Crime Accountability of Examination Agency Timeline for Investigation-Trial Overall Situation UP's law remains stricter at the entry level, particularly because it provides for life imprisonment for solver gangs and repeat offenders. The amended Central law, however, has overtaken the UP law in terms of higher monetary penalties and time-bound investigations and trials. In other words, both laws have become increasingly similar, with each being stricter in different areas. Section 5 of the UP law specifically provides for life imprisonment in certain offences. Question-4: Will the new central law also be applicable in UP? Answer: Not automatically. The new law will apply only to examinations conducted by the Central government. Cases involving paper leaks in state-level examinations will continue to be governed by Uttar Pradesh's own law. However, if the UP government wishes, it can also adopt the Central law for state examinations. There are two possible ways to do this. 1. Through a request to the Central government Education falls under the Concurrent List of the Constitution. This means there is a prescribed administrative process for implementing a Central law in state examinations. Cabinet proposal: The UP government's Personnel Department will first prepare a proposal, which must be approved by the state Cabinet. Request to the Centre: The UP government will then send an official request to the Union Ministry of Personnel, stating that it wants the Central law to apply to state-level examinations as well. Gazette notification: The Central government will issue a Gazette notification specifying the state recruitment boards and examinations that will come under the Central law. 2. By amending the state law Passing a Bill: The UP government can introduce a new Bill based on the Central law or one containing even stricter provisions, and have it passed by the state legislature. Governor's and President's approval: After being passed, the Bill will be sent to the Governor. If its provisions differ from or are stricter than the Central law, it will then be sent to the President for approval. Question-5: If the central law is implemented in UP, will UP's old law be abolished? Answer: No. The position can be understood through the following legal principles. 1. Conflicting provisions will cease to apply Under Article 254 of the Constitution, if both Parliament and a state legislature enact laws on a subject in the Concurrent List, the Central law prevails wherever there is a conflict. In such a situation, only those provisions of the UP law that directly conflict with the amended Central law will become inoperative. 2. Stricter state provisions will continue Some provisions of Uttar Pradesh's 2024 law are stricter than those contained in the Central legislation. In legal terms, stricter state provisions—such as the punishment of life imprisonment in certain cases—will continue to remain in force. 3. What will change in practice? If the Central framework is adopted, investigations into paper leaks in state examinations will have to be completed within two months. Trials will be conducted in special fast-track courts and completed within three months. At the same time, offenders can still face life imprisonment under the UP law, and their illegally acquired properties can also be attached. Question-6: Why aren't paper leak incidents stopping despite strict laws? Answer: According to experts, investigating agencies and administrative reports 1. High-return black market worth billions 2. Outsourcing and Private Vendors 3. Fierce Competition 4. Delay in Lawsuits Question-7: So is there no permanent solution to this? Answer: That's not the case, experts suggest some other measures along with strict laws Hybrid Model Examination: Paper appears on computer screen, but students fill answers with pen on OMR sheet. This will block both printing press and computer hacking routes. Use of Government Press: Paper printing should be done only in highly secure government printing presses (like currency note press or RBI press) instead of private vendors. Examination Centers Should Be Government: Examinations should be conducted only at government schools, universities and highly certified centers like TCS instead of private colleges and computer labs.

stories.title: 'Took blessings from father's memorial,' says UP sub-inspector:Mother showed it via video call; story behind Commonwealth Games gold medal
stories.summary: 'My childhood was spent in a lot of struggles. Mom and Dad did a lot for me. It was a small, two-room mud house. If it rained heavily, the roof would start leaking. Rainwater would also fill up inside the house. In this, we two sisters, brother, and Mom and Dad lived. Many people in our village had mud houses, and the road was also unpaved. When I was little, there was no electricity. I had to study in the light of a lamp. When I was in Class 7, Dad used to take me to school 12 km away on a scooter, and then bring me back in the afternoon. The mud house was later converted into a brick house by Dad with some government assistance. Before my game started, Mom showed me Dad's memorial on a video call and said, 'Take his blessings, you will definitely win gold.'' These things were said by Asmita Dey, a female sub-inspector from Gorakhpur and Commonwealth gold medalist, in a conversation with Dainik Bhaskar. A mud house, where water used to leak 23-year-old Asmita Dey says - I was born in Sunai Cheri village in South Tripura. We had a mud house in this village. There were 2 small rooms. During the rainy season, my father used to cover the roof with polythene. When it rained heavily, water would leak from the mud roof. There was no electricity in the village either. The road in front was also unpaved. It would also get waterlogged there. Many people had mud houses like ours. Father Arjun Kumar Dey was a bicycle mechanic. It was very difficult to manage household expenses. My elder sister Deva Mitra and I used to study by the light of lamps and lanterns. When the weather was bad, we couldn't even study. It was 2015, I was in Class 7. At that time, there were no roads in the village. The district headquarters was about 12 km away from there. There were no resources to go from the village to there. Father had an old scooter. When I used to go to the district headquarters to learn Judo, father would drop me off from home on his scooter in the morning. After dropping me off, father would look after the work at the bicycle shop. After that, he would pick me up by scooter in the afternoon and bring me home. This was the daily routine. After some time, my uncle (father's elder brother) helped again. I also prepared while staying with him. He lived more than 100 km away from home. It used to take about 4 hours to reach by bus. Father's dream was to build a cement house Asmita Dey says- Father married off elder sister Deva Mitra Dey. For this, mother and father also borrowed money from outside. Mother also used to say that we would build a permanent house in the village, but the financial situation was weak. There were also expenses for both our sisters' education and my sports. But, father used to say with courage that everything would be alright. Perhaps some help was received from the government there, and Papa demolished the old house to build a room with solid bricks and cement, but even that couldn't be completed. When Papa passed away, the responsibility of the house fell on Mummy's shoulders. In 2023, the UP government gave me a job as a police constable, which improved our financial situation. We also repaid the money borrowed from outside. Mummy showed the soil from the cremation ground on a video call Asmita Dey said- On August 31, Mom video-called me. Mom was at that time cleaning the spot of Dad's memorial at the cremation ground. That place is several kilometers away from the village. Showing me the soil from Dad's memorial spot, Mom said, 'Daughter, take blessings for victory from your father.' Mom was very happy that day. She kept saying that today would be good and I would win. Seeing the soil from Dad's memorial, I didn't get emotional. This was an opportunity to fulfill the dream Dad had seen for me. Mom kept saying on the video call that I would win today. For my victory, Mom went to the temple in the morning and prayed. My coach had fasted for me that day. At 12 AM, I video called Mom After winning the gold medal, I video called Mom at 12 AM on the night of August 31st. I told her, "Mom, today I won." Mom said, "I know. News reporters have come here. Everyone knows about it everywhere tonight. Your elder sister Devamitra Dey also called. Brother Devavrat Dey started crying with joy." Mom said - If Asmita's father were here today, he would have been very happy Asmita's mother said - My daughter has received a medal. I am very proud of my daughter. Our Prime Minister of India is very happy. Our Chief Minister is also happy. All our brothers and sisters of Tripura, all countrymen are very happy. This has also given me a lot of happiness. Everyone is happy, so my happiness knows no bounds. This is the proudest thing for me that my daughter Asmita has achieved this. But, one sad thing is that Asmita's father is not among us today. If Asmita's father were here today, he would also be very happy to see this. The only sad thing is that he is no longer in this world.

stories.title: BSP names 24 in-charges, most of them will be candidates:Mayawati conducts interviews, asks nephew to lead campaign; caste balance under focus
stories.summary: BSP has opened the election front for the assembly first. The party has so far announced the names of 24 assembly in-charges. Their interviews were taken by Mayawati herself. It has been a tradition of BSP that the leaders who are made assembly in-charges later become the party's candidates. In such a situation, these announcements are being considered as the party's first list of candidates. Akash also fielded, will start from Hathras BSP is not just announcing names, but is also testing the strength of its organisation by holding worker conferences in every assembly constituency. A similar conference will be held on August 10 in the Sadabad assembly constituency of Hathras. For the first time, the party's national convener Akash Anand will participate in it. The party is preparing to give an election message by gathering a large crowd at this meeting. On August 25, Akash Anand will hold a program in Jewar assembly constituency of Gautam Buddh Nagar. Here, the party will declare Satveer Singh Nagar, who has already been decided, as the assembly in-charge. BSP plans to declare candidates' names in a similar manner by holding 2-3 big rallies every month. Akash will respond to Chandrashekhar in his own style In Western UP, there is a good number of Dalit, especially Jatav voters. This has been BSP's strongest vote bank. In recent years, Chandrashekhar Azad, chief of the Azad Samaj Party, has strengthened his hold among Jatav and Muslim voters in Western UP. Due to his young face and aggressive style, a section of Dalit youth has also been attracted to him. In such a situation, Mayawati has tried to answer Chandrashekhar's challenge by fielding Akash Anand. According to political analyst Harshvardhan Tripathi, a large number of Dalit youth attended Akash Anand's rallies in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. BSP now wants to extend the same strategy to the assembly elections as well. Through Akash's electoral debut from Western UP, the party wants to strengthen its organization as well as send a political message. Betting on Brahmin face in Sadabad, Gurjar face in Jewar In Sadabad, BSP has put forward Dr. Avin Sharma. This seat was once considered a stronghold of Ramveer Upadhyay, a powerful BSP leader. He was among the party's prominent Brahmin faces. After his move to BJP, BSP is now trying to re-establish this social equation through Dr. Avin Sharma. His name has already been announced at the party workers' conference. Meanwhile, in the Jewar assembly constituency, BSP has put its trust in Gurjar leader Satveer Singh Nagar. Satveer was a BSP MLA from Dadri in 2007 and 2012. In 2019, he also contested the Lok Sabha election from the Gautam Buddh Nagar seat on a BSP ticket. Considering the significant role of Gurjar voters in Western UP, this move by BSP is considered important. Caste balance seen in the first list of in-charges If you look at the declared list of BSP, the party has tried to give representation to almost all effective social classes. Instead of relying only on the Dalit vote bank, the party is also promoting influential faces from Brahmin, Muslim, OBC, and upper-caste communities. BSP has tried to re-establish the old 'Brahmin-Dalit' social equation by giving responsibility to Brahmin leaders in many seats. The social equation of that assembly constituency is also reflected in the selection of every BSP candidate.

stories.title: First Monday of Sawan sees 3 km queue in Kashi:Flower petals showered after Mangala Aarti, 40,000 Yadav devotees to perform Jalabhishek
stories.summary: Today is the first Monday of Sawan. A huge crowd of devotees has gathered to offer water at Kashi Vishwanath. A 3-kilometer long queue of Kanwariyas has formed. Devotees are getting only 1 second to perform Jalabhishek. Entry of devotees into the sanctum sanctorum is prohibited. Baba's Mangala Aarti took place at 4 AM. After this, the temple gates were opened for darshan. Priests showered flowers on Kanwariyas and devotees. The 3-kilometre area around Kashi Vishwanath Temple has been declared a no-vehicle zone. Entry is available through 6 gates of the temple. Baba Vishwanath is giving darshan to devotees today in the form of Shankar. For security, the temple area has been divided into 5 zones. Baba Vishwanath's abode has been decorated with about 50,000 flowers from Kolkata, the city of Maa Kali. Among these, the temple has been adorned with 3000 marigolds, 1500 rajnigandha, and 500-500 garlands of roses and gerberas. It took 10 to 12 hours to decorate the entire temple. 40 thousand Yadav brothers will perform Jalabhishek of Baba Vishwanath Under the banner of Chandravanshi Gopa Seva Samiti, the 94th annual Jalabhishek Yatra will be taken out this year as well, on the first Monday of Sawan. The committee's president, Lalji Chandravanshi, informed that approximately 40 thousand Yadav brothers will travel about 17 kilometers to perform Jalabhishek and worship at 7 Shiva temples and two other temples, making a total of nine religious sites. 21 Yadav brothers will perform Jalabhishek in the sanctum sanctorum of Kashi Vishwanath. The rest will offer water through the argha. The Jalabhishek Yatra will begin at 7:30 AM from Kedar Ghat. Devotees will first perform Jalabhishek of Gauri-Kedareshwar Mahadev. After this, they will reach Tilbhandeshwar Mahadev. Then, filling Ganga water from Sheetla Ghat, they will perform Jalabhishek of Mata Sheetla and Ahileshwar Mahadev located at Man Mandir Ghat. After this, the yatra will reach Shri Kashi Vishwanath Dham, where devotees will perform Jalabhishek and have darshan of Baba Vishwanath. Following this, the yatra will conclude with darshan and Jalabhishek of Mahamrityunjay Mahadev, Trilochan Mahadev, Omkareshwar Mahadev, and finally Latbhairav Baba. Locker facility is closed at Kashi Vishwanath Temple Dham Kashi Vishwanath Temple administration said- There is limited space inside the temple, so devotees will come in a zig-zag line. Water arrangements have been made at various places so that women and the elderly do not suffer in the heat. Medical staff is also present. The most important change is that all locker facilities available in the Dham are closed. Earlier, this facility was available in the Dham. Devotees will only be allowed to carry milk, Ganga water, flowers, datura, etc., for Abhishek (ritual bathing). No other items are allowed inside. Kashi Vishwanath Temple's appeal- It may take 8-10 hours in the queue No vehicles will run from Maidagin to Godaulia throughout Sawan in Kashi Varanasi's ADCP Traffic Anshuman Mishra said that no vehicles will run from Maidagin to Godaulia throughout Sawan. While from Saturday night to Monday dawn, vehicles will not run from Benia to Ramapura-Khari Kuan to Jangambari, from Godaulia to Dashashwamedh Ghat, and from PDR Luxa to Ramapura. The no-entry time for cargo vehicles will continue from Saturday night 8 PM until Tuesday dawn. This will be applicable every week during Sawan. Additionally, routes have been determined for heavy vehicles to bypass the city. Entry for all large vehicles coming from neighboring districts will not be allowed from Saturday night. Vehicles carrying vegetables, fruits, and milk will not be stopped. All buses, trucks, and other large vehicles commuting through Varanasi city from Ghazipur, Mau, Azamgarh, Jaunpur, Chandauli, Prayagraj, and Bhadohi will be able to use the Ring Road and NH-19. Large vehicles and essential small vehicles will be routed via the Ring Road. Special arrangements for the convenience of devotees at Kashi Vishwanath

stories.title: Farmer gifts vegetables after district magistrate resolves dispute:Three-year wait for land measurement ends after direct intervention by Agra DM
stories.summary: A farmer in Uttar Pradesh's Agra visited the District Magistrate's office on Friday carrying a kilogram of fresh vegetables to thank the District Magistrate after his long-pending land measurement dispute was resolved. The farmer, Ram Prakash, placed a bag of kakoda (spiny gourd) on District Magistrate Manish Bansal's desk and said, Sir, thank you very much. My work is finally done. Please accept these vegetables I have brought for you. Smiling at the gesture, the District Magistrate replied: This is priceless. How can I refuse such a gift? Farmer had waited three years for land measurement Ram Prakash, a resident of Basai Arela in Bah tehsil, had been trying to get his agricultural land measured for the past three years. He alleged that despite repeated complaints, the Revenue Inspector and the lekhpal (village revenue official) kept delaying the process instead of carrying out the measurement. Complaint raised during grievance hearing On July 6, during a public grievance redressal programme, the farmer presented his complaint directly to District Magistrate Manish Bansal. Taking immediate note of the matter, the District Magistrate sought an explanation from the concerned officials and expressed displeasure over the delay in conducting the land measurement. Following his directions, the revenue authorities completed the measurement, resolving the long-pending dispute. Gift from his own farm Grateful that the issue had finally been resolved, Ram Prakash returned to the Collectorate on Friday during the public hearing session. He brought one kilogram of kakoda harvested from his own field as a token of appreciation. The farmer said he had submitted several applications over the past three years and had approached previous officials as well, but no action had been taken until the District Magistrate intervened. DM accepts the 'priceless' gift District Magistrate Manish Bansal said the farmer had brought the vegetables with genuine affection and gratitude. The farmer brought such a priceless gift with great affection. How could I return it? I gladly accepted it. He added that all revenue officials had been instructed to ensure timely disposal of public complaints, not only during Tehsil Day programmes but also through regular public grievance hearings.

stories.title: Yogi says SP goon sparked Sambhal riots:'Now pleading for mercy; Bareilly rioter seeks forgiveness from jail'
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Friday launched a sharp attack on the Samajwadi Party, accusing it of encouraging riots, protecting mafias and disrupting the functioning of the State Assembly. Addressing a public gathering in Ambedkar Nagar, the Chief Minister claimed that a "Samajwadi Party goon" was responsible for the violence in Sambhal and alleged that the accused was now pleading for leniency. Referring to another alleged rioter from Bareilly, he said the man was currently in jail and seeking forgiveness. "A Samajwadi Party goon incited the riots in Sambhal. The government has brought him to his knees. A goon from Bareilly used to organise riots. Today he is suffering in jail and is saying, 'Please let me go, I made a mistake. It won't happen again.'" Alleges Samajwadi Party disrupted Assembly proceedings The Chief Minister also accused Samajwadi Party legislators of creating disruptions during the Assembly session. He said the opposition prevented the House from functioning when the government sought to introduce welfare measures in the Budget. According to him, the proposals included schemes to honour social reformers such as Sant Ravidas, Dr B.R. Ambedkar and Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj, besides increasing honorariums for Anganwadi workers, fair-price shop dealers and village watchmen. “They did not allow the Assembly to function, but we are not going to stop.” See two pictures... Inaugurates projects worth over ₹706 crore During his visit, the Chief Minister inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 194 development projects worth more than ₹706.81 crore in the Jalalpur, Alapur and Tanda Assembly constituencies. He also distributed approval letters and certificates to beneficiaries of various government welfare schemes. 'SP has no interest in development' Yogi Adityanath said the government had presented a supplementary Budget of ₹59,000 crore during the recent Assembly session, but alleged that SP created disruptions and prevented meaningful debate. He claimed the party was not interested in development or the welfare of poor people. 'SP flag once symbolised fear' The Chief Minister alleged that under previous SP governments, riots frequently occurred in cities such as Meerut, Aligarh, Moradabad, Saharanpur, Bareilly, Lucknow and Kanpur. He claimed that criminals travelled in vehicles displaying SP flags and were involved in extortion. "Today our government is taking strict action against such elements." 'Every district had a mafia under SP' The Chief Minister further alleged that the previous SP government had patronised different types of mafias in every district, including sand, land and forest mafias. He claimed Uttar Pradesh had now become both "mafia-free" and "curfew-free". He warned that anyone attempting to threaten traders or interfere with young people's future would be sent to jail and their illegally acquired assets would be confiscated. Highlights welfare initiatives The Chief Minister said the government was promoting local cuisines from every district and providing free food grains to around 16 crore beneficiaries. He also highlighted medical interventions for children with hearing and speech impairments, saying some beneficiaries had received treatment and certificates during the event. Referring to encephalitis, he alleged that nearly 1,200 children used to be affected under previous governments, while accusing SP leaders of showing little concern. 'Ayodhya's development troubles SP and Congress' Yogi Adityanath said Uttar Pradesh had earned greater respect across the country and claimed that the development of Ayodhya had become a source of discomfort for both the Samajwadi Party and the Congress. He accused both parties of opposing Lord Ram and said his government was developing Ayodhya, Kashi, Mathura-Vrindavan and Vindhyachal as major religious centres. He also noted that he was the first Chief Minister to visit Govind Dham in the area. Takes swipe at Akhilesh Yadav Without naming SP president Akhilesh Yadav directly, the Chief Minister mocked his daily routine. "He used to wake up around noon, post a tweet in the afternoon, receive advice from his uncle, then go to the gym. By evening, he would be busy elsewhere and would not even know where he was. A person who cannot manage himself cannot run a state." He added that anyone threatening to incite riots would face strict action. 'Those harassing women or traders face jail' Concluding his speech, the Chief Minister said his government would not tolerate crimes against women or intimidation of traders. He said offenders would face either imprisonment or the strictest legal consequences. The Chief Minister also said around 15 crore people in Uttar Pradesh were receiving free food grains and nearly 10 crore beneficiaries were covered under the Ayushman Bharat health insurance scheme.

New audio of BJP MLA facing sexual harassment allegations:Names UP Bahubali, says, ‘I’ll have them killed before they kill me’
stories.summary: A fresh audio clip allegedly featuring Sultanpur BJP MLA Vinod Singh, who is facing allegations of sexual harassment, surfaced on Friday. In the recording, the MLA is heard speaking to the woman who has accused him of attempting to rape her. During the conversation, he allegedly claims that two local strongmen, Sonu Singh and Monu Singh, are plotting to kill him and says he could have them killed before they act against him. The woman responds mostly with brief acknowledgements such as "Yes" and "Ji" throughout the conversation. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, the woman confirmed that the audio was genuine and said the conversation took place in May 2026. Woman has accused MLA of attempted rape On Wednesday, the woman accused the BJP legislator of attempting to rape her and threatening to kill her. She alleged that the MLA called her to his residence after threatening that her daughter would be raped if she refused to meet him. She further claimed that he attempted to sexually assault her, touched her private parts and tore her clothes. According to her complaint, she managed to push him away and escape. Excerpts from the alleged conversation Earlier audio had also surfaced Another audio clip had surfaced earlier in which the MLA was allegedly heard speaking to the woman's husband. In that conversation, the MLA says: Who are Sonu and Monu Singh? Vinod Singh has had a long-standing rivalry with brothers Chandrabhadra Singh, popularly known as Sonu Singh, and Yashbhadra Singh, known as Monu Singh. According to Monu Singh, he was attacked at a court premises in 2014, during which one Jainendra Sharma was arrested. He has alleged that police call detail records showed Vinod Singh was in regular contact with the attackers, leading to the MLA being named as an accused in the case. Sonu Singh was elected MLA twice, in 2002 and 2007, on a Samajwadi Party ticket. Monu Singh has served as a block chief. Their father, Indrabhadra Singh, was also an MLA from the Isauli Assembly constituency. According to the report, Indrabhadra Singh was murdered in 1996. In 2006, Sonu and Monu allegedly orchestrated the killing of Sant Gyaneshwar in retaliation for their father's murder. Monu Singh has reportedly faced around 19 criminal cases, including charges of murder, attempted murder, rioting and offences under the Gangster Act and Goonda Act. Woman's allegations The woman held a press conference in Delhi on July 3, accusing Vinod Singh of attempting to rape her and issuing death threats. She alleged that the MLA told her, "If you do not do as I say, I will ruin you." She further claimed that 12 to 15 people had been deployed to follow her and that she had received threats of an acid attack and threats to kill her husband and children. She said she had approached the police, but no action was taken on her complaint. MLA denies allegations Vinod Singh has denied all the allegations. He claimed that the woman's husband is facing cases of forgery and cheating and alleged that the accusations were fabricated to avoid arrest and to defame him. "I have full faith in the court. The truth will come out during the investigation," the MLA said.

Postmaster siphons off ₹1.4 crore from customers:Withdraws money from accounts and fixed deposits in Sambhal, issues fake receipts
stories.summary: An assistant postmaster who gambled with customers' money was arrested on Friday in Sambhal. He embezzled 1.4 crore rupees of account holders in the post office. According to the police, Deepak Kumar used to take the money deposited in customers' accounts and FDs. In return, he would give them fake receipts. The matter came to light when the police investigated after receiving complaints from customers. It was found that the accused had invested the embezzled amount of 1.40 crore rupees in online betting platforms like Dream-11. So far, 7 cases have been registered against the accused. The case is from the Bahjoi area. This entire case of fraud with customers is from the Bahjoi post office located in Chandausi tehsil. Bahjoi police on Friday arrested accused Deepak Kumar from the Bahjoi-Sambhal road. At 2:30 PM, SP Krishna Kumar Bishnoi and CO Stuti Singh disclosed the matter. According to the police, on August 6, several account holders had lodged a complaint at Bahjoi police station. Post office customers alleged that money was withdrawn from savings accounts without their knowledge. Police investigation revealed that Assistant Postmaster Deepak Kumar, a resident of Saimar Tola, used to withdraw money from accounts and issue fake receipts. On August 7, after receiving two more complaints, a total of 7 cases were registered against Deepak. Deepak returned money to some people on complaint Police investigation also revealed that the accused assistant postmaster had returned money to some account holders. The police are conducting a financial investigation into the entire matter. The police are also trying to ascertain whether the actual embezzled amount and the number of victims are not higher than this. The police are also investigating whether other employees of the Post Office department are involved in this embezzlement. SP Krishna Kumar Bishnoi said - Deepak Kumar was posted in Chandausi in 2023-24. After this, he was transferred to Bahjoi. The investigation revealed that he embezzled a total of 1 crore 40 lakh rupees. He used to take money from people for FD and savings accounts but did not give valid receipts for it. He used to invest that money in online betting.

stories.title: Atiq Ahmed's jailed sons granted parole for brother Abaan's funeral:Deputy CM Maurya brushes aside questions on fatal road crash
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court on Friday granted parole to slain gangster-turned-politician Atiq Ahmed's jailed sons, Ali and Umar, allowing them to attend the funeral of their younger brother, Abaan, who died in a road accident. The order was passed at around 3.30 pm. Ali is lodged in Jhansi Jail, while Umar is imprisoned in Lucknow Jail. Officials said it could take six to seven hours for the brothers to reach Prayagraj after the court order reaches the respective prisons. As a result, Abaan's burial may take place late on Friday night or on Saturday. Meanwhile, the family has kept Abaan's body in a deep freezer until the funeral. Will Shaista Parveen attend? Attention has also turned to whether Atiq Ahmed's wife, Shaista Parveen, will attend the funeral. Shaista has been absconding since 2023 and did not attend the funerals of either her husband Atiq Ahmed or her son Asad after their deaths. Abaan, 21, will be buried at the family's ancestral cemetery in Kasari-Masari, where Atiq Ahmed, his father Firoz Ahmed, brother Ashraf and son Asad are also buried. Deputy CM dismisses questions on Abaan's death During a visit to Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya was asked by reporters about Abaan's death. Responding briefly, he said road accidents occur every day and questioned why the incident was being treated differently. Abaan died while travelling to meet jailed brother Abaan died on Thursday morning in a road accident near Jhansi while travelling from Prayagraj to meet his brother Ali in jail. He was travelling in a Creta SUV with four friends when the driver reportedly tried to avoid an animal on the highway. The vehicle crashed into a road divider. Abaan and one of his friends, Sonu, died in the accident, while three others sustained injuries. Their bodies were brought from Jhansi to Hatwa village in Prayagraj by ambulance early on Friday morning. Family stores body until funeral The family has placed Abaan's body in a deep freezer at his aunt's residence in Hatwa village while waiting for the parole process to be completed. Two additional deep freezers have also reportedly been arranged to preserve the body until the funeral takes place. A family member who travelled to Jhansi to receive the body reportedly said, "He belonged to Allah, and Allah has taken him back," a remark similar to one made by Atiq Ahmed's brother Ashraf after the police encounter killing of Atiq's son Asad in 2023. According to family members, Ali, who is in jail, was devastated after learning of his younger brother's death and reportedly did not sleep or eat throughout the night.

stories.title: Protest in Lucknow with CRPF jawan’s body:Wife questions how he could shoot himself three times; vows to get commandant dismissed
stories.summary: The family of a Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) jawan staged a protest in Lucknow early Friday, placing his body on Budheshwar Crossing and blocking the Lucknow–Hardoi highway for nearly two hours. Senior police officers reached the spot and persuaded the family to end the protest. The body was later taken to the family's native village in Hardoi district for the last rites. Wife rejects suicide claim The deceased jawan, 37-year-old Vineet Singh, was posted with the 112th Battalion of the CRPF in Manipur. He died on August 5 after sustaining gunshot injuries under suspicious circumstances at the CRPF headquarters in Motbung. According to the official version, he died by suicide using his personal weapon. However, his wife, Neha Singh, disputed the claim, alleging that her husband could not have shot himself three times in the chest. "How can someone shoot himself three times in the chest? Someone else must have shot him," she said, demanding a fresh post-mortem and a thorough investigation. She also accused CRPF officers of harassing her husband and forcing him to remain on duty despite being unwell. See 3 pictures... 'He had fever but was not granted leave' Neha Singh said her husband had been telling her over the phone for several days that he was suffering from fever and severe leg pain but was still being made to perform duty. She recalled that he called her on the night of August 4 to say he was feeling better and was returning to duty. In the early hours of the next morning, she received a phone call asking whether she had spoken to him recently. When she enquired about what had happened, she was only told that he had been injured before the call was disconnected. She alleged that she would fight for justice, even if it meant travelling to Manipur, and vowed to seek the dismissal of the commanding officer. Family demands post-mortem report The family said the post-mortem report should be made public so the exact cause of death could be established. They maintained that they would continue their fight for justice until their demands were met. CRPF officials handed over an ex gratia amount of ₹1 lakh to the widow. Jawan joined CRPF in 2009 Vineet Singh, a resident of Purwa Bajirao village in Hardoi district, joined the CRPF in 2009. He had recently been transferred from Jammu and Kashmir to Manipur. His body was flown from Manipur to Lucknow on Friday morning before being taken to his ancestral village for cremation. The funeral was attended by CRPF personnel from the 93rd Battalion, led by Assistant Commandant R.K. Tripathi. His elder brother, Anil Singh, performed the last rites. Vineet is survived by his father Deshraj Singh, his wife Neha Singh and their 12-year-old son, Rudra Pratap. Father cuts short pilgrimage The jawan's father, Deshraj Singh, had been undertaking the Kanwar pilgrimage to Baba Baidyanath Dham when he received news of his son's death. He immediately abandoned the pilgrimage and returned home. Meanwhile, Neha Singh has been living in a rented house in Budheshwar, Lucknow, where she is raising and educating their son.
