stories.title: ‘My entire family is gone, how do I express this:Aman is sole survivor; says wait for government housing cost six lives in Pratapgarh house collapse
stories.summary: "No one can understand the pain of losing my family. In an instant, my whole world was destroyed... what can I say?" said Aman Srivastava from Pratapgarh, breaking down in tears. The young man, who had dreamed of building a better future with his loved ones, was forced to light the funeral pyres of six members of his own family, one after another, on Thursday. Speaking through tears, Aman said, "For the past five to six years, I had been trying to get a government house. I thought that once we got the house, I would celebrate my younger brother's wedding there. Now, neither the house nor my family is left." The tragedy struck at around 2am on Wednesday in Mahuli village, Pratapgarh. As heavy rain lashed the area, Pramod Srivastava's family was asleep in a room of their old, dilapidated house when two sections of the roof suddenly collapsed. Within moments, the entire family was buried beneath the debris. On Friday, Sadar MLA Rajendra Maurya visited Aman to offer his condolences. Calling the incident deeply tragic, he said the family had been applying for government housing for the past five years, but their application had reportedly been rejected twice. He assured that the matter would be investigated. Family lived in constant fear inside a crumbling house Aman said the family's house had become dangerously dilapidated. Plaster regularly fell from the ceilings and walls, leaving them fearful of a major accident. He said they had applied three times for government housing over the past five years, with two applications being rejected. According to Aman, their latest application under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) 2.0 had finally been approved, and officials had informed them that the funds would be credited within a month. "But before the money arrived, my entire family was taken away," he said. MLA promises probe into rejected housing applications Sadar MLA Rajendra Maurya described the incident as extremely unfortunate and said he would speak to the District Magistrate to investigate why the family's earlier housing applications had been rejected. He also announced that dilapidated buildings across the district would be surveyed to prevent similar tragedies and ensure that deserving families receive timely assistance. Sole survivor performs last rites of six family members After the post-mortem on Thursday at around 4.30pm, all six bodies were taken to the electric crematorium at Phaphamau Ganga Ghat in Prayagraj. Four adults were cremated separately, while the family's two young children were cremated together. Aman, the sole survivor, lit the funeral pyres of all six relatives with trembling hands. Overcome with grief, he fainted several times during the final rites and had to be supported by relatives and family members. Cousin seeks government job and compensation for Aman Aman's cousin, Ankur Srivastava, appealed to the government to provide Aman with a government job and financial compensation to help him rebuild his life. "Our entire family is now focused on helping Aman recover from this unimaginable loss. He has lost everyone. We are now his only support and will do everything possible to help him move forward," he said. See pictures of the accident- Family had returned from Mumbai only 18 months ago Pramod Srivastava had returned to his village around one-and-a-half years ago after leaving Mumbai, where he worked in medical marketing. After his health deteriorated, he moved back to Pratapgarh and began driving an e-rickshaw to support the family. His elder son Aman worked as an accountant at Mahuli Mandi. Pramod also ran a roadside vegetable stall. The family had slowly begun rebuilding their lives and had bought a new e-rickshaw about six weeks ago. They hoped their financial condition would improve and that they would soon be able to build a new home. ₹25 lakh raised by selling land, but new house never built The family owned around 13 biswa of land. About a year ago, Pramod sold three biswa, raising nearly ₹25 lakh to construct a new house. However, due to financial difficulties and other expenses, construction never began. Around 10 biswa of land still remained with the family. The family had also applied under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana. According to relatives, they submitted applications three times over the past six years. Two were rejected, while the third was still under process. Entire family shared a single room Although the house appeared large from the outside, it had become structurally unsafe over the years. Only one room remained habitable, and the entire family slept there every night on three cots. They had also set up a small prayer area inside the room and installed an air conditioner to cope with the heat and humidity. Aman had planned to ease his father's financial burden once their new house was built and provide a better life for the family. Those dreams ended with the collapse. According to relatives, Pramod had planned to return to Mumbai and had booked a train ticket for 10 August. On the day of the accident, he had asked Aman to cancel the ticket. 6 members of the same family lost their lives, pictures- How the family's world collapsed in the early hours of Wednesday Six members of the same family were killed after their nearly 100-year-old house collapsed in Mahuli Mohalla under Nagar Kotwali police station limits in Pratapgarh during heavy rain on Wednesday night. All seven family members had been sleeping together in an air-conditioned room because of the heat and humidity. At around 2am, the roof suddenly gave way. The collapse was so sudden that no one had time to react or even call for help. Those killed were house owner Pramod Srivastava (60), his wife Rita (55), younger son Nitin (25), daughter-in-law Madhuri (23), and their two sons, Madhav (2) and Advik (10 months). According to preliminary findings, the victims died after being crushed under the debris and suffocating. The only survivor, 28-year-old Aman Srivastava, somehow managed to crawl out from the rubble and raised the alarm. Police and fire brigade teams rushed to the scene. After a rescue operation lasting around two hours, all seven family members were pulled from the debris and taken to the district hospital, where doctors declared six of them dead. The post-mortem found that several victims had suffered fatal internal injuries and multiple fractures. Aman is currently undergoing treatment in hospital. He is now the sole survivor of a family of seven.

stories.title: 'Babua will remain a child all his life':Yogi takes jibe at Akhilesh; says 'Evening gatherings were routine, change requires hitting the ground'
stories.summary: On National Handloom Day, CM Yogi Adityanath said that those who held power in the state before 2017 had no vision for development. When people in power are not interested in work, the state's deterioration is inevitable. Due to this irresponsibility, the state remained engulfed in months of curfews and riots. Innocent children died from diseases like encephalitis and dengue. Without naming the SP chief, Yogi took a jibe, saying: Some people get associated with a word in life that they can never shake off. Some people remain children throughout their lives. Babua was also like that. He would wake up at 12 noon, get ready by 2 pm, go to the gym at 5 pm, and by 7 pm the gathering would be in full swing. Then how could he think about the state's development? Read the key points from CM Yogi's speech Vote bank politics worsened the situation before 2017 The Chief Minister said that before the BJP government was formed in the country in 2014 and in UP in 2017, work for the development of artisans could have been done, but it requires thinking and vision. He listed three shortcomings of the SP government- 1- Deterioration of education: Earlier, basic schools were in bad condition. There was neither arrangement for drinking water nor toilets. Today, schools are providing bags, uniforms, and modern facilities. PM Modi's 'Nipun Bharat Abhiyan' is being implemented on the ground. 2. Security and Infrastructure: Before 2017, the state had neither electricity, nor roads, nor law and order. Daughters and traders were not safe. When markets remain deserted, it affects every artisan, woman, and youth. 3. Plunder and Insecurity: Previous governments had no interest in development works; there was just a race for plunder within the dynasty, and they themselves posed a threat to women's safety. Handloom and Handicrafts received a new identity CM Yogi stated that the handloom and powerloom industry is UP's great heritage. About 30 lakh people's livelihoods are connected to it, of which 70% are women workers. Last year, the government provided electricity facilities worth ₹109 crores to 40 thousand artisans. Before 2017, Bhadohi's carpet cluster had become almost inactive. Today, exports worth crores of rupees are happening from there to world markets. Prime Minister Narendra Modi himself took the initiative and had Bhadohi carpets laid in the country's new Parliament building. When we appreciate the sweat of our artisans and encourage them, the country's money will remain in the country and prosperity will reach directly to the homes of craftspeople. 'Chief Minister and Ministers have to descend into the field' CM Yogi said in the end that the transformation of the state is possible when the Chief Minister himself takes out time to visit every district and ministers go to ground zero. In our government, every scheme is reaching directly to the public without any discrimination and vote bank politics.

stories.title: Car gutted in Lucknow, youth burnt alive:Only skeleton left by the time fire brigade arrived; one hand found stuck in seat
stories.summary: A young man was burnt to death in a Maruti Zen car that caught fire around 11:30 PM on Thursday night in Lucknow. He could not get out of the car after it caught fire. By the time the fire brigade brought the fire under control, only his skeleton remained inside the car. The accident occurred near Saraiya Mod in the Bakshi Ka Talab (BKT) area. According to the police, the cause of the car fire is not yet clear. It is also not known whether the car caught fire while moving or if it was stationary at the time. The body has been sent for post-mortem. Young man's body found burnt on the driving seat ACP Vikas Pandey said that at around 11:30 PM, information was received about a car catching fire on the highway. When the police and fire brigade reached the spot, the car was completely engulfed in flames. After extinguishing the fire, when the car door was opened, a completely burnt body of a person was found on the driving seat. Only a skeleton remained on the seat. The forensic team was called upon receiving the information, and they collected evidence from the scene. In the initial investigation, the body could not be identified. Police identified based on car number Based on the car's number, the police traced its owner. Investigation revealed that the car was registered in the name of Almash, son of Hamidul, a resident of Khurramnagar. Upon contacting the family, it was confirmed that the body found inside the car was that of 32-year-old Almash. The ACP stated that the family is being interrogated. The cause of the car fire has not yet been clarified. The matter is being investigated keeping all aspects in mind. Another body found inside a car in Ashiana Meanwhile, the body of a person was recovered from an abandoned Swift Dzire car at Salenagar intersection in Ashiana police station area around 11:57 PM on Thursday night. According to local residents, the car had been parked on the roadside for the past three days. When a strong foul smell emanated from it on Thursday night, people informed the police. Upon receiving the information, Ashiana police reached the spot, took possession of the car, and started an investigation. During the search, the body was found inside the car. According to the police, the car's registration number is UP 33 BB 8989. The body was identified as Gyanendra Singh, son of Uday Bhan Singh, a resident of Niralanagar, Raebareli.

stories.title: VIDEO | 2 groups of schoolgirls clash outside Gorakhpur school:Argument escalates to physical altercation, hair-pulling
stories.summary: On Wednesday evening, after school hours, a fierce fight broke out between two groups of girl students at the gate of an inter college located in Chargaon, Shahpur area of Gorakhpur. First, there was an argument, which quickly escalated into a physical altercation. Someone viralized a video of this street fight on social media. It is being reported that on Wednesday evening around 4 PM, after school hours, the girl students came out of the school. During this, an argument started between two students over some issue. According to eyewitnesses, as the dispute escalated, students from one side started verbally abusing and physically assaulting the other student. During the incident, a crowd of passersby and other students gathered outside the school gate. Attempts were made to intervene, but both sides continued to clash with each other. Principal said - Investigation underway The school principal stated that as soon as information about the incident was received, the matter was taken seriously. On Thursday, the students involved in the dispute did not come to school. The entire matter is being investigated. Action will be taken as per rules if found guilty. The police say that no complaint has been received from either side so far. An investigation is also being conducted based on the video. The school administration has appealed to students and parents to maintain discipline.

stories.title: Auto-rickshaw driver's body found in Varuna river:Son says, 'Cop had been following him for three days'; police probe underway
stories.summary: A commotion erupted after the body of an auto driver was found in the Varuna River near Varuna Bridge in the Cantt police station area of Varanasi. The Kachahri outpost in-charge had reached the spot with police force upon receiving information about an abandoned auto standing on Varuna Bridge. A bottle of acid was found inside the auto. Following this, when police started searching, a body was found floating in the Varuna River. The police then informed the family members using the auto's number, retrieved the body, and sent it to the mortuary. The deceased's son, who reached the spot, alleged that his father had said that some policeman had been following him for three days. Meanwhile, police have started investigating the case. The causes of the incident are being ascertained through CCTV footage. Police arrived upon receiving information about an abandoned auto People had informed the Cantt police station that an abandoned auto bearing number UP 65 ET 8037 was standing on Varuna Bridge, with a bottle of acid kept in the front. The Kachahri outpost in-charge immediately reached the spot and gathered information about the auto, which was found to be registered in the name of Rajendra Prasad Gupta. On this, the chowki in-charge called, and they informed that their auto is driven by Gyanchand Sonkar. His number was taken and his family members were called. Boy who reached the spot made allegations After receiving information, Gyanchand Sonkar's son Ashish Sonkar reached the spot. Police got the auto identified. After that, when searched, a body was found floating in the Varuna. His son Ashish identified it as Gyanchand. Ashish said that during Sawan, everyone had gone to Ayodhya but father had not gone. For the past three days, he was saying that some policeman was following him. And today his body has been found. Police engaged in investigation Cantt Thana in-charge Raj Kishore Pandey said - The body has been taken out of the water and sent to the mortuary. The post-mortem of the body will be conducted today. Further action will be taken based on the statement of the family members. Meanwhile, police are checking CCTV footage.

stories.title: Abaan Ahmed suffered ruptured liver and lungs, broken ribs:Died from 23 injuries, post-mortem reveals; brother broke down upon seeing body
stories.summary: 23 injuries were found on the body of Abaan (21), son of mafia Atiq Ahmed, in Jhansi. The post-mortem report revealed that his liver, lungs, and spleen ruptured due to a high-impact collision. His ribs were also broken. He died due to excessive internal bleeding. Meanwhile, Sonu, Abaan's companion who was sitting behind Aban's seat in the car, died due to a fractured skull. Fractures were found in both his arms. Both were post-mortemed by a panel of 3 doctors at Jhansi Medical College on Thursday night at 11:30 PM. Aban's elder brother, Ahjam, reached inside the post-mortem house. Seeing the body of his brother Aban, he burst into tears. Relatives consoled him. After this, he asked the police for the post-mortem report. Officials said they would provide the report later. After the post-mortem, Ahjam, along with relatives, placed both bodies in the same ambulance. They departed for Prayagraj with the bodies at 12 AM. Both will be cremated today. On Thursday, Abaan was going to meet his elder brother Ali Ahmed, who is imprisoned in Abaan Jhansi Jail. Four friends were with him in the Creta car. His car collided with the divider in the Poonch area, 70 km before Jhansi on the Jhansi-Kanpur Highway. Aban and Sonu died in the accident. His 3 friends Umar Ahmed, Mohammad Zaid and Farooq Ahjam were injured. Dr. Rajneesh, who conducted the post-mortem, said- Both died due to injuries sustained in the accident. First, Aban's body was post-mortemed. After this, Sonu's body was post-mortemed. Both were post-mortemed along with Dr. Pankaj Mustaria and Dr. Zia Zafar. See 2 pictures of the accident- So much internal bleeding occurred in Abaan's body that it came out of his mouth. Aban was sitting in the front seat of the car. His friend Zaid was driving the car. Sonu was sitting behind Abaan. The car, travelling at a speed of about 120 km/h, hit the divider on the side where Abaan was sitting. This is why Aban sustained the most injuries in the accident. Shortly after the collision, Abaan and Sonu died on the spot. Eyewitness Deepak Yadav, who was the first to arrive after the accident, said - I heard the noise and was the first to reach. I tried to open the car door, but it wouldn't open. After that, I brought a crowbar (iron rod) from a house and broke the door. Deepak said - After opening the door, I first pulled out a young man. His mouth was full of blood. He said - My name is Aban, save me. After this, he became unconscious. Aban had left Prayagraj for Jhansi at 5 AM on Thursday. The Creta car hit the divider in the Poonch police station area. The impact was so strong that the car was thrown about 7 feet into the air. Its pieces were scattered about 40 feet across the highway. The left side of the car was severely damaged. Brother said - Let the brothers be brought for burial Upon receiving news of Abaan's death in the accident, his elder brother Ahjam reached Jhansi from Prayagraj. First, he reached the accident site and gathered information from the police. After this, he went directly to Jhansi Medical College. Here, he met all three injured. Ahjam said - Let the brothers be brought for burial. After Ahjam arrived, the police completed the inquest for both bodies and conducted post-mortems. Ahjam has also given a written complaint to the police, based on which the police may register a case. Sonu's brother-in-law, who arrived in Jhansi from Satna to collect Sonu's body, said - Sonu used to work with trailers. He had come home from Dubai some time ago. Here too, he was working with trailers. But currently, due to the Kanwariyas, work has stopped. He was a friend of car driver Zaid and other companions. That's why he was coming to Jhansi. Cigarettes, shoes and two books found in the car According to Jhansi police, the forensic team found cigarette packets, shoes, and two books in the car. These include 'The Idiot' and 'The Stationery Shop of Tehran'. According to the police, it is possible that Aban was carrying these items for his brother Ali. Abaan was sitting in the front seat of the car, while his companion Zaid was driving. Zaid is the son-in-law of Atiq's maternal cousin sister. He had received this car as a wedding gift. Now only 3 of Atiq's 5 sons remain Atiq Ahmed had 5 sons. Abaan was the youngest. One son, Asad, was killed in a police encounter in Jhansi in 2023. Now there are three sons. Among them, the elder son, Umar, is imprisoned in Lucknow Jail, and the second, Ali, is in Jhansi Jail. While Ahzam, older than Abaan, is currently pursuing his graduation. He has reached Jhansi. Seeing the body, he said, "Let the brothers be brought to the soil (buried)." Lawyer Umesh Pal was murdered in Prayagraj in February 2023. In this case, Atiq, imprisoned in Gujarat Jail, and his brother Ashraf, from Bareilly Jail, were brought to Prayagraj for a court appearance. There, on April 15, 2023, Atiq and Ashraf were murdered in police custody. Atiq's wife, Shaista, is currently absconding. Abaan's mother Shaista, carrying a reward of 50 thousand, is absconding Atiq's wife Shaista Parveen has been absconding since 2023. There is a reward of 50 thousand on her. There are 6 cases. Shaista did not attend the funerals of both her son Asad, after his encounter, and her husband Atiq, after his murder. Ashraf's wife Zainab is also absconding. Questions are being raised about whether Shaista will attend Aban's funeral. Murder took place in police custody Lawyer Umesh Pal was murdered in Prayagraj in February 2023. In this case, Atiq, who was imprisoned in a Gujarat jail, and his brother Ashraf, from Bareilly jail, were brought to Prayagraj for a hearing. There, on April 15, 2023, Atiq and Ashraf were murdered in police custody. Atiq's wife Shaista is currently absconding.

stories.title: Rain lashes Lucknow, highway flooded in Farrukhabad:River swallows 50 acres in Lakhimpur; rainfall 150% above normal in 24 hours
stories.summary: The spell of monsoon rain continues across Uttar Pradesh. Lucknow received rain early on Friday, while around 40 cities, including Agra and Jaunpur, remained cloudy. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for all 75 districts today, with a heavy rainfall warning for 18 districts. According to the IMD, the state has received 19.3 mm of rainfall, which is 150% above the normal 7.8 mm. Heavy rain on Thursday evening inundated homes and schools in Bijnor. Waterlogging was reported on a national highway in Farrukhabad and in several residential areas. In Rae Bareli, a road caved in after the rain, leaving a three-foot-deep crater. Rivers are also in spate due to continuous rainfall. In Lakhimpur Kheri, the Sharda River has eroded around 50 acres of land so far. In Ballia, 27 houses have been washed away by the Saryu River. In Farrukhabad, the Ganga has risen close to the danger mark, with floodwater entering 33 villages and 40 government schools. The Ganga is also flowing above normal levels in Varanasi. Floodwater has entered 40–50 small temples, while the Ratneshwar Mahadev Temple is more than half submerged. A crocodile was spotted roaming on flooded roads in Lakhimpur Kheri. Forest department officials also rescued a Russell's viper that had entered a house and released it into the forest. Meanwhile, more than 20 cities, including Lucknow, Saharanpur and Meerut, received rainfall on Thursday morning. Due to continuous rain and rain-related incidents over the past three days, schools up to Class 8 have been closed. Rain-related accidents have also continued. In Barabanki, a dilapidated wall collapsed on five children on their way to a madrasa. All five were trapped under the debris. A 7-year-old boy and his 14-year-old sister died, while the other three children were rescued by villagers and taken to hospital. In Pratapgarh, a 100-year-old house collapsed amid continuous rain, killing 13 members of the same family. See pictures of floods and rain... Lucknow weather scientist Atul Kumar Singh said- The monsoon system has now become active over UP. It is passing through Delhi, Lucknow and Patna. Due to this, several cyclones have become active. Monsoon winds have reached the plains of the Ganges. Due to its effect, there will be heavy rainfall across the state for the next 4 to 5 days.

stories.title: Senior officials spared, juniors punished over Kanpur Expressway mess:Responsible officers cleared files blindly, without inspecting the site
stories.summary: The dilapidated condition of the country's most expensive Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway has ruined the image of the Union Ministry of Road Transport. The department and NHAI (National Highways Authority of India) are facing disrepute all around. NHAI had to blacklist the construction company of a BJP leader's brother. In a hurry, the Authority tried to show by taking action against some officers that it would not spare those responsible. But the truth is that there are others responsible on whom no action has been taken. Because when the expressway was being built for a long time, what were the officers sitting above doing? Did they check the quality or allow morang and asphalt to be laid based on estimates? Are those responsible for the shoddy construction being protected? In this report by Dainik Bhaskar, we will tell who else is responsible for this. First, let's tell which 3 officers NHAI held responsible and took action against them- Major culprits of the irregularity, against whom no action was taken Responsibility - NHAI's Regional Officer Gautam is based in Lucknow. His job is to monitor NHAI projects in UP and conduct quality checks through periodic site visits. Negligence - Initially, the first defect came to light on July 26. Then he tried to suppress the matter. He said there was a problem with bitumen (coal tar) in a small area. After the matter got out of hand, action was taken against the Project Manager and the Director. Dainik Bhaskar tried to contact Vishal Gautam. The call was answered, but immediately disconnected. When called again, the phone was not picked up. Responsibility - After Saurabh Chaurasia, Sharad became the Project Director of the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway and remained in this position for about 1 year. He was responsible for managing important technical arrangements during construction. Negligence - During his tenure, instead of inspecting the quality by visiting the site, he blindly trusted files and reports. Due to less visits to ground zero, he kept approving every file with 'OK', overlooking construction deficiencies. Dainik Bhaskar tried to contact him, but it was not possible. Responsibility - He is the head of PNC Infratech, the company building the expressway. The company is named after 3 brothers - Pradeep, Naveen, and Chakresh. Naveen Jain is a Rajya Sabha MP from BJP. Negligence - Secured a two-phase tender by bidding a total of ?2926 crore, but paid no attention to site monitoring and quality control during construction. No concrete information could be found about them either. Could not be contacted despite efforts. Now know about two cases of irregularities, in which the company owner was held responsible- What was the responsibility of the officials against whom action was taken? Responsibility- He was the highest-ranking officer for construction work in the field. It was his responsibility to get every layer of soil and gravel inspected and send the report upwards. Negligence- Ignored quality and committed irregularities in the field. Action- On July 30, NHAI removed him from the project and banned him for 2 years. Responsibility- He remained Project Director from the start of construction until 2024. The maximum construction happened during his tenure. Negligence- Instead of inspecting on-site, he blindly trusted PNC's reports. The foundation of irregularities was laid during his time. Action- NHAI has issued a charge sheet, framing the charges. Responsibility- Posted in the position for the last 1 year. The work was completed and inaugurated during his tenure. Negligence- 95% of the Greenfield area work was completed a year ago. Still, they gave an 'all okay' report without checking the quality. Action- Removed from NHAI and attached to PWD. 3 Crores Spent to Repair Sunken Expressway According to NHAI, 3 crores have been spent so far on the repair of the 63 km long expressway. This cost will be borne by PNC Infratech. The company has also been fined 2% of the performance security. The negligence of Theme Engineering Services Private Limited, which monitors the quality of construction, has come to light. Therefore, this company will be excluded from future projects. NHAI itself is getting the quality checked After the embarrassment, NHAI will now get the expressway inspected with a laser profilometer. This technique uses a laser beam to measure the texture, roughness, and height of an object's surface. It creates an accurate 3D map of the surface without touching it, which will precisely reveal the irregularities. How is a non-performer company building the Bahraich Expressway? NHAI admitted that earthwork, drainage, and quality were overlooked. Still, NHAI officials avoided taking action against the company. PNC has been awarded the work for the expressway from Barabanki to Bahraich. PNC has also been given the work of constructing a flyover inside Lucknow city. PNC Company's 'Tarnished' Record

stories.title: Atiq Ahmed's son writhed in car for 2 minutes:'My name is Abaan, save me'; eyewitness recounts final moments
stories.summary: "My name is Abaan... save me." Only this much could come out of his mouth. People pulled him out of the car, but within two minutes of struggling, his breathing stopped. These were the last words of mafia Atiq Ahmed's youngest son Aban Ahmed (21). Abaan was going to meet his brother Ali, who was imprisoned in Jhansi jail. He had also bought two romantic novels for his brother. When Ali received the news of the accident in jail, he started crying. Abaan was very dear to him. Perhaps this was the reason why Abaan had met Ali 49 times in 10 months. Dainik Bhaskar's team spoke with eyewitnesses, the injured, and police. Read the complete story of the last moments of the accident... First, let's understand how the accident happened? Abaan Ahmed left for Jhansi, 400 kilometers away from Prayagraj, around 5 AM on Thursday with his 2 friends and 2 relatives. But an accident occurred 70 kilometers before reaching there. Near Khilli village in Poonch, while trying to save a calf that suddenly appeared on the highway, the Creta car went out of control. It crashed into a concrete wall built on the roadside. At that time, the car was traveling at a speed of about 120. The collision was so severe that the car flew about 7 feet in the air and its pieces scattered up to 40 feet on the highway. In the accident, Abaan and his friend Sonu died on the spot, while three people were injured. Broke car doors with rods and pulled people out Eyewitness Sakesh said, ''I was working at my shop. Suddenly there was a loud explosion. It felt like something had burst. Several people present around the shop ran to the spot. Saw that there was a severe car collision. Immediately called 112 and got an ambulance. Until the ambulance and police arrived, we ourselves got engaged in rescuing the injured and trapped people. The car doors were jammed. Before the police arrived, we broke the doors with iron rods and pulled out the injured. Later, the police and ambulance took them to the hospital.'' Accident while trying to save a calf, car crashed into wall Eyewitness Deepak Yadav said - I was going from home to the field. Then I saw that a calf was crossing the highway. To save it, the car driver turned the vehicle to the left. Meanwhile, a biker came, and to save him, the car driver turned the car even more to the left. The very next moment, the car crashed into a wall built on the roadside. Some people came running. The injured were pulled out of the car. One injured person's mouth was filled with blood. When we asked his name, he said, "My name is Abaan. Save me." After this, he didn't say anything. His breathing stopped. 10 minutes after calling, the police arrived at the spot. The police took all the injured to the hospital in an ambulance. One part of the car was damaged; Aban-Sonu were sitting on this side According to the police, 5 people were sitting in the car. Mohammad Zaid (35) was driving the vehicle, and Abaan Ahmad (21) was sitting next to him. Sonu (24) was on the seat behind Abaan. Next to Sonu were Umar Ahmad (18) and Farooq Ahjam (28). The car was running close to the middle divider. The car crashed into a concrete wall built on the roadside towards the village. The front part was completely shattered. All airbags deployed. The left side of the car was more damaged. Abaan was sitting in the front on this side, and Sonu was sitting in the back. Both sitting on the left side died on the spot. Aban suffered serious head injuries. His hands and legs were broken. Aban-Sonu kept writhing in pain for 2 to 5 mins Eyewitness Ramakant said - Abaan and Sonu kept struggling for about two to five minutes, then their breathing stopped. Ambulance driver Pravesh said - All the injured were brought to CHC Moth. From there, I brought one injured person, Umar, to Jhansi Medical College. He had a fracture in his hand. The condition of all three injured was normal; they were talking. Village head Brijesh Kumar said - The car hit the divider due to loss of balance. The car's speed was high. After the accident, about 50 villagers and I reached the spot. Injured Mohammad Umar said - Car hit the divider Mohammad Umar, injured in the accident, said - The car was at high speed. Suddenly, after losing control, it crashed into the divider. The collision was so severe that Abaan and his friend Sonu died on the spot. Umar was not informed about brother Abaan's death Lucknow Jail's Jailer Ritwik Priyadarshi said - Atiq's elder son Umar has not been informed about Abaan's death. Information is given only as per the protocol prescribed in the jail. Family members have contacted lawyers of Prayagraj District Court to allow Atiq Ahmed's two sons imprisoned in jail to participate in Abaan's funeral. The lawyers replied that a parole application will have to be filed in the High Court. Two books and cigarette pack found in the car The Creta car (UP70 FW2432) belongs to Zaid; it was received as a wedding gift. Zaid is the son-in-law of Atiq's khaleri, that is, his maternal cousin sister. Two books were found in the car - 'The Stationery Shop of Tehran' and 'The Idiot'. Besides this, a cigarette pack was also found. Was going to meet Ali in jail with friends and relatives See pictures related to the accident- Brother left with the body late at night after post-mortem Abaan's body was kept in the post-mortem house of Jhansi Medical College. After the post-mortem, the body was handed over to brother Ahjam. Abaan will be buried next to Atiq's grave in Prayagraj on Friday.

stories.title: Brij Bhushan says, 'Priyanka was misled into turning against him':'It was only a good touch-bad touch allegation'; vows to return to Parliament
stories.summary: Former BJP MP from Uttar Pradesh Brij Bhushan Singh staged a show of strength on Thursday and spoke to Dainik Bhaskar about the women wrestlers' sexual harassment allegations, the alleged conspiracy, and politics. He said, "They turned a matter of good touch and bad touch into a movement. Posters appeared in Canada and the US. Some people were working behind the scenes. Bhupinder Singh Hooda and Deepender Singh Hooda misled Priyanka Gandhi, who then joined the movement." Referring to his political future, he added, "Everything is fine now. The Parliament I was once not allowed to enter, I will return to that very Parliament." Read the full interview... After a long legal battle, court acquitted you; what would you say? Brij Bhushan: This entire matter was about 'good touch-bad touch'. I garlanded some players and gave medals to others, and I touched or hugged them after they won a wrestling match. Later, it was said that they were uncomfortable during that time. But this was turned into such a big movement, as if something very serious had happened. There were poster wars and candle marches against me even in Canada and America. Priyanka Gandhi, farmer leaders, and even Khalistanis sitting in Canada got involved in this. It was given a caste and regional color. You are continuously talking about conspiracy; according to you, who were the people behind it? Brij Bhushan: In this conspiracy, some faces were visible in front, and some were behind the curtain. If I have to name them, the most prominent role was played by Bhupinder Singh Hooda and Deepender Singh Hooda. They also misled senior Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi and connected her to this movement. Apart from this, many big lawyers, big capitalists, and a large part of the opposition were involved in it. Politics and wrestling- was there an attempt to snatch both in this conspiracy? Brijbhushan: You can say that, but an even more serious attempt was to destroy my character. Character assassination of any person is the biggest sin. The athletes who made the allegations were on the world and Olympic level, so the wrong message went out to the entire world. But after the court's decision, the truth is now in front of everyone. Will you now make an active comeback in both politics and wrestling? Brijbhushan. Where did I go? Neither from politics nor from society. I had said earlier that I will definitely return one day to the Parliament where attempts were made to stop me from entering. I am fully confident that my return to Parliament is certain. What do you think is the reason for the way people came out in your support in Ayodhya? Brijbhushan: This is not support of one day. This is the result of my nearly 50 years of penance. Since the age of 17-18, I have been working among people for public issues. The crowd that was seen on the roads today is the result of that long social and political relationship. Saints on your platform raised the issue of misuse of laws related to women; what would you say? Brij Bhushan: Laws are extremely necessary for the safety and security of women and daughters, but if they are being misused, then there should be serious discussion on it. Saints have raised this issue; if public support is built in society, then further discussion will happen. For now, there is no plan for any movement. What is your view on opposition parties and movements happening in the country? Brij Bhushan: The job of the opposition is to raise public issues. But an old party like Congress has not conducted any major movement under its own banner in the last 10 years. They only mislead people by joining others' movements, whether it's the farmers' movement, the wrestlers' issue, or recent movements.

stories.title: Safety vs privacy: How domestic-help platforms are building a two-way support system
stories.summary: The landscape of domestic help services in India is evolving as platforms aim to bolster user trust and safety. Emphasizing security, these services are implementing background checks and defining service hours. Furthermore, innovations such as AI technology and body cameras are continuously being assessed to improve safety measures. Moving forward, the success of the industry will depend on creating a trustworthy environment amidst its traditionally informal nature.

stories.title: Pests, mould, live insects: FSSAI suspends license of two food units
ICE rolls out body cameras, but policy lets agency decide which footage goes public
Supriya Sule opposes FCRA Bill, urges Centre to withdraw it or send it to JPC
stories.summary: Supriya Sule opposes the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, in its current form. She urges the government to withdraw the proposed legislation or send it to a Joint Parliamentary Committee. Foreign funding should not be viewed with automatic suspicion, she stated during her remarks. Sule also commented on youth protests and disputes over political party symbols. The NCP (SP) leader awaits a hearing on the party's legal battle.

stories.title: Explainer: What changes as Parliament passes Registration of Births and Deaths Bill
JPSC, E20, anti-reservation: The issues India is talking about
A Swedish couple moved into the dream home in Malmö; three years later, they left it behind for a rural home in Japan
stories.summary: After recently selling their newly constructed home in Sweden, a Swedish couple has made the bold decision to embrace a fresh start by purchasing an empty residence in Japan. This significant change stems from their evolving family aspirations and a burgeoning affection for Asia. They are now excited to undertake renovations on their Japanese abode while immersing themselves in the enchanting culture and scenery of Japan.

stories.title: Flesh-eating bacteria kill 5 in Louisiana, health officials warn beachgoers as all cases are linked to seawater
Who is Sunder Katwala? Indian-origin writer appointed to UK community funding body
21 of 57 TN MPs attend CM Vijay’s meet, reject Delimitation Bill; DMK, AIADMK stay away
India to recover 'Green Boots' climber's body from Everest after 30 years: Report
'We stand in solidarity': CJP delegation reaches Ranchi to support students protesting JPSC, JSSC exams
US Democrats eye probes into Trump-linked firms over impeachment if they regain House control: Report
stories.summary: In a significant move, US House Democrats are gearing up for extensive investigations into the business practices of the Trump administration. Their strategy involves utilizing hearings and subpoenas to scrutinize decisions made that may have led to personal gains. Major corporations such as Apple and Alphabet might find themselves under examination for their regulatory and contractual engagements.

stories.title: 'End this war': Senate Democrats turn up heat on Trump, seek end to Iran hostilities
stories.summary: Democrats introduced a resolution to end unauthorized US military involvement against Iran. Senator John Hickenlooper leads the effort, citing constitutional war powers. This move escalates a congressional challenge to President Donald Trump's handling of the conflict. Military leaders privately advise seeking an off-ramp from ongoing air operations. President Trump expresses confidence that the confrontation could end soon.

stories.title: Utah wildfire: Helicopter with 2 onboard crashes while fighting massive blaze
'Which freedom fighter received most severe punishment?' Kerala orders probe into Savarkar quiz
stories.summary: A school quiz question in Kerala has ignited a political controversy. The question asked about the freedom fighter receiving the most severe British punishment. General education minister N Samsudheen ordered an inquiry into the unauthorized quiz. Opposition parties accused the government of promoting a Sangh Parivar agenda. Officials are investigating who prepared and conducted the quiz.

stories.title: American entrepreneur says 'I'm shocked but honestly not surprised' as US plans to remove 60-day grace period for H-1Bs
'Army safeguarding territory': Arunachal CM Pema Khandu rejects Chinese encroachment
Evening newswrap: Mayawati hits Akhilesh over 'Pandit' twist in SP's PDA formula; IT ministry asks Meta to revamp algorithms & more
Syrian spy chief accused of 2015 'Children's Massacre' hiding in Moscow: Report
Korean proverb of the day and its lessons: 'If you don't walk today, you must run tomorrow'
A new Kansas law now bars students from accessing phones, earbuds and smartwatches all school day
stories.summary: Many states are banning smartphones in schools due to growing distractions and health concerns. Some districts now restrict student phone access from morning bell to afternoon dismissal. Parents are increasingly supporting these bans, citing research and developmental appropriateness. Concerns also focus on excessive screen time and inappropriate content accessed on school devices. Schools are now reviewing technology policies and limiting device usage during non-instructional periods.

stories.title: SAD backs women's quota, delimitation bills after Badal-PM Modi meet fuels buzz
stories.summary: Shiromani Akali Dal has expressed strong support for the prompt enactment of the women's reservation bill, emphasizing the need for fair delimitation to ensure equitable state representation. This advocacy follows a meeting between party president Sukhbir Singh Badal and Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Speculation is rife regarding a potential electoral partnership between SAD and BJP, particularly as both parties have faced declining influence in Punjab's political landscape.

stories.title: 56 decomposing bodies found at Chicago funeral home; owner’s licence suspended
Senate confirms Trump’s ex-lawyer Todd Blanche as US Attorney General
Colorado teen Jude Kofie taught himself piano at 10; now his debut album is out after $15,000 gift
stories.summary: Colorado teenager Jude Kofie has released his debut album, showcasing his piano skills. He taught himself to play the piano by ear at age ten. A generous piano tuner gifted him a valuable instrument and professional lessons. His album features diverse musical styles, including jazz and gospel influences. This release marks a significant milestone in his developing musical career.

stories.title: IT ministry asks Meta to revamp algorithms, submit roadmap to tackle deepfakes
'Congress not realising own errors': Rijiju draws parallel with Indira Gandhi post Emergency
stories.summary: Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju criticized the Congress party for its perceived lack of self-awareness. He contrasted the current leadership with former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's admission of Emergency actions. Rahul Gandhi questioned the delay in implementing the Women's Reservation Bill. He urged its immediate implementation without linking it to delimitation. The bill's passage and subsequent implementation remain a point of contention.

stories.title: Greenland issues ‘strong warning’ over Arctic drilling by Trump-linked firm
stories.summary: A US oil firm has moved equipment to Greenland without local approval. This action occurs while President Trump seeks greater US influence over the territory. Greenland's government issued a strong warning regarding the unauthorized logistical operation. The company plans to drill for oil, which faces environmental and political questions. The situation highlights Greenland's resource development authority amid US strategic interests.

stories.title: 'A morning I will cherish': Raghav Chadha's first social media post with PM Modi
Congress lost the millennials. Can it win over Gen Z?
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi is focusing on forging a bond with the youth ahead of the 2029 elections, recognizing that Gen Z will be a key voting bloc.

stories.title: US Senate passes stopgap funding bill to avert shutdown ahead of midterms
stories.summary: In a decisive move, the US Senate has passed a temporary spending bill aimed at funding government operations until December eleventh. This crucial legislation is designed to avert a government shutdown just before the midterm elections. Key components of the bill address border patrol funding as requested by Democrats and extend the deadline for enforcing a federal prohibition on certain hemp products by a month.

stories.title: 10-year-old baker's grand champion cake fetches $15,000 at Maryland county fair auction
stories.summary: At a recent county fair auction, a remarkable cake created by 10-year-old baker Herbie Martin IV fetched an astounding $15,000. Herbie dedicated countless late-night hours to master his delightful lemon blueberry recipe. This impressive sale contributed to an overall fundraising goal, raising more than $100,000 for upcoming fairs and youth initiatives, with Herbie's cake standing out as the highlight of the event.

stories.title: Green Bank Radio Restrictions: Tiny US town lives under radio-silence laws
US officials will not release cool water from Glen Canyon Dam this year, protecting hydropower while threatening humpback chub
stories.summary: This year, federal officials have decided against releasing cool water from the Colorado River reservoirs, emphasizing the need for hydropower production over the conservation of a threatened fish species. The river and its reservoirs are facing severe depletion from overuse and climate change, while states have been unable to reach a long-term agreement on water sharing. Utilities welcomed this choice, citing concerns over the costs of alternative energy sources.

stories.title: 'Changing colours like a chameleon': Mayawati hits Akhilesh over 'Pandit' twist in SP's PDA formula
stories.summary: BSP chief Mayawati criticized the Samajwadi Party's changing political stance. She accused the SP of altering its PDA formula for electoral gains. Mayawati stated the SP now targets Brahmin voters after noticing BSP's growing support. She urged all communities to remain vigilant against SP's casteist politics. Such deceptive strategies offer short-term benefits but not societal welfare.

stories.summary: Zebra mussels are proliferating swiftly in Spain's aquatic systems, resulting in considerable harm to infrastructure and creating disturbances in water supply. Experts advocate that modifying infrastructure represents the only effective long-term remedy. The mere removal of adult mussels fails to address the persistent issue of shell buildup. This invasive species has already led to substantial economic repercussions, which are projected to escalate.

stories.title: Kinshasa Growth Deepens Poverty: World Bank data tracks soaring population
'Keep your curiosity alive': PM Modi addresses IIT Delhi graduates; highlights rapid tech shift
stories.summary: During a momentous Saturday at IIT Delhi's 57th Convocation Ceremony, Prime Minister Narendra Modi inspired the graduates to welcome transformation and continually nurture their thirst for knowledge. He emphasized the importance of mentors and the networks that support their journeys. Modi also spotlighted India's commitment to self-reliance and the birth of innovative sectors, marking the occasion by inaugurating a cutting-edge AI-powered supercomputing facility.

stories.title: 'Is India truly independent?' Congress targets Centre over US Bill on Russia sanctions
stories.summary: Congress leader Pawan Khera has raised concerns about India's autonomy when it comes to purchasing Russian oil. He criticized the government's unwillingness to confront Parliament over this pressing issue. Additionally, Khera expressed solidarity with students in Jharkhand protesting recruitment irregularities, emphasizing that it's a collective duty of all political parties to address student grievances. Meanwhile, Rahul Gandhi's forthcoming initiative aims to spotlight youth challenges and the aspirations of job seekers.

stories.title: China’s hanging coffins had no known builders. Ancient DNA points to Bo people
Spain's blood-red Río Tinto may hold clues to life on Mars, Nasa says
stories.summary: The Río Tinto in Spain captivates with its vivid red and orange colors, a result of both its ancient geology and extensive mining activities. In this caustic environment, specialized microorganisms flourish by harnessing energy from iron and sulfur compounds. Over millennia, mining has intensified these natural chemical reactions, further enhancing the river’s striking look. NASA's interest lies in finding similar minerals to explore potential Martian life.

stories.summary: From ‘natural’ and ‘organic’ to ‘zero maida’ and ‘heart healthy’, the regulator is questioning whether front-of-pack promises are supported by what is inside.

stories.title: Rijiju vs Rahul over women's quota Bill: Support 'unconditionally' remark gets 'already passed' retort
stories.summary: Union minister Kiren Rijiju has called upon Rahul Gandhi to lend his 'unconditional' support to the Women's Reservation Bill. This appeal came after Gandhi's comments highlighting the necessity of women's freedom of expression for India's comprehensive development. While the opposition has shown its backing for the bill, they contest its connection to delimitation. The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023, is set to be implemented following parliamentary approval.

Zach Dell co-founded Base Power in 2023; now valued at $13 billion it has installed more than 23,000 home batteries
stories.summary: Base Power, led by Zach Dell, is revolutionizing residential energy with its advanced battery storage solutions. Having secured a staggering one billion dollars in funding, the company now boasts a valuation of thirteen billion dollars. With thousands of batteries quickly being installed, they are expanding their reach into additional states.

stories.title: Pumas are protecting human lives by preventing vehicle collisions accounting for a 76% reduction in accidents
stories.summary: Pumas in Washington's Olympic Peninsula play a crucial role in decreasing deer-related accidents on highways. By changing deer movement patterns to avoid roads and nighttime activities, they enhance safety for people traveling in the area. This study underscores the significant environmental services provided by large carnivores, demonstrating the importance of coexisting with such majestic species for community well-being.

stories.title: Akal Takht panel asks Punjab govt to address objections before anti-sacrilege talks
stories.summary: On Thursday, an expert panel from Akal Takht convened to deliberate on the proposed anti-sacrilege law. They highlighted that the Punjab government’s response failed to address critical concerns and urged it to submit a compliance report prior to any further discussions. Additionally, the panel observed that the government had yet to create its own discussion group, emphasizing that this sensitive topic demands a broader Panthic agreement for effective resolution.

Pentagon strips ex-Air Force secy of security clearance over Air Force One claim
India digest: Nagpur flat owner booked in minor rape case; CBI charges 11 in Suvendu PA case

stories.summary: Spain has implemented temporary border checks on travelers arriving by air and sea from Italy, intensifying tensions between these two European Union nations regarding migration policies. Italy had previously enacted similar measures following a significant influx of migrants into Spain. This ongoing conflict underscores the contrasting perspectives on border regulations and the management of migrants within the European Union.

stories.title: Nod for Ganga eway extensionn to Haridwar
Om Birla seeks proposal for Makar Dwar porch
stories.summary: In a recent request, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has called for the construction of a new porch to shield MPs and staff from rain at Makar Dwar. CPWD officials will investigate whether this covered entryway can be constructed, especially as the expenses for the new Parliament House project have surged. The proposed porch will offer a protective haven during vehicle wait times.

stories.title: No government role, don’t endorse Hasina’s remarks at private media event: MEA
stories.summary: In a recent statement, India expressed its disapproval of the comments made by former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. The Ministry of External Affairs emphasized that India was uninvolved in the private media event, leading to Bangladesh's fierce reaction. Dhaka labeled the event as an attack on its sovereignty, asserting that it offends the sentiments of its people and threatens already delicate bilateral relations.

stories.title: Ex-HC judge on West Bengal SIR tribunal in Supreme Court seeking protection
stories.summary: A former judge of the Calcutta High Court has approached the Supreme Court for protection, citing numerous death threats issued to her and her family ahead of elections. Reports indicate that they received threatening letters, and CCTV wires were tampered with at their residence. Despite submitting complaints, local police failed to provide adequate safety measures.

stories.title: BJP picks audio clip to target Congress over Karnataka ‘cabinet berths’
stories.summary: The BJP has claimed that funds were involved in securing ministerial roles in Karnataka, referencing a leaked audio exchange among Congress officials. BJP representatives have called for clarification from Congress leaders Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, alleging that cabinet positions were obtained through financial means. One BJP leader also raised concerns about the inclusion of an accused figure in the newly formed cabinet.

stories.title: Prime Minister flags Parliament disruptions with new NDA entrants
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi highlighted the unwavering stability of his administration since 2014, remarking on the contrasting volatility of leadership in Britain. He embraced new members into the NDA coalition, asserting that their partnership is attuned to regional interests and developmental needs. Additionally, Modi underscored the critical necessity for growth in eastern India, showcasing a dedication to inclusive progress.

stories.title: PM Modi's meet with Badal fuels buzz about BJP-SAD pact
stories.summary: Sukhbir Singh Badal, the president of the Shiromani Akali Dal, recently met with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, igniting discussions about a possible revival of their political alliance in Punjab. While the BJP has declared intentions to run independently in the upcoming elections, support for reconnecting with the Akali Dal exists among some state leaders. This split could inadvertently benefit the Aam Aadmi Party amid multifaceted party dynamics.

stories.title: Opposition wants Amit Shah in House; government says 'not your call'
stories.summary: Opposition protests continue, lampooning Home Minister Amit Shah for his absence from Parliament. Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju stated the opposition cannot dictate ministerial attendance. He asserted Shah is actively working and his presence deters extremists and terrorists. Opposition MPs disrupted proceedings, demanding Shah address police action against protesters. The Lok Sabha passed a bill amid the din, with further confrontation anticipated.

stories.title: Tribunal reforms bill gets nod, paves way for national body
stories.summary: The Cabinet has approved the Tribunals Reforms Bill, which establishes a National Tribunal Commission. This independent body will oversee appointments and functioning of approximately sixteen tribunals. The Supreme Court had previously directed the government to constitute this commission. Concerns were raised about tribunals becoming a liability for the judiciary. The bill will be introduced in the Lok Sabha soon.

stories.title: Supeme Court to Mahua: Freedom fighters faced bullets, you fear eggs
stories.summary: The Supreme Court denied Mahua Moitra's appeal for a virtual appearance in front of the police, as she expressed concerns over potential mob violence and egg-throwing incidents. In response, the court referenced the sacrifices of freedom fighters, suggesting that her fears may be unfounded. The session was overseen by Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu, with the MP's legal team advocating for video conferencing.

stories.title: Supreme Court seeks Bihar minister's record of appointment & nomination as MLC
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has requested records from Bihar regarding a minister's appointment. This minister was not an assembly member and faced a six-month deadline. He was later nominated as an MLC, which the government claims resolves the issue. The petitioner cited a 2001 judgment on non-legislator minister re-appointments. The court seeks documents on his initial appointment and subsequent re-induction.

stories.title: Supreme Court dismisses Bofors appeal, 4-decade-old case closed
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has officially dismissed an appeal that sought to challenge a 2005 Delhi High Court ruling, effectively concluding the contentious Bofors pay-off case. Advocate Ajay K Agrawal, who filed the appeal, requested an adjournment, but the court declined to extend the timeline on this matter dating back to 2018, which involved accusations against the Hinduja brothers and AB Bofors.

stories.title: No conflict of interest in RDI Fund, says government
stories.summary: The government has staunchly defended the Research, Development and Innovation Fund's comprehensive framework. Officials have emphasized that the presence of strict conflict-of-interest protocols in public funding decisions is paramount. They asserted that a basic professional relationship does not breach any regulations, and measures such as full disclosure and recusal help maintain equitable assessment of all initiatives. For decades, the Technology Development Board has upheld these essential safeguards.

stories.title: Debate Scope Sparks Clash: Andrew Wilson presses Candace Owens on her claims; X spat intensifies
stories.summary: Candace Owens and Andrew Wilson have clashed publicly over the terms of their planned debate. Owens said the discussion should focus on the Tyler Robinson case and rejected a proposed cross-examination format. Wilson responded that the debate should also examine Owens' own claims about the case and Kirk's assassination. The exchange went viral after critics accused Owens of avoiding scrutiny, fueling widespread online discussion before the debate even begins.

stories.title: Eyeing framework to regulate OTT content: I&B min
stories.summary: The I&B ministry is exploring new legislation targeting OTT platforms. This proposed framework prioritizes the regulation of offensive content while preserving users' rights. Plans include implementing robust age verification mechanisms and parental controls. Additionally, an independent review panel will be tasked with evaluating flagged content following its release and determining appropriate sanctions for any breaches of the established guidelines.

stories.title: Share data on river waters, India tells China
stories.summary: India and China participated in candid discussions regarding border conditions, taking stock of the current landscape along the Line of Actual Control. New Delhi highlighted the necessity of maintaining peace for the advancement of their bilateral relationship. Furthermore, India sought an expedited meeting on the expert committee for trans-border rivers amidst China's unveiling of a significant dam project upstream.

stories.title: Delhi high court stays food regulator's ban on certain Dabur products
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court has temporarily halted an FSSAI directive that questioned Dabur India's product claims. Acknowledging Dabur's established market presence, the court provided initial relief. The order from FSSAI was deemed unjust, as it was issued without company representation. Dabur emphasized that the FSSAI's approach contravened principles of natural justice. The case is set for a further hearing on August 24.

stories.title: ‘Little hope of tracing 2 missing sailors’, Centre informs Supreme Court
stories.summary: Two Indian seafarers remain missing after a drone attack on a merchant ship. Intense search operations have yielded no sign of the missing sailors. The government informed the Supreme Court about the grim situation. The court directed facilitation of maritime insurance payments for the families. This ensures support for the affected families during this difficult time.

stories.title: Air India salary hikes salaries of pilots by up to 15%
stories.summary: Air India has announced a significant pay rise for pilots, ranging from eight to fifteen percent, with commanders seeing the most substantial hikes. In a strategic move to resolve fleet shortages and improve career advancement opportunities, first officers will gain command upgrades at Air India Express first. Moreover, the airline plans to resume its international flight services next month, marking a return to normal operations.

stories.title: NCAER: Bihar booze ban hasn't worked; lift it, fund development work
stories.summary: A recent study advocates for the removal of prohibition in Bihar to foster state growth and enhance capital spending. It posits that banning alcohol hasn't curbed crime rates but instead has spurred illicit activities. By abolishing the prohibition, the state could potentially enjoy a tax revenue boost of 14 to 15 percent.

stories.title: Supreme Court shunts out two coal scam judges on unusual Delhi high court request
stories.summary: Supreme Court has replaced two special judges hearing coal scam cases in Delhi. The Delhi High Court requested their transfer for other judicial responsibilities. Judges Sunena Sharma and Dheeraj Mor were moved after serving for varying durations. Virender Kumar Kharta and Ajay Garg will now preside over these important cases. Both transferred judges have been attached to the principal district and sessions judge office.

stories.title: India’s crude import bill up 26% in ’26-27 Q1 despite 18% volume fall
stories.summary: In the first quarter of the year, India's crude oil import bill surged by twenty-six percent compared to last year, reaching forty-nine billion dollars, up from thirty-nine billion. Despite an eighteen percent drop in import volumes, rising oil prices, fueled by ongoing conflicts, significantly impacted costs. Russia emerged as India's primary crude supplier, contributing over forty percent, and refiners incurred substantial war-risk premiums to ensure a reliable energy supply.

stories.title: Government in Supreme Court: Audio clips linking Biren to Manipur unrest doctored
stories.summary: The Centre informed the Supreme Court about the manipulation of audio recordings, with forensic analyses revealing several modifications. The court has instructed that the most recent forensic report be provided to the Kuki Organisation, which is pursuing an inquiry into audio clips that allegedly implicate Biren Singh. Furthermore, the Supreme Court mandated that copies of the report be distributed to both involved parties.

stories.title: Post Pahalgam, panel proposes security boost at major J&K sites
stories.summary: A parliamentary committee proposed an integrated security framework for Jammu and Kashmir's tourist spots. This includes comprehensive CCTV coverage and centralized monitoring facilities for enhanced safety. Clear inter-agency standard operating procedures are also recommended before peak tourist seasons. These suggestions follow a terror attack and a committee visit to assess security arrangements. The committee noted sustained growth in tourist arrivals due to improved security and infrastructure.

stories.title: Government maps 27 Arunachal border locations with standard names
stories.summary: India has taken a decisive step by officially naming twenty-seven sites in Arunachal Pradesh on its maps, a move designed to clarify territorial boundaries and counter Chinese assertions. These sites represent key historical moments related to border conflicts, featuring important mountains and villages along the McMahon Line, helping to raise awareness of India's rightful claims on these significant lands.

stories.title: YRG Cobblemon Racism Controversy: JayMommy hits back at critics; streamer vows to stay
stories.summary: JayMommy has responded to the criticism surrounding her comments during the YRG Cobblemon event, standing by her position and calling many of her critics “losers.” She also confirmed she will keep playing on the YRG Cobblemon server despite the backlash. Meanwhile, YourRAGE briefly reacted to the situation, saying he hoped everyone involved was okay.

stories.title: WhatsApp clue, Mygate trail help CBI crack NEET paper leak
stories.summary: A WhatsApp conversation triggered the CBI's probe into the NEET-UG examination scam. Subject matter experts colluded by memorizing exam questions and distributing them to students for a fee. Tracking through Mygate app logs and WhatsApp groups led investigators to the involved students and question setters. Additionally, papers were smuggled to Rajasthan, where coaching centers disseminated the leaked materials. The CBI's chargesheet scrutinizes the organized gang's exploitation of NTA's weaknesses.

stories.title: FCRA Bill 'internal matter': India rejects US criticism
stories.summary: The government is set to expedite the Foreign Contributions Regulation Act, which focuses on managing foreign funding for organizations. In contrast to criticism from a US Congressman regarding proposed changes, the administration remains resolute. Home Minister Amit Shah has met with church leaders to resolve their issues. The Bill's discussion and possible approval in Parliament are imminent.

stories.title: Quote by Thomas Aquinas: 'Better to illuminate than merely to shine, to deliver to others...'
stories.summary: Thomas Aquinas championed the notion of disseminating wisdom for the greater good of society. He drew a distinction between individual brilliance and the act of enlightening others. This thirteenth-century principle is still highly relevant in contemporary leadership practices, stressing the importance of making intricate knowledge understandable for all. True expertise is demonstrated through the ability to clarify ideas and enhance collective understanding.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Ernest Hemingway: 'Always do sober what you said you'd do drunk. That will teach you to keep your mouth shut' and a funny lesson on self-discipline

'Don't be like Yasmin': US makes an example out of Venezuelan woman arrested by ICE, says you are illegal if...

stories.summary: In today's fast-paced world, the age-old human inclination to dodge self-reflection has intensified. Individuals often turn to myriad distractions to avoid confronting uncomfortable thoughts and feelings. This constant quest for entertainment can lead to poor decision-making and decreased well-being. Modern psychological approaches emphasize the importance of fostering moments of stillness and reflection, as understanding this behavior is essential in facing both personal and societal hurdles.

stories.title: 'Who introduced them?' US senator says it's odd to see Justin Trudeau frolicking around Katy Perry; 'He used to be in charge of a whole country'

Iltija Mufti faced interrogation regarding an alleged attack on a police officer, asserting that she experienced rough treatment by police during a protest. She emphasised that her struggles represent the desires of all Kashmiris, rather than being a personal crusade.

stories.title: Police put up posters of Lashkar commander across J&K, declare Rs 15L reward
stories.summary: Authorities are on the hunt for Lashkar commander Mohammad Lateef Bhat throughout Kashmir and Jammu, offering a significant cash reward for information that can lead to his capture. Bhat has been linked to the targeted murders of a police officer and two migrants. In a separate incident, an SUV attempted to run over officers at a Ramban checkpoint, resulting in one arrest after the vehicle was seized.

stories.title: California lost as many as 1.3 million Joshua trees in the 2020 Dome Fire
stories.summary: California scientists developed digital tools to map fire damage in the Mojave National Preserve. These new software programs help park managers focus restoration work on vulnerable desert plants. The tools assist in assessing post-fire conditions and developing recovery plans for affected areas. Scenario modeling directs limited conservation resources to high-elevation climate refugia for Joshua trees. This technology aims to improve the chances of survival for these iconic desert plants.

stories.title: 'Fake news, AI-generated': MEA dismisses report of India requesting defence pact with Israel after Mecca agreement
India counters China's 'map war', assigns official names to 27 Arunachal sites

India has maintained that such actions do not change the "undeniable" fact that the state "was, is, and will" remain an integral part of the country. Several of the newly marked locations hold strategic importance because of their proximity to the Line of Actual Control (LAC).

stories.title: A Cumberland mother's new farm stand was stolen before she could use it; strangers....
stories.summary: On its inaugural night, a mother’s bakery stand faced an unfortunate theft. However, a compassionate construction duo—a father and son team—came to the rescue, reconstructing the entire stand at no cost. They meticulously followed the original design, delivering a perfect replica within a week. With security enhancements now in place, the bakery has officially reopened, bringing sweet treats back to the community.

stories.title: Indian-origin hiker found alive after 3 nights stranded on Vancouver Island

Through their foundation, Crankstart, they invite innovative solutions to tackle urgent housing and economic challenges. Organizations can compete for funding, with the evaluation process culminating in a decision set for autumn 2027. This competition highlights the city's increasing dependency on private philanthropy in addressing critical public needs.

stories.title: 'Stop buying petrol, diesel vehicles until govt clarifies stand': Arvind Kejriwal over E20 fuel concerns
stories.summary: Addressing a press conference in Goa, Kejriwal said, "Till such a time, the government makes its intention clear, I appeal to the people to stop buying petrol and diesel vehicles. The government did not conduct any testing for E20 fuel."

stories.title: 'More like humiliation than rejection': Indian PSU employee denied US tourist visa in 20 seconds, says never going to apply again

National Handloom Day: Yogi Adityanath salutes artisans, recalls Swadeshi Movement's legacy
stories.summary: Yogi Adityanath on Thursday paid tribute to the state's weaving community, describing handloom artisans as preservers of India's cultural heritage

stories.title: "Our top priority is pilgrims' safety": Uttarakhand CM Dhami on Char Dham, Kanwar Yatra
stories.summary: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Friday said that the Char Dham Yatra is being stopped intermittently, keeping in mind the safety of pilgrims as the state continues to face heavy rainfall and landslides.

stories.title: Iran officials 'would not be surprised' if Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei dies soon: Report
Who is Sarah Jukaku? Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed has rental properties in India, Dubai in wife's name
Past tense, eye on future: Air India hikes pilots’ pay by 8% to 15%
US judge compares Meta to 'public nuisance,' orders $567m payout over child harm
India’s first satellite-guided chopper approached launched at HAL airport
Exiled Bangladeshi cricket star Shakib Al Hasan willing to return, face murder trial if safety assured
'Why fear eggs in politics?' SC tells Mauha freedom fighter took bullets to chest
stories.summary: A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said it was not inclined to interfere with the high court's direction requiring the Krishnanagar MP to join the investigation. Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for Moitra, argued that she should be allowed to appear before the investigating officer virtually as she was entitled to do so under the law.

stories.title: Harvard rejected Paul Devlin in 1981; he wrote back rejecting the rejection letter
stories.summary: In 1981, high school student Paul Devlin responded to Harvard University's rejection letter by rejecting its rejection instead. Inspired by a grammatical error in Harvard's letter, his witty reply was published byThe New York Times. More than four decades later, the letter has resurfaced online and continues to entertain readers.

stories.title: Astrobase unveils 800kN rocket engine, eyes reusability
Toronto gets its own 'Moo Deng'; pygmy hippo calf born to 20-year-old mother, took first steps within minutes of birth
One man began clearing dumped trash alone; his daily cleanups grew into a 100-volunteer movement
stories.summary: A Houston resident's initiative to clean up neglected areas has blossomed into a vibrant volunteer movement. With one hundred dedicated individuals now on board, their mission is to remove illegally dumped waste. Collaborating with local organizations and harnessing the power of social media, city officials and law enforcement are boosting efforts to tackle this pressing issue, ultimately enhancing the community's aesthetics and the well-being of its residents.

stories.title: 'Govt stealing money, destroying lives': Rahul Gandhi vows campaign against E20
Scientists watched a 1km-wide, 100m-thick section of Greenland’s Sorgenfri glacier break away
stories.summary: In a striking display of nature, a massive section of a Greenland glacier detached and collapsed into the sea, captured by scientists on a research vessel. This occurrence unfolded as part of a study examining the implications of meltwater runoff on major ocean currents. Advanced autonomous robots are being utilized to collect vital data from the hazardous ice face.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: CBI chargesheet alleges NTA's own experts leaked NEET-UG, MEA rejects US criticism of of FCRA Bill & more
stories.summary: CBI chargesheeted thirteen accused, including NTA experts, for allegedly leaking NEET-UG 2026 papers. India rejected US criticism of FCRA amendments, stating Parliament will decide the matter. Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey signed a mutual defence pact, which India is closely following. Prime Minister Modi advised NDA MPs to avoid Lutyens' Delhi and house anxiety. A meeting between Sukhbir Badal and PM Modi sparked reunion talks for BJP-SAD.

stories.title: H-1B program is not just fraud: Trump official says it's a criminal enterprise; Americans will be very angry when the investigation is over
'Do not endorse anything said': MEA rejects Bangladesh's charge over Hasina's presser
stories.summary: Ministry of external affairs stated no government role in Sheikh Hasina's media event. The ministry does not endorse statements made at the private forum. Bangladesh expressed outrage over the interaction, calling it an affront to its sovereignty. Dhaka urged India to clarify its policy regarding conspiratorial activities. Both nations seek constructive relations based on mutual respect and equality.

stories.title: MacKenzie Scott gave Native Forward $50 mn; organisation reveals how it will spend it
stories.summary: Native Forward Scholars Fund has revealed how it will use the entire $50 million unrestricted donation from philanthropist MacKenzie Scott. The organisation will spend $10 million over the next five years to expand scholarships for Native students, while placing the remaining $40 million into a permanent endowment to provide long-term support. The gift, the largest in the organisation's 57-year history, comes as demand for financial aid continues to rise, with scholars facing an average unmet need of $26,000. Native Forward says the funding will help both current students and future generations pursue higher education.

stories.title: New Jersey police officer disguised as a roadside tree catch 74 distracted drivers
